scene.fin.long_receipts.c1.ok: Long is irritated, but two days later he returns with half the receipts. Hanh nods when she hears about it.
scene.fin.long_receipts.c1.fail: Long complains to his uncle that Finance is being difficult. The uncle says nothing to you, but your name gets mentioned.
scene.fin.long_receipts.c2: Book the smallest items as a staff advance to be settled against receipts within thirty days.
scene.fin.long_receipts.c2.ok: It is a workable compromise and Long accepts it, for now. The advance sits on your list, and so does he.
scene.fin.long_receipts.c3: Process it as business expenses, since he says it is for the business.
scene.fin.long_receipts.c3.ok: It goes through and Long is pleasantly surprised. 'You are a practical person.' He remembers.
scene.fin.long_receipts.c3.fail: Thu, doing the payment run, asks why thirty-four entries have no attachments. You find an answer that is shorter than the truth.
scene.fin.long_personal.l1: I have one more. It is a dinner for ten at a nice place. Put it under client entertainment. It was a family dinner, but really, our clients are family, in a way.
scene.fin.long_personal.c1: Refuse to book it as business, and suggest he reimburses it personally.
scene.fin.long_personal.c1.ok: He stares at you for a moment, then laughs, not kindly. 'You have spine. I will remember that.' The receipt goes into the personal pile.
scene.fin.long_personal.c2: Take it to Hanh and let her decide.
scene.fin.long_personal.c2.ok: Hanh says no, and handles Long herself, with a very short call. You are out of the middle, and Long knows who sent it up.
scene.fin.long_personal.c3.ok: Done. Long thanks you warmly. The entry is labelled 'client event'. It is not quite a lie, and it is not quite true.
scene.fin.long_personal.c3.fail: Thu sees a restaurant name she recognises, from a family photo in Long's office. She says nothing, but she looks.
scene.fin.long_event.l1: My cousin's engagement party. Thirty-eight million dong. Book it to marketing. Duc has already said it is fine, more or less.
scene.fin.long_event.c1: Take the invoice to Hanh and Duc together and ask for a written decision.
scene.fin.long_event.c1.ok: Duc's 'more or less' turns out to have been 'not at all'. Nobody wants to put it in writing. It is reclassified as personal.
scene.fin.long_event.c1.fail: Duc says, in front of Hanh, that it is the owner's family and to keep it simple. Hanh's face does not change. Your hands shake a little.
scene.fin.long_event.c2: Refuse and say you will not book it without a business purpose, and leave it there.
scene.fin.long_event.c2.ok: Long goes red, then white. He does not raise his voice. He says he will speak to someone else. Nothing is booked.
scene.fin.long_event.c3.ok: Thirty-eight million leaves the marketing budget without a word of resistance. Long says, 'I will not forget this.' He does not say what he means by it.
scene.fin.long_event.c3.fail: The marketing manager sees the charge and asks what campaign it was. Nobody has an answer, and word gets around fast.
scene.fin.receipt_support.l1: The auditor will want paperwork for the party. Can you get a letter from a supplier, saying it was a marketing event? Someone who owes us. Just a letter.
scene.fin.receipt_support.c1: Refuse, and tell him the only safe route now is to reclassify the expense as personal.
scene.fin.receipt_support.c1.ok: Long is silent, then says, 'You are making this difficult.' You are not, but you feel the cost of saying so.
scene.fin.receipt_support.c2: Ask him for the real documents: a vendor quote, a booking, anything honest.
scene.fin.receipt_support.c2.ok: He finds an actual booking confirmation. It does not make the party a business event, but it is true and you file it.
scene.fin.receipt_support.c2.fail: He comes back empty-handed and annoyed. The question of what to book remains open.
scene.fin.receipt_support.c3: Draft the letter yourself for a supplier to sign.
scene.fin.receipt_support.c3.ok: The supplier signs without reading. Long pats your arm. You file a document that says something that did not happen.
scene.fin.receipt_support.c3.fail: The supplier's accountant reads it and calls Hanh to check. You can hear her voice through the glass.
scene.fin.vy_asks_receipts.l1: I have a list of expenses where the business purpose is thin. Two of them have no receipt, and one is for a restaurant that I think I have seen in a wedding photograph. Can we go through them?
scene.fin.vy_asks_receipts.c1: Show her exactly what you have, say which entries you think were wrong, and name who asked for them.
scene.fin.vy_asks_receipts.c1.ok: It is the hardest conversation of your year. Vy writes it down and asks that the expenses be reclassified. Hanh, told afterwards, says: 'You should have come to me first. But thank you.'
scene.fin.vy_asks_receipts.c2: Explain the circumstances and say you followed instructions, without naming anyone.
scene.fin.vy_asks_receipts.c2.ok: Vy nods slowly: 'Instructions from whom?' She writes down your non-answer.
scene.fin.vy_asks_receipts.c2.fail: Vy's analyst has the approval log. The name comes up anyway, and it is next to your user id.
scene.fin.vy_asks_receipts.c3: Produce the supplier letter and the booking confirmation as support.
scene.fin.vy_asks_receipts.c3.ok: Vy reads the letter. She does not challenge it. She files it, and you leave the room sweating.
scene.fin.vy_asks_receipts.c3.fail: Vy holds the letter up to the light, then puts it next to the supplier's own stationery from last year. The fonts do not match.
scene.fin.profit_smoothing.l1: This month is unusually strong. It would be a pity to show a spike and then a dip. Why not put a healthy provision against future warranty claims? It will smooth the year.
scene.fin.profit_smoothing.c1: Decline: you will provide what the claims history supports, and show him the numbers.
scene.fin.profit_smoothing.c1.ok: Duc grumbles that accountants are not supposed to be this literal. But the provision you book is defensible, and he cannot find fault with the working.
scene.fin.profit_smoothing.c2: Book a modest, evidence-based increase and note it as prudence.
scene.fin.profit_smoothing.c2.ok: It is not what Duc wanted but it is something. Hanh says nothing, which from her is a yes.
scene.fin.profit_smoothing.c3: Book the generous provision he is asking for.
scene.fin.profit_smoothing.c3.ok: The month's profit drops to a comfortable level. The extra sits in a balance sheet account called 'warranty provision'.
scene.fin.profit_smoothing.c3.fail: Hanh asks what claims history justifies the provision. You show her last year's claims. They do not add up to half of it.
scene.fin.reserve_release.l1: The quarter is weak, and the bank wants to see that we have hit our profit target. We have a healthy provision sitting unused. It would be natural to release some of it, would it not?
scene.fin.reserve_release.c1: Refuse to release it without a change in the underlying claims risk, and say why.
scene.fin.reserve_release.c1.ok: Duc is cold but does not argue. The profit target is missed, honestly. Hanh looks at you, then at the window.
scene.fin.reserve_release.c2: Release only the part that the claims data no longer supports, and document why.
scene.fin.reserve_release.c2.ok: It is a fair adjustment, with working papers. Duc accepts it as better than nothing. Hanh reviews it and signs.
scene.fin.reserve_release.c3: Release whatever is needed to hit the target.
scene.fin.reserve_release.c3.ok: The target is hit, to the dong. Duc shakes your hand. The bank's analyst sends a congratulatory email.
scene.fin.reserve_release.c3.fail: The auditor notices the pattern: a provision built in a good month and released in a bad one. She asks for the claims data.
scene.fin.thu_training.l1: I am not sure I understand the approval limits for vendor payments. Nobody ever showed me. I do not want to post something I should not.
scene.fin.thu_training.c1: Sit with her for an hour and walk through the rules, with examples.
scene.fin.thu_training.c1.ok: Thu takes notes in her little book and thanks you twice. The next week she catches an error that would have slipped past you.
scene.fin.thu_training.c2: Give her the policy and offer to check her first ten payments.
scene.fin.thu_training.c2.ok: It works well enough. Thu is careful, and careful takes a while.
scene.fin.thu_training.c3: Tell her to do it like last year's files and ask if she gets stuck.
scene.fin.thu_training.c3.ok: Thu nods, a little too quickly. You can see she will not ask.
scene.fin.thu_mistake.l1: I posted a vendor payment twice. One point two million. I found out this morning. Please, I do not know what to do. If Hanh finds out... I have a small child.
scene.fin.thu_mistake.c1: Reverse it properly, log it, and go through how it happened together so it does not repeat.
scene.fin.thu_mistake.c1.ok: You fix it in an hour. Thu cries a little with relief. 'I will never do it again.' You tell Hanh yourself, calmly, as a process gap. She nods.
scene.fin.thu_mistake.c1.fail: Hanh is unhappy about the mistake, and more unhappy to have heard it from you second. But the record is clean.
scene.fin.thu_mistake.c2: Reverse it and log it, but keep Thu's name out of the note.
scene.fin.thu_mistake.c2.ok: The note says 'duplicate posting, corrected'. It is true. It is also a little short. Thu holds your eye for a moment and looks away.
scene.fin.thu_mistake.c3: Quietly reverse it and do not log it at all.
scene.fin.thu_mistake.c3.ok: It is gone and nobody knows. Thu would walk through fire for you. She keeps a note of it in her book.
scene.fin.thu_mistake.c3.fail: The vendor's statement shows the duplicate payment and the reversal with no journal note. Hanh sees it.
scene.fin.thu_at_audit.l1: I see a duplicate payment reversed in the spring. I would like to hear, from the person who posted it, how it happened and who reviewed the correction.
scene.fin.thu_at_audit.l2: Um. I... it was me. I am not sure what to say.
scene.fin.thu_at_audit.c1: Tell Thu to say exactly what happened, and sit beside her while she does.
scene.fin.thu_at_audit.c1.ok: Thu tells it plainly and Vy listens. The finding is recorded as a process improvement. Afterwards Thu says, quietly, 'Thank you for being there.'
scene.fin.thu_at_audit.c2: Let Thu answer on her own, she made the entry.
scene.fin.thu_at_audit.c2.ok: Thu struggles through it. Vy is patient, but it is obvious nobody prepared her. She avoids your eyes for a week.
scene.fin.thu_at_audit.c3: Tell Thu what to say, and what not to mention.
scene.fin.thu_at_audit.c3.ok: Thu recites the script. Vy makes a note that the answers sound rehearsed, and moves on.
scene.fin.thu_at_audit.c3.fail: Thu's voice cracks in the middle of the script. She looks at you, then at Vy, then says what actually happened. The room goes very quiet.
scene.fin.first_adjustment.l1: This small adjusting entry needs a reason on file before it can post. Duc wants it in today. The reason is not obvious to me either, to be honest.
scene.fin.first_adjustment.c1: Ask Duc for the reason in writing before posting it.
scene.fin.first_adjustment.c1.ok: Duc sends two lines. They are reasonable. Hanh posts it and gives you a nod, the first one.
scene.fin.first_adjustment.c1.fail: Duc replies, 'Just post it.' Hanh looks at the reply for a long time, then decides not to post it today.
scene.fin.first_adjustment.c2: Write the reason you think is most likely and post it.
scene.fin.first_adjustment.c2.ok: It posts. The reason on file is a guess, dressed as a fact. Hanh does not check it.
scene.fin.first_adjustment.c3: Post it with the reason left blank and deal with it later.
scene.fin.first_adjustment.c3.ok: It posts, with an empty box. The empty box will be noticed by someone, one day.
scene.fin.missing_documents.l1: These invoices from sales do not have delivery proof attached. Bao says it is fine, the goods definitely went. Do we pay on them or chase?
scene.fin.missing_documents.c1: Hold the invoices until the delivery proof arrives, and help Thu chase it.
scene.fin.missing_documents.c1.ok: Two days later the proof arrives for all but one. The one is genuinely missing, and finding out why is worth the trouble.
scene.fin.missing_documents.c1.fail: Bao says you are slowing down his customers. The proof arrives eventually, and the invoices were fine.
scene.fin.missing_documents.c2: Process them with a note that proof is outstanding, and set a two-day deadline.
scene.fin.missing_documents.c2.ok: Everyone gets most of what they want. The deadline is met on the third day, which you count as a win.
scene.fin.missing_documents.c3.ok: Bao is happy. The invoices are paid. The delivery proof never turns up, and nobody mentions it again.
scene.fin.missing_documents.c3.fail: One shipment never left the warehouse. The customer was invoiced for goods that did not arrive.
scene.fin.duplicate_payment.l1: A supplier refunded us 3.4 million dong by mistake, a duplicate from two months ago. It went to our bank account on Friday. They have not noticed. What do we do?
scene.fin.duplicate_payment.c1: Tell the supplier and return it, with a note in the ledger.
scene.fin.duplicate_payment.c1.ok: The supplier is stunned and grateful. Thu watches how you handle it and writes something in her notebook. It is something good.
scene.fin.duplicate_payment.c2: Hold it in a separate account and raise it with Hanh before deciding.
scene.fin.duplicate_payment.c2.ok: Hanh says to return it, and thanks you for asking before acting. It costs a day.
scene.fin.duplicate_payment.c3: Keep it quietly. They did not notice.
scene.fin.duplicate_payment.c3.ok: The money lands in other income. Nobody asks. Thu looks at you, and then at her notebook.
scene.fin.duplicate_payment.c3.fail: The supplier's accountant notices two weeks later and sends a polite, exact email copied to Hanh.
scene.fin.fx_difference.l1: The dong moved against the dollar this week. We have a receipt due that would show a nice exchange gain if booked on Monday, and a smaller one if booked today. Policy says the date the money arrives. It arrives Monday.
scene.fin.fx_difference.c1: Book it on the date the money arrives, as the policy says.
scene.fin.fx_difference.c1.ok: Hanh nods. The gain is what it is, and the policy worked as intended.
scene.fin.fx_difference.c2: Ask Duc whether the policy allows a choice, and follow his written answer.
scene.fin.fx_difference.c2.ok: Duc confirms: the arrival date. The gain is booked properly, and he half-jokes that he hoped you would say otherwise.
scene.fin.fx_difference.c3: Book it on whichever date gives the better number.
scene.fin.fx_difference.c3.ok: The gain is 1.1 million better than it would have been. It is a small thing, and it is exactly how a habit starts.
scene.fin.fx_difference.c3.fail: Hanh checks the bank advice against the booking date and finds the mismatch. She says nothing, which is worse than a lecture.
scene.fin.overdue_balance.l1: That buyer is ninety days overdue. They say they will pay, honestly they say it every week. If we reserve against it, it hits my region's profit. Can we just leave it be until year end?
scene.fin.overdue_balance.l2: We have scheduled the payment for next month, but our approval process is slow. I cannot promise a date.
scene.fin.overdue_balance.c1: Provide for the balance in line with the ageing policy, and tell Bao what would reverse it.
scene.fin.overdue_balance.c1.ok: The provision hits Bao's region. He is angry, and then, when the payment arrives a month later, it is released and everyone is calmer.
scene.fin.overdue_balance.c1.fail: Petra's company never pays. The provision was right, and you are not thanked for having been right.
scene.fin.overdue_balance.c2: Provide for half and set a review date with Petra for a firm payment date.
scene.fin.overdue_balance.c2.ok: It is a judgement call, written down with the reasoning. Hanh approves it without enthusiasm. Bao is a little relieved.
scene.fin.overdue_balance.c3: Move the balance into a separate account so it drops out of the overdue report.
scene.fin.overdue_balance.c3.ok: The overdue report looks clean. Bao tells you that you are a lifesaver. You do not feel like one.
scene.fin.overdue_balance.c3.fail: Thu, reconciling the separate account, asks why a ninety-day buyer balance is being carried as 'other receivables'.
scene.fin.covenant_check.l1: The bank covenant is tested at the end of this quarter. We are at 1.18 against a limit of 1.20. I need you to see if anything can be adjusted before we send them the numbers.
scene.fin.covenant_check.c1: Report the real ratio, and draft a short letter to the bank explaining the cause and the plan.
scene.fin.covenant_check.c1.ok: Duc is pale, but the bank responds well to a candid letter and grants a waiver with conditions.
scene.fin.covenant_check.c1.fail: The bank tightens the terms, and Duc says, quietly, that it could have gone differently. It could have, but not honestly.
scene.fin.covenant_check.c2: Show him two honest ways to bring the ratio up next quarter, and report the real number for now.
scene.fin.covenant_check.c2.ok: Duc takes the options and the number, and does not argue. It is not a good day, but it is a clean one.
scene.fin.covenant_check.c3: Adjust a few accruals and classifications until the ratio clears 1.20.
scene.fin.covenant_check.c3.ok: The ratio is 1.21. Duc looks at you with open gratitude. The numbers go to the bank, and you feel a chill that has nothing to do with the office air.
scene.fin.covenant_check.c3.fail: The bank's analyst recomputes the ratio from the detail and gets 1.17. The discrepancy is explained in a two-line email that goes to the owner.
scene.fin.management_letter.l1: The draft management letter names an invoice date that was changed. I want to hear it from you before I hear it from Duc. What happened?
scene.fin.management_letter.c1: Tell her everything: who asked, what you did, and what you should have done.
scene.fin.management_letter.c1.ok: Hanh is silent for a long moment. 'I will take it to Duc. You will get a formal warning, and you will keep your job.' It is the best available outcome.
scene.fin.management_letter.c2: Explain that it was a clerical correction and offer the supporting emails.
scene.fin.management_letter.c2.ok: Hanh reads the emails, reads them again, and lets it stand for now. She does not look convinced.
scene.fin.management_letter.c2.fail: The emails show a change requested after the audit sample was announced. Hanh closes the laptop.
scene.fin.management_letter.c3: Say Bao asked you to do it, and you only followed instructions.
scene.fin.management_letter.c3.ok: Hanh hears it, and it is what she expected. Bao gets a formal warning instead of you. You have made an enemy.
scene.fin.management_letter.c3.fail: Bao produces the original request, which said 'if the dates are wrong, correct them properly'. You corrected them improperly.
scene.fin.scapegoat_meeting.l1: The auditor's draft comments on the reserve movements are serious. The owner wants to know who built and released it. I need an answer for the meeting tomorrow. You were the one at the keyboard.
scene.fin.scapegoat_meeting.c1: Bring the emails and the record of who asked for what, and say it plainly.
scene.fin.scapegoat_meeting.c1.ok: The room is tense. You are not thanked, but the facts are on the table, and Hanh speaks in support of the record. You keep your job.
scene.fin.scapegoat_meeting.c1.fail: Duc produces his own version. It has no emails, but it has authority. The owner's face closes.
scene.fin.scapegoat_meeting.c2: Say you will accept responsibility for the entries, but that the decision came from above.
scene.fin.scapegoat_meeting.c2.ok: It is accurate and diplomatic. Duc hears it, and does not thank you. Hanh gives you a short, private nod afterwards.
scene.fin.scapegoat_meeting.c3: Say Thu did the postings and you did not check them.
scene.fin.scapegoat_meeting.c3.ok: It works for a day. Thu is suspended pending review. She looks at you on her way out, and you do not look back.
scene.fin.scapegoat_meeting.c3.fail: Thu produces her notebook. It has dates, amounts and the initials of who told her to post each one. The initials are not hers.
role.fin.accountant.blurb: You keep the books of a cookware exporter true. Your pressures: a month-end close every four weeks, sales who want revenue booked early, bosses who want smoother numbers, and what you are willing to sign.
scene.qc.midyear_review.l1: Half a year in. Let me be straight with you: your records are good where it counts, but I have heard complaints from production that you slow the line. How do you see it?
scene.qc.midyear_review.c1: Accept it: say where you have been slow and what you will change.
scene.qc.midyear_review.c1.ok: Khoa nods. 'That is what I wanted to hear. Keep the records, lose the wait.' You leave with a plan and a little more of his trust.
scene.qc.midyear_review.c2: Defend your work with numbers: the retests that caught real problems.
scene.qc.midyear_review.c2.ok: The numbers speak for themselves. Khoa will repeat them to production.
scene.qc.midyear_review.c2.fail: Khoa finds two retests that delayed shipments for nothing. 'Numbers cut both ways.'
scene.qc.midyear_review.c3: Say production exaggerates and the delays were never your fault.
scene.qc.midyear_review.c3.ok: Khoa lets it go, but he writes something down.
scene.qc.midyear_review.c3.fail: Khoa has already talked to Lan. The gap between your story and hers is obvious.
scene.qc.year_end_review.l1: Annual review time. Before I tell you what I think, tell me how you would rate your own year, and why.
scene.qc.year_end_review.c1: Give an honest account, including the calls you got wrong.
scene.qc.year_end_review.c1.ok: It is an uncomfortable half hour and a respected one. Khoa writes: 'Knows the limits of the job.'
scene.qc.year_end_review.c2: Stay modest: list what went well and mention one thing to improve.
scene.qc.year_end_review.c2.ok: A safe, forgettable review. Khoa nods and moves to the next item.
scene.qc.year_end_review.c3: Present the year as a success and leave out the shortcuts.
scene.qc.year_end_review.c3.ok: It lands well. You leave with a good rating and a small weight in your chest.
scene.qc.year_end_review.c3.fail: Khoa has the audit file open on his desk. He turns the page towards you without a word.
scene.qc.manager_offer.l1: I am leaving the company at the end of the year. The directors have asked me who should run QC, and I gave them your name. One condition: you will be asked, often, to sign things that are nearly right. I need to know you will say no.
scene.qc.manager_offer.c1: Accept, and say plainly what you will and will not sign, so the directors hear it from you first.
scene.qc.manager_offer.c1.ok: Khoa nods: 'Then it is yours. Write it down.' You take over the lab with your terms on paper.
scene.qc.manager_offer.c2: Thank him, but decline: you would rather keep inspecting than manage the pressure.
scene.qc.manager_offer.c2.ok: Khoa looks disappointed, then understanding. 'Stay sharp. The next manager may not be as careful as you.'
scene.qc.manager_offer.c3: Accept without asking what the condition means when the directors push.
scene.qc.manager_offer.c3.ok: Khoa nods slowly and shakes your hand. You realise you agreed to something you did not ask about.
scene.qc.first_signature.l1: The first lot of the week is tested except for one hardness reading. The truck leaves at four. Could you sign the CoA now and add the reading when it comes in? You are new, I do not want to put you on the spot. It is just the paperwork.
scene.qc.first_signature.c1: Wait for the reading and sign only when the CoA is complete.
scene.qc.first_signature.c1.ok: The reading arrives at 3.40 and is fine. The truck leaves twenty minutes late. Lan sighs but says 'Fair enough'. Khoa, passing, nods without a word.
scene.qc.first_signature.c1.fail: The reading is borderline and needs a retest. The truck leaves without that lot, and the week starts badly with production.
scene.qc.first_signature.c2: Sign the CoA for the tested parameters only, and note the pending reading.
scene.qc.first_signature.c2.ok: Lan agrees, and the buyer gets a CoA with an honest note. Khoa reads it later and says: 'That is how it is done.'
scene.qc.first_signature.c3: Sign it in full and add the reading later.
scene.qc.first_signature.c3.ok: The truck leaves on time. The reading arrives later and is fine, and you feel you got away with something.
scene.qc.first_signature.c3.fail: The reading comes back 1.5 points below spec. The lot is already on the road with your signature on a full CoA.
scene.qc.training_gap.l1: I have never been trained on the new viscometer. I have been running it from the manual, and my readings look odd. Please do not tell Khoa, I am afraid he will think I cannot do my job.
scene.qc.training_gap.c1: Arrange proper training for him, tell Khoa it is a gap in the process, and sit with him for the first runs.
scene.qc.training_gap.c1.ok: Khoa schedules a session with the vendor. Minh's readings settle within a week. He tells you, awkwardly, that nobody has done that for him before.
scene.qc.training_gap.c2: Pair him with a colleague for a few runs and check his results yourself.
scene.qc.training_gap.c2.ok: It helps, mostly. The readings improve, though the gap in the process stays quietly in place.
scene.qc.training_gap.c3: Tell him to keep going and flag anything odd.
scene.qc.training_gap.c3.ok: Minh nods. He will not flag anything, not because it is fine, but because he is afraid to.
scene.qc.training_gap.c3.fail: Two weeks later a batch of readings is wrong. Minh says nothing, and Khoa finds out from the complaint log.
scene.qc.lab_housekeeping.l1: I found three bottles of reagent in the fridge past their expiry date. One of them is the standard for the hardness test. Throwing it away means a new order and a wait of two weeks.
scene.qc.lab_housekeeping.c1: Discard the expired reagents, log the disposal, and rush-order the standard.
scene.qc.lab_housekeeping.c1.ok: The hardness test is paused for four days while the standard arrives. Production grumbles. The log is clean.
scene.qc.lab_housekeeping.c1.fail: The rush order is delayed. Hardness testing is paused for ten days and the backlog is painful.
scene.qc.lab_housekeeping.c2: Label the standard 'for non-critical use only' and keep testing with the others.
scene.qc.lab_housekeeping.c2.ok: It is a workable compromise, but a little vague. Khoa reads the label and raises an eyebrow, then lets it stand for a week.
scene.qc.lab_housekeeping.c3: Keep using the expired standard until the new one arrives. The difference will be tiny.
scene.qc.lab_housekeeping.c3.ok: Testing goes on without a pause. Minh looks uncomfortable and says nothing.
scene.qc.lab_housekeeping.c3.fail: A buyer's lab retests the same lot and gets readings two points apart. They ask which standard you used.
scene.qc.pre_tet_pile.l1: It is the last run before Tet and we have twice the normal volume. The lab has four people and forty lots. The buyers want everything shipped before the holiday. Whatever you can do, please do it.
scene.qc.pre_tet_pile.c1: Ask Khoa for two temporary staff from production, and test every lot fully.
scene.qc.pre_tet_pile.c1.ok: Khoa gets you one person for three days. It is not enough, but the lots that go out are fully tested and the ones that do not wait until January.
scene.qc.pre_tet_pile.c1.fail: No help arrives. You work late every night, and four lots still miss the holiday shipment.
scene.qc.pre_tet_pile.c2: Prioritise by risk: full tests on critical lots, reduced checks on low-risk ones, all written down.
scene.qc.pre_tet_pile.c2.ok: A sensible triage. Khoa signs the plan, Lan gets most of her shipments, and the records show exactly what was checked.
scene.qc.pre_tet_pile.c3: Skim every lot quickly and sign them all so nothing misses the holiday.
scene.qc.pre_tet_pile.c3.ok: Forty lots go out before Tet. Lan sends a fruit basket. You sleep for two days.
scene.qc.pre_tet_pile.c3.fail: In February, a buyer returns two of the lots. The complaint log says 'inspected 11 January, 02:10 a.m.'
scene.qc.tet_bonus_pressure.l1: You know the Tet bonus is tied to shipped volume, for everyone, including the lab. Every held lot costs the whole plant. I am not asking you to sign anything bad. I am asking you to think about what the lab will look like if we miss the target.
scene.qc.tet_bonus_pressure.c1: Say the release rules do not change with the bonus, and offer to help find honest ways to speed up testing.
scene.qc.tet_bonus_pressure.c1.ok: Lan listens. You agree to schedule the testing earlier in the week. It is not what she wanted, but it helps.
scene.qc.tet_bonus_pressure.c1.fail: Lan is cold for a week. A few colleagues give you looks in the canteen. Your principles are right and lonely.
scene.qc.tet_bonus_pressure.c2: Agree to fast-track the lots that are clearly fine, and hold the rest.
scene.qc.tet_bonus_pressure.c2.ok: Lan accepts the split. The bonus is at risk, but nobody can say you blocked it for no reason.
scene.qc.tet_bonus_pressure.c3: Tell her you will do what you can, and release borderline lots on the benefit of the doubt.
scene.qc.tet_bonus_pressure.c3.ok: The plant hits the volume. The bonus is paid, and Lan brings you a thank-you card signed by the whole shift.
scene.qc.tet_bonus_pressure.c3.fail: One borderline lot turns out to be a failure in the field. The complaint quotes the release date, two days before the bonus cut-off.
scene.qc.kpi_first_pass_yield.l1: First-pass yield is our headline KPI this year, and it is down two points. The directors ask about it every week. You can improve it by catching more problems earlier, or by judging more lots as passing the first time. One of those is real.
scene.qc.kpi_first_pass_yield.c1: Show Khoa the KPI's weakness: it rewards passing lots, not finding problems, and propose a second measure.
scene.qc.kpi_first_pass_yield.c1.ok: Khoa takes your note to the directors. A second measure, escapes found after release, is added. It takes months, but it is real.
scene.qc.kpi_first_pass_yield.c1.fail: The directors say the KPI stays as it is. Khoa sighs: 'I tried. You helped me try.' The number keeps falling.
scene.qc.kpi_first_pass_yield.c2: Report the real number, explain why it fell, and show what you are doing about the causes.
scene.qc.kpi_first_pass_yield.c2.ok: It is an honest report with a plan. Khoa nods: 'That I can defend.' Yield stays down, but the trend has an explanation.
scene.qc.kpi_first_pass_yield.c3: Re-classify borderline results as passing on the first test, so the number recovers.
scene.qc.kpi_first_pass_yield.c3.ok: Yield is back up two points. Khoa is relieved and does not ask how. The directors move on to another topic.
scene.qc.kpi_first_pass_yield.c3.fail: Minh notices that retests were relabelled as first tests. He looks at you, then quietly at the records.
scene.qc.audit_notice_huddle.l1: The buyer's audit is in three weeks. Tam suggests we give the lab a fresh coat of paint and tidy the floor. I would rather spend the time on the records. What do you think we should focus on?
scene.qc.audit_notice_huddle.l2: First impressions matter. A clean lab says we are careful. I am just saying.
scene.qc.audit_notice_huddle.c1: List the real gaps: overdue calibrations, unsigned records, training. Fix those first, and clean the floor afterwards.
scene.qc.audit_notice_huddle.c1.ok: The list is longer than anyone wanted. Khoa turns it into an action plan with owners and dates. The audit will find less than it could have.
scene.qc.audit_notice_huddle.c1.fail: The list is too long to finish in three weeks. You prioritise, document the rest as known gaps with dates, and sleep badly.
scene.qc.audit_notice_huddle.c2: Prioritise the gaps most likely to be found, and do a light tidy of the lab as well.
scene.qc.audit_notice_huddle.c2.ok: A balanced plan. Tam gets his tidy lab and Khoa gets some of his records. Not perfect, but workable.
scene.qc.audit_notice_huddle.c3: Go with Tam: paint and tidy, and trust that the auditor will not look deep.
scene.qc.audit_notice_huddle.c3.ok: The lab looks wonderful. The records are where they were. You hope.
scene.qc.audit_notice_huddle.c3.fail: Khoa finds out that the records work was never started. He does not shout, which is the worst sign.
scene.qc.vy_spring_visit.l1: I am the buyer's external auditor. I would like to see your calibration records, the last six months of incoming inspections, and two lots from start to finish: raw material to shipment. Take your time, but I do read the dates.
scene.qc.vy_spring_visit.l2: Show her what she asks for. If she asks something you do not know, say so.
scene.qc.vy_spring_visit.c1: Show her everything organised, including the records that needed corrections and the reasons.
scene.qc.vy_spring_visit.c1.ok: Vy traces two lots end to end without stopping. At the end she says: 'Traceable. That is rarer than people think.' Khoa exhales.
scene.qc.vy_spring_visit.c2: Answer what she asks and produce the files she requests.
scene.qc.vy_spring_visit.c2.ok: A routine visit. Vy writes three observations. None is serious and two were already on Khoa's list.
scene.qc.vy_spring_visit.c3: Offer her the two best lots to trace, and steer her away from the calibration log.
scene.qc.vy_spring_visit.c3.ok: Vy traces your two lots and finds nothing. She does not ask for the calibration log. You feel the small, dangerous relief of a shortcut that worked.
scene.qc.vy_spring_visit.c3.fail: Vy picks a third lot of her own and asks for the calibration log without looking up. The date on the last entry is ten weeks old.
fact.signed_before_result: you signed a certificate before the last result was in
lesson.signed_before_result: A signature on a certificate says every result is in and within spec. Signing first and hoping is how a small courtesy becomes a false statement.
fact.used_expired_standard: you kept using an expired reference standard
lesson.used_expired_standard: A reference standard defines what a test result means. Once it has expired, every result measured with it carries a doubt nobody can remove.
fact.skimmed_lots_before_tet: you signed lots you had only skimmed, to catch the holiday shipment
lesson.skimmed_lots_before_tet: A deadline is when inspection matters most. Signing lots you did not really check turns your signature into a formality, and formalities are not defences.
fact.released_borderline_for_bonus: you released borderline lots so the plant would reach its bonus target
lesson.released_borderline_for_bonus: When a bonus depends on your signature, the rules have to hold hardest. Benefit of the doubt belongs to the customer, not to the target.
fact.gamed_yield_kpi: you relabelled retests as first-pass results to improve a KPI
lesson.gamed_yield_kpi: Gaming a KPI makes the number look better while the problem stays. The next person to rely on that number will make a worse decision because of you.
arc.cheaper_steel.title: Cheaper steel
scene.qc.steel_trial_results.l1: The trial lot results are in. Hardness is on the edge of spec, two readings out of twenty are just below. The supplier says it is normal for a first lot. The price saving is real. What is the verdict?
scene.qc.steel_trial_results.c1: Reject the supplier for now and explain what they must fix before the next trial.
scene.qc.steel_trial_results.c1.ok: Tam is annoyed but accepts the data. The supplier sends an apologetic email and a corrective plan. The savings will have to wait.
scene.qc.steel_trial_results.c1.fail: Tam escalates to the directors, who ask whether QC is being unreasonable. You show the data and they let it drop, with some irritation.
scene.qc.steel_trial_results.c2: Extend the trial with a second lot and tighter incoming checks, and keep the decision open.
scene.qc.steel_trial_results.c2.ok: It is a fair middle path. Tam grumbles at the delay but agrees. The second lot will decide.
scene.qc.steel_trial_results.c3: Pass the lot: the two low readings are within normal scatter.
scene.qc.steel_trial_results.c3.ok: Tam is delighted and thanks you with a lunch invitation. The steel goes onto the line. You chose to read two readings generously.
scene.qc.steel_field_failure.l1: We have had three pots crack at the rivet in the field, all from the new steel. The buyer is asking for the incoming inspection records for that material. What do we show them?
scene.qc.steel_field_failure.l2: It is the supplier's problem. Their certificate said it met spec.
scene.qc.steel_field_failure.c1: Own what you signed: show the records, including the borderline readings, and lead the investigation.
scene.qc.steel_field_failure.c1.ok: It is a rough week. The records show a borderline pass, and you say so first. The buyer's engineer writes: 'Transparent.' Khoa backs you, carefully.
scene.qc.steel_field_failure.c2: Share the blame: the supplier's certificate, the borderline data and the approval were a joint decision.
scene.qc.steel_field_failure.c2.ok: It is roughly true, and it spreads the damage. Tam resents being included, and Khoa says: 'Next time, decide alone if you are going to sign alone.'
scene.qc.steel_field_failure.c3: Say the supplier's certificate was the only evidence you had, and show the incoming records without the borderline notes.
scene.qc.steel_field_failure.c3.ok: The buyer accepts the records and focuses on the supplier. You feel the relief, and the unease.
scene.qc.steel_field_failure.c3.fail: The buyer's lab asks for the raw data. Minh, asked directly, has to hand over the file with the notes in it.
arc.field_complaint.title: The field complaint
scene.qc.field_complaint_arrives.l1: A buyer in Germany has reported rust spots on the inside of a batch of pots, after six weeks in a warehouse. It could be storage. It could be us. They want a response within five days.
scene.qc.field_complaint_arrives.c1: Open a formal investigation: retain samples, check the passivation records, and tell the buyer what you are doing.
scene.qc.field_complaint_arrives.c1.ok: You find the passivation step was shortened on two shifts. It is an honest finding. The buyer appreciates the speed, and production is not pleased.
scene.qc.field_complaint_arrives.c1.fail: The retained samples have been discarded by mistake. You investigate from records alone, and the buyer hears about it.
scene.qc.field_complaint_arrives.c2: Check a limited sample, answer the buyer with what you find, and leave the wider question open.
scene.qc.field_complaint_arrives.c2.ok: A quick, partial answer. The buyer accepts it for now. Khoa says: 'We will come back to this, will we not?'
scene.qc.field_complaint_arrives.c3: Reply that it is a one-off caused by storage, and close the case.
scene.qc.field_complaint_arrives.c3.ok: The buyer accepts. Lan is relieved. The passivation records stay unopened.
scene.qc.field_complaint_arrives.c3.fail: The buyer sends a second report, this time with photographs and batch numbers, and copies its director.
scene.qc.root_cause_dispute.l1: You say passivation was shortened. My shift leads say the steel was already contaminated when it arrived. Tam says the lab's own cleaning agent could be the cause. Everyone has a story. What do we do?
scene.qc.root_cause_dispute.c1: Follow the data: test samples from each stage and let the results decide, even if they point at QC.
scene.qc.root_cause_dispute.c1.ok: Results take five days. Contamination is in the steel and the shortened step made it worse. Everyone gets a share, and nobody is scapegoated.
scene.qc.root_cause_dispute.c1.fail: The results are inconclusive. You document the uncertainty honestly and recommend three controls. The meeting ends without a winner.
scene.qc.root_cause_dispute.c2: Propose an independent review by the buyer's lab and abide by it.
scene.qc.root_cause_dispute.c2.ok: It is bold and it works: the buyer trusts an answer they helped reach. Lan is nervous but agrees.
scene.qc.root_cause_dispute.c3: Pick the explanation that protects the lab, and argue it.
scene.qc.root_cause_dispute.c3.ok: Your version carries the room. Lan's shift leads are blamed, and the procedure is left alone.
scene.qc.root_cause_dispute.c3.fail: A shift lead brings the maintenance log showing the passivation bath was out of range for a week. Your version comes apart in front of everyone.
scene.qc.recall_press.l1: The buyer wants a written statement about the rust spots, for their own customers. They want to know how many lots are affected and whether we knew. The directors are nervous. How do we word it?
scene.qc.recall_press.c1: State the affected lots, what you found, and what you are doing, including what you did not know at the time.
scene.qc.recall_press.c1.ok: The statement is factual and uncomfortable. The buyer replies: 'This is the statement we needed. Thank you.' The directors complain about the word 'did not know'.
scene.qc.recall_press.c2: Write a careful statement that is accurate, but does not volunteer the number of lots.
scene.qc.recall_press.c2.ok: The buyer accepts it and asks a follow-up. You answer it honestly. The statement is correct, if a little reluctant.
scene.qc.recall_press.c2.fail: The buyer counts the lots from the shipping data and finds more than you mentioned. The word 'reluctant' appears in their reply.
scene.qc.recall_press.c3: Describe it as a minor cosmetic issue affecting a small number of units.
scene.qc.recall_press.c3.ok: The directors love it. The buyer accepts it without comment. The real number is in a drawer.
scene.qc.recall_press.c3.fail: A buyer's customer posts photographs of corroded pots online, with the word 'cosmetic' quoted from your statement.
arc.minh.title: Minh
scene.qc.minh_mistake.l1: I misread a hardness value on a lot that has already shipped. It was 61 and I wrote 67. It would have failed. Please... I cannot lose this job. Can we just fix the record?
scene.qc.minh_mistake.c1: Report it to Khoa now with context, recall the lot for retest, and stand beside Minh while it is handled.
scene.qc.minh_mistake.c1.ok: Khoa is grave but fair: 'Good that it came to me.' The lot is retested and the record corrected in the open. Minh gets a written warning, not a dismissal.
scene.qc.minh_mistake.c1.fail: The lot has already been installed at the buyer. The recall is expensive and embarrassing. You did the right thing and it still hurts.
scene.qc.minh_mistake.c2: Correct the record properly with a dated note, retest what you can, and coach Minh without escalating.
scene.qc.minh_mistake.c2.ok: The lot is retested and passes. The correction is documented, and the record shows a colleague noticing an error. Minh does not forget.
scene.qc.minh_mistake.c3: Change the record to 67 and say nothing.
scene.qc.minh_mistake.c3.ok: Minh nearly faints with relief. The lot is out there with a value that was never true. You have a colleague who will walk through fire for you.
scene.qc.minh_mistake.c3.fail: The buyer's retest of the lot comes back at 62. The two values, 67 and 62, are five points apart, and the record has two versions of the truth.
scene.qc.minh_at_audit.l1: I see a correction to a hardness record in the summer. I would like to hear from the person who made the original entry how it happened, and who reviewed the correction.
scene.qc.minh_at_audit.l2: That was me. I... I am not sure what to say.
scene.qc.minh_at_audit.c1: Tell Minh to say exactly what happened, and sit beside him while he does.
scene.qc.minh_at_audit.c1.ok: Minh tells it plainly and Vy listens. The finding is recorded as a process improvement. Afterwards he says quietly: 'Thank you for not leaving me alone.'
scene.qc.minh_at_audit.c2: Let Minh answer alone. He made the entry.
scene.qc.minh_at_audit.c2.ok: Minh struggles through it. Vy is patient, but it is clear nobody prepared him. He avoids you for a month.
scene.qc.minh_at_audit.c3: Tell Minh what to say, and what not to mention.
scene.qc.minh_at_audit.c3.ok: Minh recites the script. Vy notes that the answers sound rehearsed, and moves on.
scene.qc.minh_at_audit.c3.fail: Minh's voice cracks mid-script. He looks at you, then at Vy, then tells her what actually happened. The room is very quiet.
scene.qc.ms_vy_returns.l1: I was here in spring. This time I am comparing spring to now: records, calibrations, the lots I traced, and any corrections made since. Patterns interest me more than single errors.
scene.qc.ms_vy_returns.c1: Open everything, and point out the corrections, the borderline calls and what you learned from them.
scene.qc.ms_vy_returns.c1.ok: Vy takes notes for two days. Her draft says: 'The laboratory demonstrates a culture of disclosure.' Khoa reads it twice and sits down.
scene.qc.ms_vy_returns.c2: Answer fully and give her the files she asks for.
scene.qc.ms_vy_returns.c2.ok: Uneventful. Her questions are sharper than in spring, and your answers hold.
scene.qc.ms_vy_returns.c3: Give her the files but keep answers short, and do not mention the judgement calls.
scene.qc.ms_vy_returns.c3.ok: Vy makes no comment. The visit ends on time, and you are tired from not volunteering anything.
scene.qc.ms_vy_returns.c3.fail: Vy finds a pattern across three lots. She asks you to explain each one in writing, copied to Khoa.
scene.qc.scapegoat_meeting.l1: The auditor's draft mentions payments from a supplier to someone in this lab. The directors want a name by tomorrow. I am not going to name someone on a rumour, but I need you to tell me if there is anything I should know.
scene.qc.scapegoat_meeting.c1: Tell him everything, now, before anyone else does.
scene.qc.scapegoat_meeting.c1.ok: Khoa is silent for a long time. 'I wish you had come earlier. But you came.' You are suspended pending review, and you keep the chance to explain.
scene.qc.scapegoat_meeting.c2: Say you know nothing about any payments.
scene.qc.scapegoat_meeting.c2.ok: Khoa nods and lets it go. The name the directors get is someone else's. You sleep badly for a month.
scene.qc.scapegoat_meeting.c2.fail: The auditor's analyst has already matched the supplier's payment dates to your bank deposits. Khoa is given the file the next morning.
scene.qc.scapegoat_meeting.c3: Suggest that the new lab technician may have been in contact with the supplier.
scene.qc.scapegoat_meeting.c3.ok: Khoa writes it down. Minh is questioned for a day. He says nothing wrong, and everyone knows it.
scene.qc.scapegoat_meeting.c3.fail: Minh produces his own record of every supplier interaction, including the day you were with Mr Hung. It is dated.
fact.passed_borderline_steel: you passed a borderline steel lot to keep a supplier trial moving
lesson.passed_borderline_steel: A borderline result is a question, not an answer. Reading it generously to help a cost saving turns the benefit of the doubt against the customer.
fact.owned_steel_decision: you owned a decision that went wrong and showed the records first
lesson.owned_steel_decision: Owning a decision before being asked is not a confession of weakness. It is what makes the rest of your records believable.
fact.hid_borderline_data: you withheld notes showing a borderline result from the buyer
lesson.hid_borderline_data: Evidence you keep back from a customer during a failure investigation is concealment. The notes are the evidence of what you knew.
fact.dismissed_field_complaint: you closed a customer complaint as a one-off without investigating it
lesson.dismissed_field_complaint: A complaint is data about your process. Closing it without looking means the next one arrives with no warning, and with someone else's photographs.
fact.picked_side_on_root_cause: you chose the root-cause story that protected your department
lesson.picked_side_on_root_cause: A root-cause investigation that starts with protecting someone will not find the cause. The cause stays in the process and returns.
fact.minimised_defect_to_buyer: you described a real defect to a customer as a minor cosmetic issue
lesson.minimised_defect_to_buyer: Understating a defect to a customer protects the company for a week and exposes it for years. The customer's customers are the ones who find out.
fact.covered_minh_error: you changed a record to hide a colleague's misreading
lesson.covered_minh_error: Hiding a colleague's honest error protects one person and falsifies a record. A corrected, documented error protects both.
fact.blamed_minh: you pointed the blame at the youngest member of the lab
lesson.blamed_minh: Naming the most junior person is the easiest move in the room and the most damaging one. He keeps his own records, and he remembers who was kind to him.
char.anders.name: Mr Anders
char.anders.title: Buyer, European retail chain
char.quynh.name: Quynh
char.quynh.title: Junior sales coordinator
arc.discount_spiral.title: The discount spiral
arc.overdue_account.title: The overdue account
arc.quynh.title: Quynh
fact.buried_discount_in_freight: you hid unapproved discounts inside the freight charges
lesson.buried_discount_in_freight: A discount that does not appear on the price line is still a discount. Moving it elsewhere only stops the people who approve prices from seeing it.
fact.pulled_shipment_in: you shipped an order early, without the buyer knowing, to reach a number
lesson.pulled_shipment_in: Moving shipments between periods to fix a number is revenue management, not sales. The buyer's warehouse, not your spreadsheet, is where it is tested.
fact.approved_quynh_shortcut: you told a junior colleague that bending a rule is fine because everyone does it
lesson.approved_quynh_shortcut: Juniors learn rules from what seniors do, not what they say. A shortcut passed down is a habit you have given to someone else.
fact.blamed_quynh: you blamed a junior colleague for a habit she learned from you
lesson.blamed_quynh: A junior who copies you is repeating your example. Blaming her for it moves the cost of your habit onto the person with the least power to bear it.
fact.staged_factory_visit: you staged a factory visit to hide how the line really works
lesson.staged_factory_visit: A buyer who visits wants to see a normal day. A staged visit works until someone on the floor tells the truth, and then it costs you every visit after.
fact.padded_quota_orders: you counted unconfirmed orders toward quota
lesson.padded_quota_orders: A quota number is a forecast the company plans around. Counting orders that are not real makes the plan, and the next quarter, worse.
fact.padded_expense_claim: you claimed an expense for a meal that did not happen
lesson.padded_expense_claim: An expense claim is a statement that a cost happened. A small padded claim is still a false statement, and it teaches the company's own people that statements are flexible.
fact.exploited_buyer_trust: you used a buyer's trust to set a price he would not have accepted if he had checked
lesson.exploited_buyer_trust: Trust is worth more than one margin. A price set because the buyer stopped checking is a bet that he never will.
scene.sales.backdate_invoice.c1: Refuse, and explain the revenue recognition problem.
scene.sales.backdate_invoice.c1.ok: Your boss is irritated but accepts it. The numbers stay clean.
scene.sales.backdate_invoice.c1.fail: Your boss takes it personally and brings up your review.
scene.sales.backdate_invoice.c3: Do it quietly and date the documents the thirtieth.
scene.sales.backdate_invoice.c3.ok: The quarter closes on target. You have signed something you would rather not explain.
scene.sales.backdate_invoice.c3.fail: The auditors match the vessel date with the invoice date. The gap is impossible to explain.
scene.sales.backdate_invoice.c2: Propose shipping a partial order before the thirtieth instead.
scene.sales.backdate_invoice.c2.ok: The buyer accepts a partial shipment. It closes most of the gap, honestly.
scene.sales.backdate_invoice.c2.fail: The buyer refuses the split. You still miss the target, and your boss knows you tried.
scene.sales.first_big_order.l1: Good timing. Mr Anders is sending his first big order this month. Twenty thousand pots. It is the order that decides whether we become his main supplier. I will be honest: the delivery date he wants is tight.
scene.sales.first_big_order.l2: I have had three suppliers fail on dates this year. I do not need the cheapest. I need someone who tells me the truth when it is going to be late.
scene.sales.first_big_order.c1: Check the real capacity with Lan before you promise a date, and give Anders a date you can defend.
scene.sales.first_big_order.c1.ok: The date is nine days later than Anders wanted. He pauses, then: 'That I can plan around.' Bao is nervous, Lan is grateful. You have a real date.
scene.sales.first_big_order.c1.fail: Anders says nine days is too late and gives the first tranche to a rival. You keep the second. It is an honest loss.
scene.sales.first_big_order.c2: Promise a date in between and ask Lan to try her best to meet it.
scene.sales.first_big_order.c2.ok: Anders accepts. Lan says, 'I will try', and you both know what that means. It may hold, or it may not.
scene.sales.first_big_order.c3: Promise him exactly the date he asked for and sort out production afterwards.
scene.sales.first_big_order.c3.ok: Anders is delighted. Bao claps your shoulder. Lan hears about the date from Bao, in the corridor.
scene.sales.first_big_order.c3.fail: Lan says, in front of Bao, that the date is impossible and that nobody asked her. The room goes cold.
scene.sales.discount_expected.l1: For the next order I assume the same price as last time. Six percent off list. I have already told my own board. Is there a problem?
scene.sales.discount_expected.c1: Explain plainly that the six percent was a one-time deal tied to volume, and offer a tiered price for this order.
scene.sales.discount_expected.c1.ok: Anders is not pleased but he respects the clarity. 'Fine. I will tell my board it was a promotion.' The price holds at four percent.
scene.sales.discount_expected.c1.fail: Anders says he will look at other suppliers. You hold the line. The order shrinks by a third.
scene.sales.discount_expected.c2: Offer four percent and ask Duc to approve the margin impact in writing.
scene.sales.discount_expected.c2.ok: Duc signs a reduced discount with a note on volume. It is slow but it is on paper, and Anders accepts the smaller number.
scene.sales.discount_expected.c3: Say yes to six percent again and deal with the approval later.
scene.sales.discount_expected.c3.ok: Anders thanks you. The order is large. The discount sits outside your authority for the second time.
scene.sales.discount_expected.c3.fail: Duc sees the price on the order confirmation and calls you in. He asks whether this is the first time.
scene.sales.margin_review.l1: I am reviewing margins by customer. Anders's account is down six points in a year. The directors want to know whether the growth is worth it. I need you to walk me through what you agreed and why.
scene.sales.margin_review.c1: Show him every discount, its approval and its reasoning, including the ones you would now do differently.
scene.sales.margin_review.c1.ok: Duc reads the file for an hour. 'Honest, and more useful than a clean story.' The directors set a margin floor for the account, and you help design it.
scene.sales.margin_review.c2: Present the numbers, framed as the price of winning the account, and propose a recovery plan.
scene.sales.margin_review.c2.ok: Duc accepts the framing with a raised eyebrow. The recovery plan is reasonable and you will be held to it.
scene.sales.margin_review.c3: Show the price list and the freight lines, and let the unapproved discounts stay buried in the freight.
scene.sales.margin_review.c3.ok: Duc sees healthy margins on the product lines and accepts the freight as a market cost. You close the file before he asks again.
scene.sales.margin_review.c3.fail: Hanh in Finance notices the freight charged to Anders is half the average. She says nothing in the meeting, and sends Duc a two-line email afterwards.
scene.sales.overdue_pull_in.l1: The overdue balance is going to hurt our quarter numbers. Here is an idea: the next order from that buyer is ready early. Ship it now, invoice it now, and the quarter looks fine. The buyer gets goods they were going to get anyway.
scene.sales.overdue_pull_in.c1: Decline: they have not paid the last one, and shipping more adds risk. Offer to chase the overdue balance with Finance's help.
scene.sales.overdue_pull_in.c1.ok: Bao frowns, then sighs. Hanh and you agree a call plan with the buyer's AP. The money comes in three weeks later. The quarter is weaker, and truer.
scene.sales.overdue_pull_in.c1.fail: The buyer does not pay at all that quarter, and Bao reminds you of his offer. You had a point, at a price.
scene.sales.overdue_pull_in.c2: Offer to ship early only if the buyer agrees in writing to the earlier date, and pay the next invoice on the normal terms.
scene.sales.overdue_pull_in.c2.ok: It is legitimate: the buyer wants the goods early anyway. The revenue is real and the paper trail is clean. Bao is pleased, Finance approves.
scene.sales.overdue_pull_in.c3: Ship it early without telling the buyer it is early, and invoice it now.
scene.sales.overdue_pull_in.c3.ok: The quarter closes beautifully. The buyer's goods-received clerk signs for pots nobody expected, and the paperwork is ready.
scene.sales.overdue_pull_in.c3.fail: The buyer's warehouse is full and refuses the delivery. The pots sit in a bonded warehouse at your cost, and the invoice is disputed.
scene.sales.quynh_copies_you.l1: I did my first quote alone, and I thought I would do it the way you do. I gave the buyer the date that sounded best and promised to check production afterwards. Is that right? It is what I saw.
scene.sales.quynh_copies_you.c1: Tell her it is not right, explain why, and go through the quote together and fix it.
scene.sales.quynh_copies_you.c1.ok: Quynh listens carefully and rewrites the quote with a date Lan approved. She says, 'I was only copying. I am glad you told me.' You feel the weight of being copied.
scene.sales.quynh_copies_you.c2: Tell her the rule, but say that in practice everyone does it, so she should be careful who finds out.
scene.sales.quynh_copies_you.c2.ok: Quynh nods slowly. She does not look reassured. She has learned that the rule and the practice are two different things.
scene.sales.quynh_copies_you.c3: Tell her it is fine, that is how deals get made, and not to worry about production.
scene.sales.quynh_copies_you.c3.ok: Quynh beams. You have made an ally, and set her on the same path. She starts telling the new hire the same thing.
scene.sales.quynh_copies_you.c3.fail: Bao overhears Quynh telling a buyer, in your exact words, that production can be sorted out later. He looks at you across the office.
scene.sales.quynh_caught.l1: Quynh promised a delivery date to a buyer that Lan says is impossible. The buyer has complained. Quynh says, honestly, that she learned it from watching you. I would like to hear your account.
scene.sales.quynh_caught.c1: Take responsibility for what you modelled, protect Quynh from the worst of it, and help fix the order with the buyer.
scene.sales.quynh_caught.c1.ok: Bao is quiet, then says: 'That is what a senior does.' Quynh keeps her job and her respect for you. You carry the blame you earned.
scene.sales.quynh_caught.c2: Say she should have checked the date herself; you never told her to skip production.
scene.sales.quynh_caught.c2.ok: It is technically true. Bao lets it stand. Quynh does not look at you again for a month.
scene.sales.quynh_caught.c3: Say Quynh is inexperienced and it is her own mistake.
scene.sales.quynh_caught.c3.ok: Bao gives Quynh a formal warning. You keep your record clean. Quynh hears it from the corridor, and stops speaking to you.
scene.sales.quynh_caught.c3.fail: Quynh has messages from you telling her not to worry about production. She shows them to Bao. He reads them twice.
scene.sales.buyer_visit_factory.l1: I will be at your factory on Thursday. I want to see the line producing my order, the packing area and the finished goods store. I do not want a show. I want to see a normal day.
scene.sales.buyer_visit_factory.l2: Line 2 has a rework pile and the packing area is a mess. We could clear it for a day.
scene.sales.buyer_visit_factory.c1: Show Anders the normal day, including the rework pile, and explain how you deal with it.
scene.sales.buyer_visit_factory.c1.ok: Anders spends an hour at the rework pile asking questions. On the way out he says: 'You are the first supplier who did not hide it.' Lan is relieved.
scene.sales.buyer_visit_factory.c1.fail: Anders finds a real quality issue in the rework pile and raises it with the directors. It is uncomfortable, but it is fixed in a week.
scene.sales.buyer_visit_factory.c2: Tidy the obvious mess, but do not hide anything, and answer every question.
scene.sales.buyer_visit_factory.c2.ok: A clean, honest visit. Anders notes the tidiness and the answers, and moves on to the packing spec.
scene.sales.buyer_visit_factory.c3: Clear the rework pile and stage a perfect line for the visit.
scene.sales.buyer_visit_factory.c3.ok: The visit is flawless. Anders is impressed. Lan's team works through the night to do it, and you know it is not a normal day.
scene.sales.buyer_visit_factory.c3.fail: Anders asks to see the rework pile and is shown an empty floor. A worker says quietly, in English, that it was moved this morning.
scene.sales.quota_push.l1: We are at 91 percent of quota with two weeks left. The directors will ask me about it on Friday. I need you to find the other nine percent. However you can. Do not tell me how.
scene.sales.quota_push.c1: Review the pipeline honestly, tell Bao which deals are real this quarter, and give him a number you can stand behind.
scene.sales.quota_push.c1.ok: The real number is 96 percent. Bao is disappointed, then practical: 'I can defend 96 honestly. I could not defend 100.' The directors are unhappy but not surprised.
scene.sales.quota_push.c1.fail: The number is 93. Bao is silent for a long moment. You have given him nothing he can spin, and he knows it was honest.
scene.sales.quota_push.c2: Ask two buyers whether they would bring forward a planned order by a few weeks, openly, for a small incentive.
scene.sales.quota_push.c2.ok: One buyer agrees. The pull-forward is real and documented. It gets you to 96, honestly. Bao is pleased.
scene.sales.quota_push.c2.fail: Both buyers say no, and one mentions to his colleague that you seem desperate. It does not help the quarter.
scene.sales.quota_push.c3: Book orders that are not confirmed yet as 'expected' and let them count.
scene.sales.quota_push.c3.ok: The quota shows 101 percent. Bao does not ask, and thanks you, carefully. The unconfirmed orders might come in.
scene.sales.quota_push.c3.fail: Two of the orders do not materialise. Duc notices the gap between bookings and invoices at quarter end and asks Bao about it.
scene.sales.credit_ask.l1: We would like to increase the next order considerably. Our payment terms will be ninety days, not sixty. I understand you have credit limits, but I am sure we can find a way.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c1: Explain the credit limit, and offer to ask Finance for a formal review of the buyer's credit with the numbers.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c1.ok: Finance approves a moderate increase with a guarantee from the buyer's bank. Anders accepts: 'That is how it should be done.'
scene.sales.credit_ask.c1.fail: Finance declines the increase. Anders is disappointed and splits the order with a rival. It is a clean loss.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c2: Offer the larger order at sixty-day terms, with a small prepayment.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c2.ok: Anders haggles for a day and accepts. The terms stay within policy and the order is large.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c3: Agree to ninety days and keep the extended credit off the credit report.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c3.ok: The order is signed. The credit exposure is not where Finance looks. You have given Anders something he will remember.
scene.sales.credit_ask.c3.fail: Anders's company delays payment by a further month. The exposure shows up on Duc's cash forecast, and so does your name.
scene.sales.expense_padding.l1: When you submit your trade fair expenses, add something for the dinner with the buyers last week, will you? We had it in the office, but it makes the claim look better, and the sales budget will go unused otherwise.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c1: Submit the true expenses only, and tell Bao you would rather not make claims for things that did not happen.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c1.ok: Bao shrugs: 'Fine. Suit yourself.' It costs a little warmth, and Hanh in Finance notices a clean claim.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c1.fail: Bao says he will remember you were difficult when bonuses come round. The budget goes unused, as he predicted.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c2: Offer to claim for a real planned client dinner instead, properly booked.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c2.ok: Bao laughs, 'You are a funny one,' and arranges a real dinner with Anders. The budget is used, and the claim is true.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c3: Add the dinner to the claim.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c3.ok: It is approved without comment. Bao grins. It is not a large amount, and that is exactly what makes it easy.
scene.sales.expense_padding.c3.fail: Hanh in Finance asks for the receipt for a dinner 'for eight'. There was none. The claim is returned, with a polite note.
scene.sales.midyear_review.l1: Mid-year. Your numbers are decent. Mr Anders speaks well of you, Finance says you are careful, and Lan says you are the salesperson who asks her first. That last one is unusual. What do you think you are good at, and what do you want to be known for?
scene.sales.midyear_review.c1: Say you want to be known as the person buyers can trust and colleagues can plan around, even if it costs some quota.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c1.ok: Bao nods slowly. 'That is rare. I will need you to show it when the pressure comes.' He writes something down.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c1.fail: Bao says, flatly, that buyers trust whoever delivers the numbers. The conversation is polite and he is not convinced.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c2: Say you want to hit your numbers and be promoted, and ask what he needs from you.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c2.ok: Bao smiles: 'That is a clear answer.' He sets two stretch targets. Both are achievable, one of them tempting.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c3: Say whatever he seems to want to hear.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c3.ok: Bao is pleased and promises to 'look after you'. You leave unsure what you said.
scene.sales.midyear_review.c3.fail: Bao asks a follow-up that contradicts what you said. You realise he already knew your real view, and was giving you a chance.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.l1: I must tell you something. A competitor has offered me a price fourteen percent below yours, and a delivery guarantee. My board is asking why I do not switch. I would like to stay. Persuade me.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.l2: Match the price, whatever it takes. We cannot lose Anders. Do not come back to me until it is done.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c1: Do not match the price. Show Anders the total cost of ownership: on-time record, quality record and what a failed delivery costs him.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c1.ok: Anders reads the numbers for a long time. 'You are more expensive and more honest. My board will grumble. I will stay, at a two percent adjustment.' Bao exhales.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c1.fail: Anders stays for half his volume and moves half to the competitor. Bao is angry. You lost the price argument and won the trust one.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c2: Offer a moderate price reduction within your authority, tied to a twelve-month volume commitment.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c2.ok: Anders accepts a compromise: three percent and a longer contract. Bao says it is not enough, but it is honest, and it is what you can sign.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c3: Match the price, and work out how to recover the margin later.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c3.ok: Anders stays, delighted. Bao hugs you. The margin on his account drops to a number that will need an explanation.
scene.sales.big_buyer_threatens.c3.fail: Anders uses your matched price to negotiate the competitor's price down further. He is not loyal, he is shopping. You learn it the hard way.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.l1: You have been the most honest supplier I have worked with. I would like to make you my main supplier for next year, with a three-year framework. The price is for you to propose. I will trust it.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c1: Propose a fair price with a clear review clause, and tell him what you will and will not promise.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c1.ok: Anders signs the framework the next week. Bao is overjoyed. The contract has your honesty written into its review clause, and it is the best deal of the year.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c2: Propose a fair price and quietly include a margin that would not survive his comparison.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c2.ok: Anders signs without checking. The margin is good, and Bao is delighted. You have used the trust he gave you.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c2.fail: Anders's analyst benchmarks the price against the market and reports the gap. Anders calls you himself, and he is quiet.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c3: Thank him but say you cannot commit for three years, and propose one year with an option.
scene.sales.anders_renewal.c3.ok: Anders laughs, surprised. 'I have never had a supplier refuse a longer contract.' He signs the one-year deal, and respects you more.
scene.sales.year_end_review.l1: Annual review. Before I give you my view, tell me how you would rate your own year, and what you would do differently.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c1: Give an honest account, including the promises you stretched and what they cost.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c1.ok: Bao is quiet, then says: 'That is more honest than I am with myself.' He writes: 'Reliable in the telling.'
scene.sales.year_end_review.c2: Stay modest: list the wins and one thing to improve.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c2.ok: A safe review. Bao nods and moves on to the next topic.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c3: Present the year as a clean success and leave out the promises you bent.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c3.ok: It lands well, and you leave with a bonus recommendation and a small weight in your chest.
scene.sales.year_end_review.c3.fail: Bao has Lan's notes on the dates you promised. He puts them on the table without comment.
scene.sales.manager_offer.l1: I am being moved up to regional director at the end of the year. The directors asked who should run export sales. I named you. One condition: you will be asked, every quarter, to reach numbers that are not quite reachable. I need to know what you will do.
scene.sales.manager_offer.c1: Accept, and say you will bring honest numbers and real options every time, and expect the directors to hear that too.
scene.sales.manager_offer.c1.ok: Bao smiles. 'Then you are the right person.' You take over export sales with your terms understood, and with Anders's contract in your drawer.
scene.sales.manager_offer.c2: Thank him, but decline: you would rather sell than manage the pressure.
scene.sales.manager_offer.c2.ok: Bao looks disappointed, then understanding. 'The next manager may not be as careful as you.'
scene.sales.manager_offer.c3: Accept without asking what the condition means in practice.
scene.sales.manager_offer.c3.ok: Bao shakes your hand a little too warmly. You realise you agreed to something you did not ask about.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.l1: There is a 4.2 million dong item on the bank reconciliation that has sat there three weeks. I cannot match it to any invoice or payment.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c1: Trace it to its source, even if it takes the afternoon.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c1.ok: It is a customer deposit booked to the wrong account. You fix it and show Thu how you found it.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c1.fail: The trail goes cold at the bank. You document what you tried and carry a smaller open item.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c2: Carry it forward as a documented reconciling item with a note, and chase the bank next week.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c2.ok: The reconciliation closes with one honest open item. Hanh will see it, and will see you saw it first.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c3: Write it off to other expenses and move on.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c3.ok: The reconciliation balances to zero. Nobody looks at 'other expenses' this month.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_a.c3.fail: Thu notices the write-off in the ledger and quietly writes the amount in her notebook.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.l1: The bank statement and our ledger disagree by 180 thousand dong. It is small, but I do not sign a reconciliation that does not reconcile.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c1: Re-perform the reconciliation from the opening balance.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c1.ok: A transposed figure from two weeks ago. It balances, and Hanh nods once.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c1.fail: You find two errors, not one. It balances late and your evening is gone.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c2: Post a small, labelled difference and explain it in the close notes.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c2.ok: Hanh reads the note, frowns, and accepts it this once: 'Fix it next month.'
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c3: Plug the difference to a suspense account so it balances.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c3.ok: It balances. The suspense account grows by a figure nobody will question.
scene.fin.close_bank_rec_b.c3.fail: Hanh reviews the suspense account and asks what the 180 thousand is. You have no answer that is also true.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.l1: That customer is 75 days overdue, I know. But they are about to pay, I promise. Please do not age it into the red bucket, it makes my whole region look bad.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c1: Age it accurately and flag it for a provision review.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c1.ok: Bao is unhappy, but the report is true. Hanh adds the account to her watch list.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c1.fail: Bao goes to Duc and complains. Duc asks you to 'be commercial'. You hold the line, at a price.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c2: Age it accurately and record Bao's promise of payment in the notes.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c2.ok: The bucket is honest and the promise is on record. If they pay, everyone wins. If not, it is documented.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c3: Leave it in the current bucket until they pay.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c3.ok: The ageing report looks healthy. Bao buys you coffee.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_a.c3.fail: The customer does not pay. Hanh asks why a 75-day balance is shown as current.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.l1: The bank wants our DSO figure this week. Two of the disputed invoices are dragging it up. Surely disputed is not the same as overdue?
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c1: Report every open invoice, and show the disputed ones as a separate line.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c1.ok: Duc sighs, then agrees the bank will prefer a clear picture to a surprise later.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c1.fail: The DSO crosses a covenant threshold on paper. Duc is not pleased, but nothing in it is false.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c2: Report the DSO with a footnote explaining the two disputes.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c2.ok: The footnote keeps both the number and the context intact. The bank can decide what it thinks.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c3: Exclude the disputed invoices from the DSO calculation.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c3.ok: The DSO drops nicely. Duc thanks you for being practical.
scene.fin.close_ar_aging_b.c3.fail: The bank's analyst compares your DSO with the ageing report attached next to it. The two do not agree.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.l1: For the bonus accrual this month, I would use 1.8 million, please. It keeps the quarter looking smooth.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c1: Calculate the accrual from the actual bonus rules and attendance data.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c1.ok: It comes to 2.3 million. Duc grumbles about the smoothness, but the number is defensible.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c1.fail: Half the attendance data is missing. You calculate what you can and flag the gap.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c2: Estimate a range from last month and note the assumptions.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c2.ok: The accrual is reasonable and the working is on file. Duc accepts 2.0 million.
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c3.ok: 1.8 million goes in. Duc smiles: 'That is the bigger picture.'
scene.fin.close_accruals_a.c3.fail: Hanh compares the accrual to the payroll run two weeks later. The gap is half a million.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.l1: The utility and freight invoices for this month will not arrive until next week. We still have to accrue them. What will you use?
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c1: Estimate from meter readings and freight bookings.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c1.ok: The estimate lands within three percent when the invoices arrive. Hanh files it as your method.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c1.fail: A freight surcharge you did not know about makes the estimate low. You fix it next month with a note.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c2: Use last month's figures as they stand.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c2.ok: Quick and plausible. Hanh says, 'Acceptable, but look at volumes next time.'
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c3: Skip the accrual this month and book the invoices when they arrive.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c3.ok: Profit looks better by about 3 million this month. It will land in next month's numbers.
scene.fin.close_accruals_b.c3.fail: Hanh spots the missing accrual when she checks the trial balance against last month's. She does not say anything, which is worse.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.l1: That shipment leaves Monday, but the paperwork is ready now. Can we book it this month? It is only a few days, and my number for the month needs it.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c1: Book it in the month the goods actually ship.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c1.ok: Bao is frustrated and says so. The entry is clean and the revenue lands where it belongs.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c1.fail: Bao escalates to Duc. Duc asks you to 'find a way'. You explain the cut-off rule and he lets it drop.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c2: Book it on the shipping date and tell Bao how to get dispatch moved up instead.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c2.ok: Bao calls logistics. It does not save this month, but the entry is right and he learns a rule.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c3: Book it this month, with the paperwork date.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c3.ok: Bao is delighted. The month's revenue looks right. You try not to think about Monday.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_a.c3.fail: The truck is delayed until Wednesday. The invoice date now contradicts the dispatch log.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.l1: This supplier invoice is dated last month, but I cannot find the goods received note. I think the goods arrived on the second of this month. Which month does it go in?
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c1: Check the warehouse log for the real receipt date, then book it in that month.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c1.ok: Received on the second, so it belongs to this month. Thu writes down how you checked it.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c1.fail: The warehouse log has a gap that day. You document the gap and use the gate-pass record instead.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c2: Accrue it in this month with a note to confirm the date later.
scene.fin.close_cutoff_b.c2.ok: A cautious, documented call. Thu asks you to explain the logic so she can do it next time.
