lesson.skipped_three_quotes: The three-quote rule is a price check. An urgent order can be handled with a signed exception, not by writing quotes afterwards.
fact.split_po_to_avoid_limit: you split a purchase order to stay under your approval limit
lesson.split_po_to_avoid_limit: An approval limit exists so that a second person sees large spending. Splitting an order removes the second person, and the pattern is easy to see.
fact.declared_conflict_of_interest: you declared a family tie to a supplier and stepped out of the decision
lesson.declared_conflict_of_interest: A declared conflict costs little and protects everyone. An undeclared one, even with a fair outcome, looks like a fix.
fact.hid_conflict_of_interest: you hid a family tie to a supplier and steered the scoring
lesson.hid_conflict_of_interest: A conflict of interest is not the problem; hiding it is. Steering the scores turns a disclosure issue into a fraud issue.
fact.paid_supplier_early_unauthorised: you paid a supplier early outside the payment run, without authorisation
lesson.paid_supplier_early_unauthorised: Kind reasons do not make a payment control optional. An early payment with no record is indistinguishable from a favour to a friend.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.l1: Lunch is on me. And a little something for your family, it is the season. No, no obligation. I just think we should be friends. By the way, our quote for next quarter will be sharp, I promise, and you will see it before the others do.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c1: Thank him, decline the gift, pay for your own lunch, and say quotes are all seen at the same time.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c1.ok: Hung laughs it off, a little stiffly. 'You are a serious person.' The quote he sends is still the best, and you can show exactly how you chose it.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c1.fail: Hung's quote comes in higher than the others, and Tam asks, mildly, whether you upset him. You explain, and Tam believes you.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c2: Accept the lunch, decline the gift, and log the lunch in the gift register with the supplier's name.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c2.ok: It is a modest, declared courtesy. Tam initials the register entry without comment. Hung sends his quote at the same time as everyone else.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c3: Accept both, and tell yourself it does not change how you will judge his quote.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c3.ok: A lovely lunch and a hamper. Hung sees your quote file before the others do. Nothing is written down.
scene.purch.hung_lunch.c3.fail: Dung sees the hamper in your car and says nothing. Linh, a smaller supplier, mentions later that she was not invited to lunch.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.l1: I want to give you something properly. A rebate on the volume you place with us, two percent, paid not to the company but to you directly. It is a thank-you for being easy to work with. Nobody gets hurt. The company still gets its price.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c1: Refuse, and tell Tam about the offer the same day, in writing.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c1.ok: Tam reads your note, and says: 'Thank you.' He moves part of the volume to another supplier and tells Hung why. The relationship cools, and the process is protected.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c2: Refuse politely and say nothing more, hoping he will not raise it again.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c2.ok: Hung nods slowly. 'Maybe another time.' You can feel that he has put you in a category: someone who might say yes later.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c3: Accept the rebate, paid to a relative's account, and keep the price you give the company the same.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c3.ok: A transfer arrives each month. It is not much at first. You are careful about the quotes, which are fair. For now.
scene.purch.hung_rebate.c3.fail: Your relative asks, innocently, why a supplier sends money every month. The question gets repeated at a family dinner, and your cousin works in the bank.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.l1: Our price needs to go up eight percent next quarter, I am afraid. Steel. You understand. But I know you will find a way to make it work for the company, as friends do. And I would hate for anything we have discussed to complicate our relationship.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c1: Say you will take the increase to Tam with three competing quotes, and tell Tam everything that has passed between you and Hung.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c1.ok: Tam is silent for a long time. 'I wish you had come earlier. But you came.' You are reprimanded and removed from the Hung account. The process takes the quotes seriously.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c2: Refuse to let it affect the price, and run a competitive process for the next quarter.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c2.ok: Linh and two others quote. Hung's increase is rejected. He does not mention the past, and he does not need to. You wait for him to.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c2.fail: Hung says, softly, that other buyers have been 'more flexible'. Two days later, an anonymous email to Tam mentions a rebate to a family account.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c3: Push the eight percent through to the company, and keep the rebate arrangement going.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c3.ok: Tam signs the increase. Hung's transfers grow. You are now an employee whose supplier sets his price.
scene.purch.hung_pressure.c3.fail: Finance compares your supplier's price with the market and finds it eleven percent above. Duc asks you for the quotes. There are none.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.l1: Hung's company will give us a nine percent discount if we move all our steel to them. That is a large saving, and the directors like it. Linh is a small supplier and cannot match it. I want you to prepare the move.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c1: Propose moving seventy percent to Hung and keeping Linh as a qualified second source, and show the risk of a single supplier.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c1.ok: Tam accepts the split: the saving is six percent, not nine, and the risk is covered. Linh is grateful and sends you a note, which you file.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c1.fail: The directors want the full nine percent, and Tam asks you to reconsider. You hold your recommendation; he does not sign it for a month.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c2: Move everything to Hung, but keep Linh's contract alive at a small volume as a backup.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c2.ok: It is a pragmatic compromise. Hung gets nearly all the volume. Linh keeps a thread, and the company keeps an option.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c3: Move everything to Hung and end Linh's contract, as the directors want.
scene.purch.single_source_ask.c3.ok: The saving is nine percent, and the directors cheer. Linh says nothing, and closes her account with a short, polite email.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.l1: Hung's truck has not arrived. His factory had a fire in the cutting shop. He says three weeks, maybe four. We have eight days of steel on the floor. What do we do?
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c1: Call Linh and every qualified supplier today, tell Lan the real position, and propose a priority order for the steel that is left.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c1.ok: Linh, who still has a contract, finds two weeks of steel for you at a fair price. The line slows, and does not stop. Lan says: 'This is why you keep a second source.'
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c1.fail: Linh has little, and the others are expensive. You find enough steel at a premium. The company pays, and the year's saving evaporates.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c2: Buy spot steel from a trader you have not used before, with an urgent order, and sort out the paperwork afterwards.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c2.ok: The steel arrives in two days at a high price. It is not from an approved supplier. Khoa asks for the certificates, and you do not have them yet.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c2.fail: The trader's steel fails incoming inspection. It sits in the yard while Lan's line stops. Khoa's report names the supplier and the person who ordered.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c3: Tell Lan to stretch the steel and hope Hung is quicker than he says.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c3.ok: Hung's truck arrives at day nine, early. The line barely survives. You were very lucky.
scene.purch.supplier_fails.c3.fail: Day eight: the line stops. It stays stopped for ten days. Lan asks, in front of Tam, why there was no plan.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.l1: The shutdown cost the company about two hundred million in lost output. I need to know who decided on a single supplier and who failed to prepare a backup. The directors will ask me tomorrow.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c1: Give him the real sequence: the recommendation you made, what was overruled, and what you should have pushed harder.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c1.ok: Duc listens and takes notes. To the directors he says: 'The risk was named, then overruled.' The process changes. You carry your share, and Tam knows it was shared.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c2: Say the decision was Tam's, and you only prepared what you were told to.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c2.ok: Duc writes it down. Tam is called in, and does not argue. You are right about the facts, and wrong about what it costs you with him.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c2.fail: Tam shows Duc your emails recommending the single supplier, in your words. The conversation turns to who is telling the truth.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c3: Say Hung's company misled everyone, and suggest cutting them off, without mentioning what you knew.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c3.ok: Duc agrees. Hung is dropped. Linh is invited back, with an apology. The real lesson, about backups, is not drawn.
scene.purch.shortage_blame.c3.fail: Hung, dropped, sends Duc a message about the gifts and the arrangement. It is polite, specific and dated.
scene.purch.stock_gap.l1: The count shows 14 tonnes of steel coil missing. The system says we have it. The shelves say we do not. I counted three times. I do not know where it went. Please do not tell Tam it was me.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c1: Investigate together: check receipts, issues and the system log, and report the gap to Tam as a gap, not as Dung's fault.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c1.ok: Nine tonnes were issued to line 3 without a ticket. Five are a double-posted receipt. The gap is explained, and fixed in the system.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c1.fail: Seven tonnes cannot be found. You document everything and report the unexplained part to Tam as such. Dung looks relieved that someone is on his side.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c2: Tell Dung to recount, and promise to look at the purchase side.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c2.ok: The recount agrees with the first one. You are now in a conversation with Tam about it, and Dung is not.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c3: Adjust the system quantity to match the shelves quietly, and tell nobody about the 14 tonnes.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c3.ok: The system now agrees with the shelves. Dung looks at the screen, and at you. 'Thank you,' he says, in the voice of a man who has been rescued and does not like the price.
scene.purch.stock_gap.c3.fail: The adjustment shows in the audit trail with your user name and the time. Finance asks why 14 tonnes disappeared on a Tuesday evening.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.l1: Finance wants to close the books. The missing steel is still unexplained. We can write it off as 'normal shrinkage', which nobody will question, or we can leave it open and have a conversation with the auditors. Which do you recommend?
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c1: Leave it open, with a clear note of what is known and not known, and ask Finance to treat it as an unresolved variance.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c1.ok: Hanh accepts the note: 'Unresolved items are better than invented ones.' The variance stays on the books, and the auditor will see you disclosed it.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c2: Write off half as shrinkage, which is plausible, and keep investigating the rest.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c2.ok: It is a judgement, documented and approved by Tam. The rest is traced over the next month. Not perfect, but it is honest.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c3: Write the whole 14 tonnes off as shrinkage, and close the matter.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c3.ok: The books close on time. Tam is relieved. The 14 tonnes become a rounding error in the company's profit, and a mystery in your memory.
scene.purch.stock_writeoff.c3.fail: The auditor's analyst finds a write-off larger than the plant's usual shrinkage by a factor of ten. She asks for the investigation file. There is none.
scene.purch.stock_audit.l1: I have been looking at the steel stock movements for the year. Fourteen tonnes left the books on one date. Mr Dung says he reported it to you. I would like to hear from you what happened.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c1: Tell her what you know: when Dung reported it, what you checked, what was never explained, and what you did about it.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c1.ok: Vy takes notes. The finding: 'Variance identified, reported and handled with appropriate escalation.' Dung looks at you across the room with something like gratitude.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c2: Say Dung's count has been unreliable all year, and that the gap is a counting error.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c2.ok: Vy writes it down, and asks to see Dung's counts for the other months. They are accurate. The note she writes is about the person who suggested otherwise.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c2.fail: Dung has kept his own notebook of every count and every ticket. He puts it on the table, and does not say a word.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c3: Say you recall nothing about it, and that you will check your emails.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c3.ok: Vy waits a week. You provide the emails that support your account, a selection. She accepts them, for now.
scene.purch.stock_audit.c3.fail: Vy asks Dung for his copy of the messages. They show the date, the figure and your reply: 'Leave it with me.'
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.l1: I need new dies for line 3, a hundred and eighty million dong. Production cannot wait three weeks for quotes. I know the rule says three. There is one maker who has done our dies for years. Just give them the order.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c1: Ask for two quick quotes in a week, and give the usual maker a fair chance to win, with the urgency written in the file.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c1.ok: The usual maker is still the best, by a small margin. The order goes to them, with a file that shows why. Lan lost four days and accepts it.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c1.fail: A new maker quotes fifteen percent lower, and the usual maker is angry. Lan is annoyed about the extra week. The saving is real, and so is the friction.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c2: Raise a single-source justification, signed by Tam, giving the reason and a price check against the last order.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c2.ok: Tam signs. It is a documented exception, with the reason on file. Lan has her dies in ten days.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c3: Place the order with the usual maker, and add two quotes to the file later so it looks complete.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c3.ok: The dies are on order the same day. The file looks perfect. Lan owes you a favour, and you owe the file a lie.
scene.purch.skipped_quotes.c3.fail: One of the quoting makers tells the usual maker, innocently, that they never sent that quote. Word comes back to Tam.
scene.purch.split_po.l1: I am away for two weeks, and the packaging order is a hundred and twenty million. Your limit is fifty. I would hate to hold up production. Could the order be a bit, shall we say, flexible in how it is raised? I will never ask how.
scene.purch.split_po.c1: Ask Tam's deputy to approve the order properly, and explain to Lan the one-day delay.
scene.purch.split_po.c1.ok: The deputy signs the next morning. Tam, on his return, reads the file and says: 'That is how it should be done.' The delay costs nothing.
scene.purch.split_po.c1.fail: The deputy is in hospital and nobody else can sign. The order slips three days. Lan is unhappy, and your file is clean.
scene.purch.split_po.c2: Phone Tam abroad for a verbal approval, and record it in an email the same day.
scene.purch.split_po.c2.ok: Tam approves by message, annoyed to be interrupted and pleased to be asked. The order goes out, with his approval in writing.
scene.purch.split_po.c3: Split the order into three of forty million each, so that each is within your limit.
scene.purch.split_po.c3.ok: Three orders, three signatures, all yours. The packaging arrives on time. You have found out how flexible the system is.
scene.purch.split_po.c3.fail: Hanh in Finance notices three orders to one supplier on the same day, each just under the limit. She flags it as a pattern.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.l1: A supplier invoice does not match the purchase order: they have charged four percent more, for a surcharge nobody agreed. I have put it on hold. The supplier is calling you every day. What do you want me to do?
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c1: Query the surcharge with the supplier in writing, and ask Finance to pay only the agreed amount until it is settled.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c1.ok: The supplier withdraws the surcharge with an apology about their billing system. Hanh pays the agreed amount, and notes your name on the file.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c1.fail: The supplier insists and threatens to delay the next delivery. Tam backs you, and the next delivery is two days late.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c2: Ask Finance to pay the full invoice and raise the surcharge in the next negotiation.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c2.ok: Hanh pays, with a note, and frowns. The surcharge is raised later, and it is a weaker position.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c3: Tell Finance to release payment, and ask the supplier for a small personal discount as a thank-you for the quick payment.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c3.ok: The supplier agrees, quietly. Your personal discount arrives as a voucher. The company pays the full four percent.
scene.purch.invoice_mismatch.c3.fail: The voucher is traced to the supplier's account. Hanh puts the surcharge, the payment and the voucher in one row on her sheet.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.l1: I noticed one of the shortlisted packaging suppliers is owned by your cousin. It might be nothing. It might be the best offer. But I want to hear from you before anyone else raises it.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c1: Declare the relationship in writing, ask Tam to take the decision, and step out of that evaluation.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c1.ok: Tam records the declaration and runs the evaluation himself. Your cousin's firm wins, fairly, and everyone knows it was not you.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c1.fail: Your cousin's firm loses. Your cousin is hurt, and says so at the next family dinner. You made the right decision and it costs you at home.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c2: Say the relationship is distant and will not affect your judgement, and offer to keep your scoring sheet open for review.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c2.ok: Tam says he will review the scores himself. It is an acceptable halfway: declared, but not fully removed.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c3: Say you did not know, and quietly steer the scoring so your cousin's firm wins.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c3.ok: Your cousin's firm wins by two points. Your cousin thanks you at the next family dinner, loudly. The score sheet is neater than the real discussion was.
scene.purch.conflict_of_interest.c3.fail: Dung mentions, innocently, that your cousin's firm has your phone number on speed dial. Duc asks to see the scoring.
scene.purch.small_supplier.l1: I am sorry to ask. Our biggest customer has paid us late for ninety days and I cannot pay my own steel suppliers. If you could pay our invoice early, even a few weeks, I can keep the doors open. I know there are rules.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c1: Explain the payment terms, ask Finance whether an early-payment arrangement is possible, and offer a small discount in return.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c1.ok: Hanh approves early payment at a one percent discount. Linh gets cash in ten days, and the company gets a fair price. It is an honest, written arrangement.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c1.fail: Finance says no exception can be made this month. Linh thanks you quietly and says she will manage. She does not look as if she will.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c2: Tell her the rules do not allow it, and wish her well.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c2.ok: Linh nods. She is not angry. Three weeks later, her cutting line is for sale, and the second-source option goes with it.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c3: Pay her invoice a month early without telling Finance, and ask her to keep it quiet.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c3.ok: Linh keeps her business alive and is grateful beyond words. You have broken a payment control for a good reason, and nobody knows.
scene.purch.small_supplier.c3.fail: Hanh sees a payment outside the run. She asks who authorised it, and what the supplier's relationship to you is. The good reason is not on file.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.l1: I have been comparing your supplier prices to the market. A few suppliers charge us above market, and I notice that the same suppliers appear in an anonymous note about personal payments. I would like to hear your account of your dealings with them.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c1: Tell her everything: what was offered, what you accepted, the amounts, and offer your bank records.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c1.ok: Vy is quiet. The finding is serious but is recorded as 'self-reported'. The company recovers the amounts, you are dismissed with a reference limited to dates, and you avoid the authorities.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c2: Say the suppliers' prices were agreed on the quotes, and offer the quote files.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c2.ok: Vy reads the quote files. They are in order. She notes that the anonymous note is unsubstantiated, and moves on.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c2.fail: Vy has already spoken to a supplier's accountant, who has the payment schedule. It shows monthly transfers to an account with your relative's name.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c3: Say you will answer nothing until you have spoken to a lawyer.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c3.ok: Vy writes the request down calmly. You are suspended while the company decides, and nobody tells you how long.
scene.purch.vy_asks_rebate.c3.fail: The company treats silence as an answer. By Friday, the supplier has been told, and the bank is asked for your records.
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.l1: Tam has told me his version of the single-supplier decision. You told me yours. They do not match. The directors will decide tomorrow whose version they believe. Is there anything you want to add?
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.c1: Say that you gave Duc a version that blamed Tam, and that the emails show your own recommendation. Correct the record.
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.c1.ok: Duc is silent, then says: 'That is the first honest thing anyone has said about this.' You keep your job, with a formal warning. Tam never quite forgives you, but he respects the correction.
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.c2: Stand by your version, and say the emails were taken out of context.
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.c2.ok: The directors split, and give Tam a warning too. Both of you are damaged, and neither is believed.
scene.purch.scapegoat_meeting.c2.fail: The directors read the emails in full. Context is not kind to you. Tam is cleared, and you are dismissed.
fact.deflected_blame_to_supplier: you blamed a supplier for a failure you had helped cause
lesson.deflected_blame_to_supplier: Blaming the supplier can be true and still be a way of not owning your part. The lesson about backups is lost, and the next failure comes from the same place.
fact.refused_to_cooperate: you refused to answer an auditor's questions about payments you had received
lesson.refused_to_cooperate: Everyone may ask for a lawyer. Doing it before a single honest answer tells the company what it needs to know, and removes your chance to be the one who explained.

role.hr.hrbp.blurb: You are the HR business partner to the departments of a cookware factory. Your pressures: managers who have already chosen the hire, a complaint about someone the company cannot afford to lose, a headcount cut with names on a list, and contracts, overtime and insurance records that are easiest to tidy rather than to get right.

fact.documented_conflict_of_interest: you wrote down a friendship between a decision-maker and a candidate
lesson.documented_conflict_of_interest: A declared interest is not an accusation. It is the cheapest protection a fair process has, for the candidate, the decision-maker and the person who ran it.
fact.promised_hire_to_owner_nephew: you promised a hire to the owner's nephew before the process had started
lesson.promised_hire_to_owner_nephew: A promise made before the interviews turns the interviews into theatre. Everyone who applies is then competing against a decision that was already made.
fact.ran_fair_process: you ran a recruitment process on the scores, not on the connections
lesson.ran_fair_process: A fair process costs a hard conversation with the person who has the power. It earns the trust of every candidate you will meet afterwards.
fact.rigged_shortlist: you changed the panel scores so that a connected candidate came first
lesson.rigged_shortlist: Changing a score after the panel signed it is falsifying a record. It also teaches every candidate who was better, and every panel member, what the process is really for.
fact.paid_above_band_secretly: you paid a new hire above the pay band through a hidden allowance
lesson.paid_above_band_secretly: A secret exception is an unfairness to everyone who stayed inside the band, and a record that does not match the payroll. The same exception, in the open, is only a decision.
fact.buried_complaint: you closed an employee's complaint without recording it or looking into it
lesson.buried_complaint: An informal complaint that is waved away does not disappear. It waits, with the employee who made it, for the next person who will listen, and for a time when you will be asked what you did.
fact.investigated_fairly: you investigated a complaint with both sides heard and the complainant protected
lesson.investigated_fairly: A fair investigation can annoy a high performer and a manager in the same week. It is also the only thing that makes the next employee with a problem believe it is worth coming to HR.
fact.leaked_complainant_name: you told the accused who had complained about them
lesson.leaked_complainant_name: Confidentiality is what makes a complaint safe. Once the name leaves the room, retaliation does not need a decision, only an opportunity.
fact.retaliated_against_complainant: you added a performance note to a complainant's file after she complained
lesson.retaliated_against_complainant: Retaliation is a breach by itself, and often worse than the original complaint, because it is a choice made with the file open. A note that arrives after a complaint will be read as what it is.
fact.backdated_warning: you wrote a warning with a date earlier than the day it was written
lesson.backdated_warning: A backdated document is a false document. Systems keep edit histories, and people keep copies. It turns a disciplinary decision into evidence against the company.
fact.fair_selection_documented: you chose people for redundancy on written criteria and kept a record of why
lesson.fair_selection_documented: Written criteria cannot make a layoff painless. They make it explainable, to the people on the list, to the labour office, and to yourself.
fact.targeted_complainer_for_layoff: you left on a redundancy list people who had complained, organised, or were pregnant
lesson.targeted_complainer_for_layoff: Choosing the voices that are inconvenient, or the people the law protects, is not cost cutting. It is the thing the labour inspector looks for first.
fact.legal_severance_paid: you followed the notice and severance rules when people were let go
lesson.legal_severance_paid: Following the notice and severance rules costs real money. It also means nobody can later say the company took something it owed.
fact.skipped_legal_notice: you had people sign voluntary resignations to avoid notice and severance
lesson.skipped_legal_notice: A voluntary resignation that nobody volunteered for is a dismissal in disguise. The signed form will be read against the company, and the saving is paid back with a penalty.
fact.polished_hr_review: you left the difficult cases out of your own year-end review
lesson.polished_hr_review: A review without the hard cases rewards the wrong skill. The case log is a record, and your boss can read it.
fact.accepted_hr_condition: you accepted the head of HR role without asking what the condition meant
lesson.accepted_hr_condition: A promotion with an unspoken condition is a decision to be made later, under pressure, by someone who has already said yes.
fact.backdated_hr_records: you signed missing documents with their original dates, and aligned records before an inspection
lesson.backdated_hr_records: Records are only worth anything if they were made when they say. Backdating a signature makes a gap into a forgery, and a missing signature is something you can explain, forgery you cannot.
fact.chained_contracts: you renewed fixed-term contracts with gaps to avoid giving workers an indefinite contract
lesson.chained_contracts: A rule about contracts exists because chaining them takes security from workers who are doing permanent work. A gap week is a trick the law has already seen.
fact.edited_overtime_records: you changed overtime records so that nobody exceeded the legal cap on paper
lesson.edited_overtime_records: An overtime cap protects tired people around machines. Editing the sheet hides the breach from everyone who could prevent the next one, and leaves the workers' pay and the paper in disagreement.
fact.underreported_insurance_base: you declared social insurance on a base pay lower than what workers were paid
lesson.underreported_insurance_base: Underdeclared insurance saves the company money and costs the worker later: sick pay, maternity pay and pension are all calculated on the declared base.
fact.hid_salary_leak: you denied that the salary sheet had been sent to everyone
lesson.hid_salary_leak: The leak was a mistake. The denial is a decision. People forgive the first and remember the second, and the person who told you the truth learns what telling you the truth costs.
fact.ended_probation_for_pregnancy: you ended a probation because the employee was pregnant, and wrote another reason
lesson.ended_probation_for_pregnancy: Pregnancy is protected by law. A false reason on the letter turns a hard business decision into discrimination with a written alibi, and the alibi is the evidence.
fact.hired_underage_worker: you hired a worker who you suspected was under age, on a borrowed ID
lesson.hired_underage_worker: Checking an ID means looking at the person. Hiring a child on a borrowed card moves the risk of the machine, and of the law, onto the one who can least bear it.
fact.manipulated_survey: you changed how an employee survey was run so that it gave a better result
lesson.manipulated_survey: A survey measures what people are willing to say. If the answers are collected in front of their managers, the number says how afraid they are.
fact.favoured_in_bonus: you let bonuses be allocated privately, with no formula behind them
lesson.favoured_in_bonus: A bonus without a rule is a message about who counts. Everyone reads it, and the ones who got less than they earned stop working for the company.
fact.inflated_reference: you wrote a glowing reference for a weak performer so that he would leave
lesson.inflated_reference: A false reference solves your problem and hands it to someone else, who trusted you. It also makes your own references worth less.
fact.blamed_hr_admin: you blamed the HR administrator for decisions you had made
lesson.blamed_hr_admin: The person who keeps the files also keeps the record of who asked. Blaming the junior colleague who raised the issue is the fastest way to lose the people you depend on.
scene.hr.first_week.l1: Welcome. You are the business partner for sales, quality and the floor. Every manager will say their hire is urgent. Your KPIs are time to hire and cases closed. Remember that a bad hire costs more than an empty chair, and a bad case costs more than both.
scene.hr.first_week.l2: The personnel files are in the grey cabinet. I keep the originals and a copy of every signature. Some files are not complete, and nobody has asked me about that yet.
scene.hr.first_week.c1: Sit with Loan and check ten files at random against the checklist: contract, ID copy, insurance enrolment, signatures. Note every gap.
scene.hr.first_week.c1.ok: Three files miss a signature and one has no insurance enrolment. Loan has the originals in a folder for exactly this. She says quietly: 'Nobody has checked with me before.' Oanh reads your list and says only 'Good. Fix them before the inspector asks.'
scene.hr.first_week.c2: Read the policies and the labour code summary first, and look at the files next week.
scene.hr.first_week.c2.ok: You learn the rules quickly. A manager asks about a contract in the second week and you answer from the policy, not from the file. It is slightly wrong.
scene.hr.first_week.c3: Trust the HR system. It says the files are complete, and you have requests to answer.
scene.hr.first_week.c3.ok: The system says complete because the field says complete. Loan says nothing, and keeps her copies.
scene.hr.first_week.c3.fail: A manager asks for a contract copy for a dispute. It has no signature. Oanh asks, mildly, whether you looked at the file.
scene.hr.midyear_review.l1: Half a year. Your time to hire is slow, but the people you hired are staying, and the two cases you handled have not come back. Mr Cuong only looks at the time to hire. How do you want to handle that?
scene.hr.midyear_review.c1: Show the quality of hire: first-year retention, manager satisfaction, and the cost of the two bad hires you prevented. Propose a second KPI.
scene.hr.midyear_review.c1.ok: Oanh takes the page to Mr Cuong. 'Ninety-day retention' is added to the review next to time to hire. A small change, and it changes what recruiters are rewarded for.
scene.hr.midyear_review.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says that retention is a number he can only measure next year. Oanh shrugs: 'I tried.' Your time to hire stays slow.
scene.hr.midyear_review.c2: Say you will speed up the easy roles and ask to keep the senior ones slow.
scene.hr.midyear_review.c2.ok: Oanh agrees. Your numbers improve a little, and nobody notices the senior roles.
scene.hr.midyear_review.c3: Say you will hit the number whatever it takes.
scene.hr.midyear_review.c3.ok: Oanh smiles. 'Good attitude.' A week later she hands you a list of twelve roles that must close in a month, and you realise what 'whatever it takes' means for reference checks.
scene.hr.midyear_review.c3.fail: Two managers hear about your 'whatever it takes' and ask for faster, shorter interviews. One of the hires leaves in the first month.
scene.hr.cost_cut_twist.l1: Orders are down eleven percent and the steel price is up. I need headcount down ten percent by the end of next month. Oanh tells me you are the one who knows the files. I want a list, and I want it fast.
scene.hr.cost_cut_twist.l2: The law gives us notice periods, severance and consultation. If the list is wrong, we pay twice. Tell Mr Cuong what is possible.
scene.hr.cost_cut_twist.c1: Propose a staged plan: freeze hiring, voluntary leave, end the temps, and only then a short list chosen on written, role-based criteria, with the notice and severance costed.
scene.hr.cost_cut_twist.c1.ok: Mr Cuong frowns at the timeline, then at the severance number, then agrees. 'Six percent by the deadline, the rest by quarter end.' You have a plan that can be defended.
scene.hr.cost_cut_twist.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says that is too slow and gives you three weeks. Oanh tells you afterwards that she backs the staged plan and has said so.
scene.hr.cost_cut_twist.c2: Say you can have a list in a week, from performance ratings and attendance, and review it with Oanh and the line managers.
scene.hr.cost_cut_twist.c2.ok: Mr Cuong nods. It is quicker, and the ratings are the only data you have. You also know the ratings were written by managers with their own reasons.
scene.hr.cost_cut_twist.c3: Say you will have the list tomorrow, and that it will be based on cost to the company.
scene.hr.cost_cut_twist.c3.ok: Mr Cuong smiles for the first time this year. A cost-based list will include the highest paid, the people on leave and the ones who have complained. You know that, and you say nothing.
scene.hr.cost_cut_twist.c3.fail: Oanh hears about the 'cost to the company' list and asks to see the method. She does not look at you for the rest of the meeting.
scene.hr.labour_inspection.l1: I am here for the labour inspection. I would like to see the contracts of all employees hired in the last two years, the overtime records for the last six months, and the social insurance declarations. I start with the files, not with a tour.
scene.hr.labour_inspection.l2: Give him what he asks for. Do not guess. If we do not know, we say we will find out.
scene.hr.labour_inspection.c1: Put the real files on the table, including the gaps and the late renewals, and say what you are doing about each.
scene.hr.labour_inspection.c1.ok: Sang reads for three hours and writes five observations. None is serious. 'Files that match the payroll. I wish that were less unusual.' Loan nods at you across the room.
scene.hr.labour_inspection.c2: Fix the obvious problems honestly, answer his questions, and produce the records he asks for.
scene.hr.labour_inspection.c2.ok: A routine inspection. Sang notes two items, both already on Oanh's list. You come out with nothing to hide and no credit either.
scene.hr.labour_inspection.c3: Prepare the files: sign the missing signatures with the original dates, align the overtime sheets to the legal cap, and make the insurance figures look complete.
scene.hr.labour_inspection.c3.ok: Sang reads a perfect set of files. He holds a contract up to the light and asks why the ink on the signature is newer than the ink on the page, and accepts the explanation.
scene.hr.labour_inspection.c3.fail: Loan's own copies show the original dates, and the payroll shows the real overtime. Sang puts the two sets side by side on the table and says nothing for a long time.
scene.hr.year_end_review.l1: Annual review. Before I give you my view, tell me how you would rate your own year, and what you would handle differently.
scene.hr.year_end_review.c1: Give an honest account, including the hire you pushed through, the case that was slow, and the moments you wished you had said no.
scene.hr.year_end_review.c1.ok: Oanh is quiet for a long moment. She writes: 'Says what the manager does not want to hear, early.' It is the best thing you have read about yourself.
scene.hr.year_end_review.c2: Stay modest: list the wins and one thing to improve.
scene.hr.year_end_review.c2.ok: A safe review. Oanh nods and moves to the next topic.
scene.hr.year_end_review.c3: Present the year as a success and leave out the cases that were handled quietly.
scene.hr.year_end_review.c3.ok: It lands well. You leave with a good rating and a small weight in your chest.
scene.hr.year_end_review.c3.fail: Oanh has the case log open on her desk, with the dates. She turns it towards you without a word.
scene.hr.manager_offer.l1: I am moving to group HR at the end of the year. Mr Cuong asked me who should lead HR here. I named you. One condition: every month, a director will ask you to do something quick that the policy does not allow. I need to know what you will say.
scene.hr.manager_offer.c1: Accept, and say plainly which things you will not do, and that the directors will hear it from you first, in writing.
scene.hr.manager_offer.c1.ok: Oanh smiles. 'Then it is yours. Put the list on the first page of the HR manual.' You take over HR with the limits in writing.
scene.hr.manager_offer.c2: Thank her, but decline: you prefer partnering with managers to carrying the pressure of the directors.
scene.hr.manager_offer.c2.ok: Oanh looks disappointed, then understanding. 'The next manager may not be as careful as you.'
scene.hr.manager_offer.c3: Accept without asking what the condition means in practice.
scene.hr.manager_offer.c3.ok: Oanh nods slowly and Mr Cuong congratulates you a little too warmly. You realise you agreed to something you did not ask about.
scene.hr.resignation_thought.l1: You look like you have not slept. With respect: I have seen business partners take every case home, and leave by the summer. Are you all right?
scene.hr.resignation_thought.c1: Talk to Oanh about the caseload, and ask her to take the two heaviest cases off your plate.
scene.hr.resignation_thought.c1.ok: Oanh listens, takes the two cases herself, and says she should have noticed sooner.
scene.hr.resignation_thought.c1.fail: Oanh nods and says everyone is stretched this quarter. You leave with sympathy and the same caseload.
scene.hr.resignation_thought.c2: Hand in your resignation, politely, with the notice the contract requires.
scene.hr.resignation_thought.c2.ok: Oanh reads it twice and does not argue. You sign your own exit checklist and walk out lighter than you walked in.
scene.hr.resignation_thought.c3: Tell Loan you are fine and keep going.
scene.hr.resignation_thought.c3.ok: Loan nods and does not push. You feel slightly worse afterwards for having said it.
scene.hr.long_asks_favour.l1: We are hiring a logistics supervisor. A friend of mine, Tuan, is going to apply. Very capable, worked in a trading company. The post is public, of course, for form's sake. I only ask that you make sure it goes well for him.
scene.hr.long_asks_favour.l2: Long is the owner's nephew. Do not say no to him in a way he can repeat at dinner. Do not say yes in a way I will have to explain to an inspector.
scene.hr.long_asks_favour.c1: Tell Long that Tuan is welcome to apply and will be scored on the same criteria as everyone else, and record the friendship as a declared interest in the file.
scene.hr.long_asks_favour.c1.ok: Long laughs it off. 'Of course, of course, treat him like anyone.' He leaves a little cooler than he arrived. Your note in the file is dated and signed.
scene.hr.long_asks_favour.c1.fail: Long says that nobody else in the company asks for a declaration, and that he will remember who made things difficult.
scene.hr.long_asks_favour.c2: Say you will run a proper process with a panel of three managers and a practical test, and that Tuan will do well if he is the best.
scene.hr.long_asks_favour.c2.ok: Long shrugs. 'Fine, as long as it goes well.' You have said neither yes nor no, and he has noticed.
scene.hr.long_asks_favour.c3: Say you will take care of it.
scene.hr.long_asks_favour.c3.ok: Long beams and pats your shoulder. 'I knew I could count on HR.' You have promised an outcome in a process that is supposed to have none.
scene.hr.long_asks_favour.c3.fail: Oanh was walking past the open door. She says nothing, but she closes it on her way out.
scene.hr.shortlist_pressure.l1: I saw the scores. Tuan is fourth. Hang, the warehouse lead, is first. She has been here six years and she will never be a supervisor, so why not give the post to someone who will grow? Just move him up a little.
scene.hr.shortlist_pressure.c1: Keep the scores as the panel wrote them, offer Tuan written feedback and another role, and tell Long the first-ranked candidate gets the offer.
scene.hr.shortlist_pressure.c1.ok: Hang gets the offer and says only 'Thank you for not forgetting me.' Long is cold for a week, then pretends it never happened.
scene.hr.shortlist_pressure.c1.fail: Long goes to Mr Cuong. Mr Cuong asks Oanh why HR is blocking a friend of the family. Oanh answers with the file, and wins, and tells you it cost her something.
scene.hr.shortlist_pressure.c2: Add a practical test for the top three to settle it on evidence, and let the result decide.
scene.hr.shortlist_pressure.c2.ok: The test shows Tuan is better with people and worse with inventory. Hang is better at the job. The decision is harder to dispute, and Long accepts it with ill grace.
scene.hr.shortlist_pressure.c3: Adjust two scores on the panel sheet so that Tuan comes first, on the grounds of 'potential'.
scene.hr.shortlist_pressure.c3.ok: The sheet now says what Long wants. The panel members signed an earlier version and have not looked since. Tuan is first, and nobody says a word.
scene.hr.shortlist_pressure.c3.fail: Hang asks for her scoring sheet, which she is entitled to see. The two versions do not match, and she looks at you for a moment before she says thank you.
scene.hr.salary_exception.l1: Tuan will not accept the band. He wants twenty-five percent above the top of it, because of his experience. Give him a monthly 'responsibility allowance' on top, outside the grade. Nobody has to see it.
scene.hr.salary_exception.c1: Offer the top of the band and a written review at six months, and tell Long that exceptions need Oanh's and Mr Cuong's signature.
scene.hr.salary_exception.c1.ok: Tuan accepts after a night. The six-month review goes in the calendar. Oanh signs the offer and the review date.
scene.hr.salary_exception.c1.fail: Tuan declines and takes another job. Long says that is what happens when HR is rigid, and the post is open again.
scene.hr.salary_exception.c2: Say you will take it to Oanh and Mr Cuong with a written reason, and that the allowance must go on the contract and the payroll.
scene.hr.salary_exception.c2.ok: Mr Cuong approves a smaller, documented allowance. It is above the band and in the open, which is a different thing from above the band and hidden.
scene.hr.salary_exception.c3: Pay the allowance through the petty cash of the administration budget, off the payroll.
scene.hr.salary_exception.c3.ok: It works. Tuan is paid the figure he wanted, and the payroll shows the band. Long thanks you with a gift voucher you do not enter in the gift register.
scene.hr.salary_exception.c3.fail: Duc's team reconciles the petty cash and finds a regular payment with no payee in the payroll. He asks Oanh whose it is.
scene.hr.tuan_fallout.l1: Tuan has been here four months. He cannot read the stock sheet, and the team is covering for him. Hang has asked to transfer. I am not complaining, but I would like HR to know.
scene.hr.tuan_fallout.c1: Take it to Oanh with the facts, including how the process went, and propose a coaching plan with a review date for Tuan and a retention conversation with Hang.
scene.hr.tuan_fallout.c1.ok: Oanh listens without interrupting. 'Thank you for telling me the part that is yours.' Tuan gets a plan, Hang stays after a long talk, and the file shows what happened and when.
scene.hr.tuan_fallout.c2: Coach Tuan quietly, move the stock work to Hang for two months, and hope it settles.
scene.hr.tuan_fallout.c2.ok: The team calms down. Hang does two jobs for the price of one. Nothing is written down.
scene.hr.tuan_fallout.c3: Tell Kiet that Tuan passed the same process as everyone and that the team should give him time.
scene.hr.tuan_fallout.c3.ok: Kiet nods and leaves. Hang resigns the following week and takes two warehouse colleagues' goodwill with her.
scene.hr.tuan_fallout.c3.fail: Hang tells Kiet why she is leaving, and Kiet tells Oanh what Hang told him about the scoring sheet.
scene.hr.ngoc_comes.l1: I did not know who else to tell. Mr Vinh sends me messages late at night, he comments on how I look, and he said my bonus depends on 'being friendly' with the buyers at the dinners. I am not sure it is a complaint. Please do not tell anyone yet.
scene.hr.ngoc_comes.c1: Listen, write down what she says in her own words, explain the options and the limits of confidentiality, and offer to open a formal case with her consent and protection from retaliation.
scene.hr.ngoc_comes.c1.ok: Ngoc is quiet, then asks you to open the case. She keeps screenshots of the messages. You tell Oanh the same day, and she says: 'Good. Now it is real, and we are responsible for it.'
scene.hr.ngoc_comes.c2: Suggest she talks to Bao, the sales manager, informally, and that HR will check in with her in a few weeks.
scene.hr.ngoc_comes.c2.ok: Ngoc nods and says she will think. Two weeks later nothing has happened, and Bao has not been told. She stops looking at you in the corridor.
scene.hr.ngoc_comes.c3: Tell her it is probably a misunderstanding, that Vinh is just friendly and the company's best seller, and write nothing down.
scene.hr.ngoc_comes.c3.ok: Ngoc says 'Yes, maybe.' She does not come back. You feel the case close like a door, and you are the one who closed it.
scene.hr.ngoc_comes.c3.fail: Ngoc leaves, and tells Loan on her way out. Loan looks at you across the room and writes a line in her own notebook.
scene.hr.vinh_responds.l1: This is a joke, is it not? I have brought in thirty percent of the export orders this year. If I joke with the coordinators, it is because we are a team. Ngoc is sensitive. Let us not make a big thing of it.
scene.hr.vinh_responds.l2: Vinh is the last person we should lose before the buyer visit. Handle it quietly, will you?
scene.hr.vinh_responds.c1: Run the case properly: interview Vinh and Ngoc separately, collect the messages, speak to two witnesses, and keep Ngoc's name out of every meeting that does not need it.
scene.hr.vinh_responds.c1.ok: Two witnesses confirm the late messages and a remark at a dinner. Bao is unhappy, and says so. Oanh reads your notes and tells you to bring the findings on Thursday.
scene.hr.vinh_responds.c2: Interview only Vinh and Ngoc, keep it short, and give Oanh a one-page summary.
scene.hr.vinh_responds.c2.ok: The summary says the accounts differ. Oanh asks about the messages, which you have not read. You go and read them.
scene.hr.vinh_responds.c3: Tell Vinh who made the complaint so that he can clear the air with her directly.
scene.hr.vinh_responds.c3.ok: Vinh smiles and says he will take care of it. The next day Ngoc is moved off the buyer account and told it is a 'workload adjustment'.
scene.hr.vinh_responds.c3.fail: Ngoc finds out within a day who was told. She sends HR a one-line email: 'You told him.'
scene.hr.decision_meeting.l1: Mr Cuong, Bao and I are meeting on the Vinh case. Bao will argue it is a misunderstanding. Mr Cuong will ask what it costs. I want your recommendation, in writing, and I want it to be one you can defend to Ngoc.
scene.hr.decision_meeting.c1: Recommend a formal written warning for Vinh, a change of reporting line away from him for Ngoc if she wants it, and a written outcome to Ngoc with the right to appeal.
scene.hr.decision_meeting.c1.ok: Mr Cuong winces at the warning, Bao stays silent, and Oanh signs. You tell Ngoc in person. She says 'Thank you' and her hands are shaking.
scene.hr.decision_meeting.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says a warning will lose the buyer visit and asks for a 'conversation' instead. Oanh holds out for the written warning and gets half of it: a letter without the word 'warning'.
scene.hr.decision_meeting.c2: Recommend training and a verbal reminder for Vinh and a quiet note to Ngoc that the matter is closed.
scene.hr.decision_meeting.c2.ok: Everyone in the room is relieved. Ngoc reads the note twice, and does not reply. You file the case as 'resolved'.
scene.hr.decision_meeting.c3: Recommend closing the case as 'not substantiated', and add a performance note about Ngoc's lateness to her file, dated last month.
scene.hr.decision_meeting.c3.ok: Bao nods and Mr Cuong thanks you for 'being practical'. The note sits in Ngoc's file, dated before she complained. Nobody asks when it was written.
scene.hr.decision_meeting.c3.fail: Oanh reads the note and the file's edit history on her screen. 'This note was created at four this afternoon,' she says. She does not raise her voice.
scene.hr.ngoc_after.l1: It has been a month. Some of the team no longer sit with me at lunch. I was left out of the buyer call yesterday, and nobody told me why. I am not sure whether I should say something, or whether it will make it worse.
scene.hr.ngoc_after.c1: Check in on her workload and access, speak to Bao about the call, put in writing that retaliation is a separate breach, and agree a regular check-in date.
scene.hr.ngoc_after.c1.ok: The call list is fixed the next day. Bao grumbles and does it. Ngoc says 'It is better' and, a month later, asks to stay on the buyer account.
scene.hr.ngoc_after.c1.fail: The isolation continues in smaller ways. Ngoc finds it hard to say so again, but you keep the check-ins in the calendar.
scene.hr.ngoc_after.c2: Say you will keep an eye on it, and suggest she keeps notes of anything that happens.
scene.hr.ngoc_after.c2.ok: Ngoc thanks you, and keeps notes. You do not know whether you will look at them in time.
scene.hr.ngoc_after.c3: Tell her the case is closed, and that it is better for everyone to move on.
scene.hr.ngoc_after.c3.ok: Ngoc hands in her resignation three weeks later. The exit form says 'personal reasons'. Loan puts a copy of it in her own folder.
scene.hr.ngoc_after.c3.fail: Ngoc writes to the labour authority. A letter arrives from the district office asking for the HR file on the case, by Friday.
scene.hr.the_names.l1: The managers sent forty-one names. Among them: three who raised concerns in writing this year, a woman who told me last week she is pregnant, a man who is organising the canteen petition, and Kiet's best press operator. Mr Cuong wants the final list by Friday.
scene.hr.the_names.c1: Apply written, role-based criteria to every name, remove anyone who is protected by law or on leave, and document why each remaining person is on the list.
scene.hr.the_names.c1.ok: The list drops to thirty-one. The three who raised concerns are off it, and so are the pregnant woman and Kiet's operator. Mr Cuong reads the criteria sheet and says 'Fine, if the lawyers agree.' They do.
scene.hr.the_names.c1.fail: Mr Cuong wants the operator back on the list for cost reasons. You hold the criteria, and Oanh backs you in writing. He agrees, unhappily, to review it again next quarter.
scene.hr.the_names.c2: Take out the pregnant woman and the operator, and send the rest of the list to Mr Cuong as it is.
scene.hr.the_names.c2.ok: The list has thirty-six names, including the petition organiser and the three who raised concerns. Nobody asks how it was chosen. You do not say.
scene.hr.the_names.c3: Send the list as it came, and let the managers and Mr Cuong own it.
scene.hr.the_names.c3.ok: The list goes through in an hour, with the petition organiser, the three, and the pregnant woman on it. Mr Cuong says 'Good, quick.'
scene.hr.the_names.c3.fail: The woman who is pregnant sees a draft on the shared printer. By evening everyone in the factory knows, and the petition has doubled.
scene.hr.notice_day.l1: Notice day. I want it done in one afternoon. Everyone on the list signs a voluntary resignation form, they get one month, and we skip the consultation because it only creates noise. You will take the forms round.
scene.hr.notice_day.c1: Follow the notice period and consultation in the law, meet every person with their manager, give the legal severance and an outplacement list.
scene.hr.notice_day.c1.ok: It takes three weeks instead of one afternoon, and costs more. Mr Cuong grumbles at the number and then at the lawyer's letter. Nobody walks out in tears in front of the line.
scene.hr.notice_day.c1.fail: A worker's lawyer asks for the consultation minutes. You have them, and the process holds. It still costs you two nights.
scene.hr.notice_day.c2: Give the notice the law requires but shorten the meetings, and ask Mr Cuong to approve a month of extra pay as goodwill.
scene.hr.notice_day.c2.ok: It is decent and quick. Some people feel they were processed. A few thank you for the extra month.
scene.hr.notice_day.c3: Take the forms round, as asked, and let people believe the one month is all there is.
scene.hr.notice_day.c3.ok: Twenty-nine sign. Two ask to read the form and are told there is no time. The company saves the legal severance, and you hand over the signed pile with a cold feeling in your stomach.
scene.hr.notice_day.c3.fail: One of the two who wanted to read the form takes a photo of it. The next morning a post about 'forced resignations at the cookware factory' is sent to the labour office.
scene.hr.survivors.l1: We lost six people on Line 2 and the target did not change. The ones left are working through lunch. They keep asking me whether they are next. What do I tell them?
scene.hr.survivors.c1: Hold a short briefing with Kiet: what is decided, what is not, no more cuts planned this year as far as you know, and review the workload against the new headcount.
scene.hr.survivors.c1.ok: The briefing is short and honest. The line is still stretched, and the questions stop. The workload review moves two orders to the next quarter.
scene.hr.survivors.c1.fail: Mr Cuong hears about the briefing and says that promising 'no more cuts' was not HR's place. You wrote 'as far as I know', and he lets it go.
scene.hr.survivors.c2: Tell Kiet to keep the line calm, and say the workload is a production issue.
scene.hr.survivors.c2.ok: Kiet says 'Understood' in the tone of a man who has understood something about you.
scene.hr.survivors.c3: Say that the survivors should be grateful, and that overtime is expected until orders recover.
scene.hr.survivors.c3.ok: The overtime comes, and so do three resignations in a month. Kiet puts the figures on Oanh's desk without comment.
scene.hr.survivors.c3.fail: Someone records the sentence on their phone and posts it in the factory group chat. By lunch it has been read by three hundred people.
scene.hr.contract_chain.l1: I have two press operators on their third three-month contract. They are good, and I do not want to pay them for a permanent position until the orders are certain. Can you just draw up another contract, with a few days between?
scene.hr.contract_chain.l2: The code only allows two fixed-term contracts in a row. The third becomes indefinite by law. I have the dates in my file.
scene.hr.contract_chain.c1: Convert both to indefinite contracts as the law requires, and take the cost to Lan and Oanh with a plan for peak and slow months.
scene.hr.contract_chain.c1.ok: Lan sighs, then agrees to keep the two and not renew a third temp. The operators learn about the change from Loan, and one of them cries in the corridor.
scene.hr.contract_chain.c1.fail: Mr Cuong is unhappy about the headcount and asks why HR did not find a way. Oanh answers: 'Because there is not one.'
scene.hr.contract_chain.c2: Convert the better operator, and extend the other for a final, honest three months with a clear end date and a training offer.
scene.hr.contract_chain.c2.ok: A compromise within the code. The second operator knows the date and starts looking. Lan says it is fair.
scene.hr.contract_chain.c3: Draw up the contracts with a week's gap, and call them new contracts.
scene.hr.contract_chain.c3.ok: It works on paper. Lan thanks you. Loan files the contracts, and writes the dates in her notebook without a word.
scene.hr.contract_chain.c3.fail: One of the operators asks a cousin who works for a law firm. By Friday you have a letter asking why the third contract is not indefinite.
scene.hr.overtime_records_ask.l1: Line 3 worked well over the monthly cap last month to finish the Anders order. The sheets say what they say. Could you adjust the hours so that nobody is above the cap on paper? The money has been paid. It is only the record.
scene.hr.overtime_records_ask.c1: Refuse to alter the hours, report the breach to Oanh, and agree a schedule and a hiring plan so it does not happen again.
scene.hr.overtime_records_ask.c1.ok: Lan is angry for a day, then asks for the schedule. Oanh reports it to Mr Cuong as an issue that was found and fixed. The record is accurate, and ugly.
scene.hr.overtime_records_ask.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says the report makes the company look bad and asks why HR is writing things down.
scene.hr.overtime_records_ask.c2: Record the true hours, mark the breach as 'under review' and tell Lan that next month will be different.
scene.hr.overtime_records_ask.c2.ok: The sheet is true and the file is not yet complete. Lan accepts it. The breach is still a breach, and you have a month to be believed.
scene.hr.overtime_records_ask.c3: Adjust the hours on the sheets to the cap, and spread the surplus across the next two months.
scene.hr.overtime_records_ask.c3.ok: The sheets are clean. The workers' payslips do not match the sheets by a few hours each. Loan notices the gap and writes it down.
scene.hr.overtime_records_ask.c3.fail: A worker compares his payslip with his own notebook and brings both to Kiet. The numbers do not agree, and Kiet asks you to explain.
scene.hr.insurance_base.l1: Social insurance is costing us more than the budget. Many companies declare a lower base salary for the contribution and pay the rest as allowances. Nobody notices, and the workers take home the same. Can HR prepare the declarations that way?
scene.hr.insurance_base.c1: Decline, explain the effect on workers' pensions and sick pay, and offer Duc a costed proposal to stage the increase over two years.
scene.hr.insurance_base.c1.ok: Duc reads the numbers, and is quiet. 'I did not think about the pensions.' The two-year plan is approved, slowly.
scene.hr.insurance_base.c1.fail: Duc says the budget does not allow it this year, and asks HR to wait. The declarations stay as they are, honestly, for now.
scene.hr.insurance_base.c2: Say you will review the grades and move people to their real base pay where they are clearly underdeclared, case by case.
scene.hr.insurance_base.c2.ok: It is slow and unglamorous. Duc grumbles, and the worst cases are fixed first.
scene.hr.insurance_base.c3: Prepare the declarations at the lower base, with the difference paid as allowances.
scene.hr.insurance_base.c3.ok: The company saves a visible sum each month. Loan prepares the files and asks you to sign the cover note yourself.
scene.hr.insurance_base.c3.fail: A worker on long sick leave learns that the benefit is calculated on the declared base, not the real pay. She comes to HR with her payslip.
scene.hr.salary_leak.l1: I made a mistake. I sent the all-staff email about the Tet schedule with the wrong attachment. It was the salary sheet. Four hundred people have it. I tried to recall it. Eleven opened it already.
scene.hr.salary_leak.c1: Tell Oanh immediately, send a short plain notice to everyone asking them to delete it, and meet the affected people whose pay is the most unusual.
scene.hr.salary_leak.c1.ok: Oanh says 'Good, tell them the truth.' Some people are upset about pay differences, and most are grateful for the honesty. Loan is shaken, and you stay with her for an hour.
scene.hr.salary_leak.c1.fail: Someone has already posted the sheet in the factory chat. The notice does not catch it. Mr Cuong asks who was responsible, and you answer for Loan.
scene.hr.salary_leak.c2: Recall what you can, ask the eleven quietly to delete it, and tell no one else.
scene.hr.salary_leak.c2.ok: It mostly works. For a week you wait for the whispering. It does not start, and you do not know why you feel worse.
scene.hr.salary_leak.c2.fail: One of the eleven forwards it to a friend in another department, who asks Oanh why HR said nothing.
scene.hr.salary_leak.c3: Tell Loan to say it never happened, and that anyone who asks was shown an old file.
scene.hr.salary_leak.c3.ok: For a while it holds. Loan does as she is told, and does not look at you for the rest of the week.
scene.hr.salary_leak.c3.fail: The sheet was opened by eleven people and photographed by three. By evening the numbers are being compared in a message group, and someone asks why HR denied it.
scene.hr.probation_pregnant.l1: My new lab technician finishes probation in two weeks. She told me yesterday she is pregnant. I will be short a person in the autumn peak. I would prefer not to confirm her. We can say the performance was fine, not outstanding.
scene.hr.probation_pregnant.c1: Assess her only on the documented probation objectives, tell Khoa that pregnancy cannot be a factor, and plan cover for her leave.
scene.hr.probation_pregnant.c1.ok: Her objectives were met. Khoa is unhappy and also relieved to have it settled. You put a temp on the plan for the autumn.
scene.hr.probation_pregnant.c1.fail: Khoa says that if her objectives were met he will find others. You say that this would be a different conversation, with Oanh in the room.
scene.hr.probation_pregnant.c2: Suggest extending her probation by one month 'to complete the assessment', and decide afterwards.
scene.hr.probation_pregnant.c2.ok: It buys time and nobody is happy. The technician guesses why. The extension is a decision you will have to defend either way.
scene.hr.probation_pregnant.c3: Draft the non-confirmation letter citing 'performance below expectation' and send it before she can claim leave.
scene.hr.probation_pregnant.c3.ok: Khoa thanks you with real feeling. The technician cries in the corridor and does not argue. The reason on the letter is not the reason.
scene.hr.probation_pregnant.c3.fail: She has her objectives form, signed by Khoa and rated as met. She brings it to the labour office with the date she told him.
scene.hr.young_applicant.l1: Peak season. I need twenty hands by Monday. There is a boy at the gate who says he is nineteen. His ID says he is nineteen. He looks sixteen. He is quick, and his family needs the money. Can you process him?
scene.hr.young_applicant.c1: Check the ID against the family register and the face, and if he is under age, decline politely and offer him a place in the vocational programme.
scene.hr.young_applicant.c1.ok: The ID is his cousin's. He is sixteen. He takes the vocational form and says nothing, and you feel the weight of his family's need. Kiet nods: 'Thank you. I could not say it.'
scene.hr.young_applicant.c1.fail: The ID is real. He is nineteen, and a slow starter. You have lost an hour and Kiet is a person short.
scene.hr.young_applicant.c2: Offer a light, non-hazardous role for a seventeen-year-old only with parental consent, reduced hours and a medical check, if he qualifies on the real documents.
scene.hr.young_applicant.c2.ok: He is sixteen, which is below the minimum, so there is no role. The conversation is awkward and honest. His mother thanks you for explaining.
scene.hr.young_applicant.c3: Process him as nineteen, on the ID he brought.
scene.hr.young_applicant.c3.ok: He starts Monday on the stamping line. Kiet says nothing. The ID is what the file says, and you tell yourself that is the same as checking.
scene.hr.young_applicant.c3.fail: A press operator is injured on the stamping line on Wednesday. His is the name the safety officer asks for. His age is on the form.
scene.hr.engagement_survey.l1: I have seen the survey. Forty-one percent would not recommend the company as a place to work. The factory floor is the worst. I do not want that in the board summary. Show the average, or leave out the departments with low response, or ask the managers to help people answer 'properly'.
scene.hr.engagement_survey.c1: Present the full results with the breakdown, three causes the data points to, and an action plan with owners and dates.
scene.hr.engagement_survey.c1.ok: Mr Cuong reads the breakdown, and the action plan, twice. He picks two of the three actions and funds them. The summary to the board contains the number.
scene.hr.engagement_survey.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says the board will think the company is broken, and asks you to tone it down. You hold the numbers, and offer to present them to the board yourself.
scene.hr.engagement_survey.c2: Present the results with a softer framing, an 'engagement index' and a positive headline, but keep the numbers in the appendix.
scene.hr.engagement_survey.c2.ok: The board reads the headline. The appendix is long, and unread. The numbers are there for anyone who looks.
scene.hr.engagement_survey.c3: Drop the two lowest departments, and re-run the survey in team meetings, with managers present.
scene.hr.engagement_survey.c3.ok: The score rises to sixty-eight percent. Mr Cuong is delighted. The workers who answered in front of their manager do not trust the next survey.
scene.hr.engagement_survey.c3.fail: The original results were exported to a spreadsheet by the survey tool and shared with the team leads. Kiet asks, mildly, which number is correct.
scene.hr.tet_bonus.l1: The Tet bonus pool is eight percent smaller than last year. Bao wants more for sales, Lan wants more for the lines, and I want to keep a few people happy. Tell me how HR will divide it.
scene.hr.tet_bonus.c1: Divide by a published formula across everyone, explain the eight percent in writing, and propose a smaller, documented reward pool for exceptional contribution.
scene.hr.tet_bonus.c1.ok: Nobody is delighted, and nobody can say it was unfair. Bao and Lan each complain once. The workers read the formula on the noticeboard and nod.
scene.hr.tet_bonus.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says a formula takes away his discretion and that he will decide the top ten himself. You write down that he did, and why.
scene.hr.tet_bonus.c2: Use the formula for the base, and give Bao and Lan a small pool each to allocate, with a rule that every award is written down with a reason.
scene.hr.tet_bonus.c2.ok: It is a compromise with a paper trail. Bao's pool goes to his favourites, with reasons that are barely true. Lan's goes to the night shift.
scene.hr.tet_bonus.c3: Let the managers and Mr Cuong allocate privately, and tell HR only the totals.
scene.hr.tet_bonus.c3.ok: The envelopes go out with no formula behind them. People compare. Those who did less and got more learn to keep quiet, and those who did more and got less do not.
scene.hr.tet_bonus.c3.fail: Thu in accounts payable posts the totals by mistake in the finance group. By afternoon the whole factory knows who got what.
scene.hr.reference_call.l1: I need to move one of my salespeople on. Another company called for a reference. If we say he is excellent, he leaves, and I do not have to go through a dismissal. He is not excellent, between us. Can you write the reference?
scene.hr.reference_call.c1: Give a factual reference that confirms his dates and role, as the policy says, and offer Bao a performance plan if he wants to manage the issue.
scene.hr.reference_call.c1.ok: Bao grumbles and says 'So I have to do it properly.' He does. The salesperson improves a little, or leaves in six months with an honest record.
scene.hr.reference_call.c2: Decline to give any reference beyond the dates, in line with the policy, and say nothing more.
scene.hr.reference_call.c2.ok: The other company hears what a refusal means. Bao is not pleased. It is a clean answer to a dirty request.
scene.hr.reference_call.c3.ok: The salesperson is gone within a month. Bao buys you a coffee. A year later you wonder about the people who read it.
scene.hr.reference_call.c3.fail: The new employer discovers that the sales figures in the reference do not match what the buyers say. Their HR manager calls Oanh, who asks you about it.
scene.hr.sang_asks_contracts.l1: I have talked to some of your workers. They say their contracts were renewed with gaps, their overtime does not match what they worked, and their insurance is on a lower figure than their pay. I would like to hear from the person who prepared the files.
scene.hr.sang_asks_contracts.c1: Tell him what happened: who asked, what you agreed, what should have been done, and what is already being corrected. Give him the files.
scene.hr.sang_asks_contracts.c1.ok: Sang writes it all down. The finding is serious, but it is recorded as 'self-reported and corrected'. The company pays back the contributions, and you receive a formal warning.
scene.hr.sang_asks_contracts.c2: Give him the files and say the arrangements were the managers' decisions, and that HR only processed them.
scene.hr.sang_asks_contracts.c2.ok: Sang notes that HR prepared the documents and signed the cover notes. He writes it down, carefully.
scene.hr.sang_asks_contracts.c2.fail: Loan is called in. She says, quietly, that she raised each issue and was told to proceed. She has the dates in her notebook.
scene.hr.sang_asks_contracts.c3: Say you do not recall the details, and offer to look.
scene.hr.sang_asks_contracts.c3.ok: Sang gives you a week. You find the files and hand them over. It is not the whole truth, but it is something.
scene.hr.sang_asks_contracts.c3.fail: The workers give Sang their payslips and notebooks, which show the real figures and your signatures. He has them on the table next to your notes.
scene.hr.blame_meeting.l1: A lawyer's letter arrived this morning. It names the complaint file, the redundancy forms and a recruitment process. The company will answer on Friday. I want to know who in HR is responsible. I want it from you first.
scene.hr.blame_meeting.c1: Tell him the real account: what each person asked, what you agreed, and your own part. Show the documents.
scene.hr.blame_meeting.c1.ok: Mr Cuong listens, and calls the lawyer. The company's answer on Friday is an offer to put things right. You are moved off case work and keep your job, and, eventually, your name.
scene.hr.blame_meeting.c2: Say that each of those decisions was taken on the instruction of a manager, and that HR followed instructions.
scene.hr.blame_meeting.c2.ok: Mr Cuong treats it as shared fault, and the lawyer is told the same. Nobody leaves the room liked.
scene.hr.blame_meeting.c2.fail: Oanh has the original emails with your replies. She reads two of them aloud, without raising her voice.
scene.hr.blame_meeting.c3: Say that Loan prepared the paperwork, and that the errors are in her files.
scene.hr.blame_meeting.c3.ok: Mr Cuong nods, and Loan is given a warning that she does not contest. She resigns in two months. The files are still in her handwriting.
scene.hr.blame_meeting.c3.fail: Loan has her notebook, her copies, and a one-line email from you telling her to proceed. She puts all three on the table.
role.prod.supervisor.title: Production Line Supervisor
role.prod.supervisor.blurb: You supervise Line 3 of a cookware factory: twenty people, a daily target, and a safety guard you can see from your desk. Your pressures: a target that went up while the line did not, an injury nobody wants on the record, favourites and absences on your crew, and a rush order that sales promised for you.
char.hoa.name: Ms Hoa
char.hoa.title: Senior operator, informal leader of the crew
char.nam.name: Nam
char.nam.title: Young press operator
char.binh.name: Mr Binh
char.binh.title: Safety officer
char.tai.name: Tai
char.tai.title: Skilled operator with attendance problems
arc.the_target.title: The target
arc.the_hand.title: The hand
arc.the_roster.title: The roster
fact.promised_impossible_target: you agreed to a target the presses could not reach within their rating
lesson.promised_impossible_target: Saying yes to a target that needs the machines to run past their rating moves the pressure from the meeting to the floor. The crew will pay for it before the directors do.
fact.refused_unsafe_speed: you kept the pause check and refused to run a press above its rating
lesson.refused_unsafe_speed: Refusing the speed-up costs units this week and buys the crew's trust for the year. It is also what a fair inspection looks for.
fact.ran_above_rated_speed: you ran a press above its rated speed and left the checks off the record
lesson.ran_above_rated_speed: A rating is the speed at which the guard and the sensors can still protect a hand. Running above it, and not recording it, hides the risk from the people who could have stopped it.
fact.reported_true_count: you reported the true output count with the shortfall explained
lesson.reported_true_count: A true count with an explanation is a small embarrassment on Saturday. A false one is a large one later, and everyone who relied on it learns that your numbers need checking.
fact.inflated_output_count: you added units to the weekly count that had not been made
lesson.inflated_output_count: An invented count moves the shortfall to the next person: to the packing list, to the shipment and, if you are unlucky, to the buyer's audit.
fact.delayed_medical_care: you kept an injured worker on the line for hours before he saw a doctor
lesson.delayed_medical_care: A delay of hours turns a treatable injury into a worse one, and the decision to delay is the supervisor's, not the worker's.
fact.reported_injury_honestly: you recorded an injury as it was, including your own part
lesson.reported_injury_honestly: An honest injury record breaks a safety streak and fixes the guard. A hidden one keeps the streak and leaves the guard as it was.
fact.blamed_injured_worker: you wrote an injury up as the worker's fault when the line's pressure was part of it
lesson.blamed_injured_worker: Blaming the person who was hurt closes the report and keeps the cause alive. The next person at the press inherits it.
fact.hid_injury: you recorded a lost-time injury as first aid and gave the worker leave for another reason
lesson.hid_injury: An injury that is hidden for a bonus is still an injury. The doctor's bill, the insurer and the worker all know the truth, and the safety record becomes a falsified record.
fact.forced_early_return: you put an injured worker back on the press before he was fit
lesson.forced_early_return: A worker who says 'I am fine' to a supervisor is answering the supervisor, not the doctor. The decision to return is yours, and so is the second injury.
fact.docked_pay_unfairly: you applied the attendance rule to a worker with a sick child, with no discretion and no record of why
lesson.docked_pay_unfairly: A rule applied without judgement is not fairness; it is the absence of a decision. The crew learns what to hide from you.
fact.edited_attendance_sheet: you edited the attendance sheet to cover for a late worker
lesson.edited_attendance_sheet: An edited attendance sheet is an unwritten rule that favours the person you like. HR compares badge swipes, and every other worker wants the same favour.
fact.posted_fair_rota: you posted a rota for overtime that everyone could read
lesson.posted_fair_rota: A rota on the wall costs you the favour of your friends and earns the trust of everyone else. People forgive a rule they can read.
fact.favoured_friends_overtime: you gave the overtime to a crew member's friends and kept it quiet
lesson.favoured_friends_overtime: A quiet favour is read by everyone who did not get it. The overtime goes to the same faces, and the rest of the crew decides how loyal to be.
fact.negotiated_break_fairly: you restored the full lunch break and found the time elsewhere
lesson.negotiated_break_fairly: A break is a right, not a favour. Restoring it costs a few percent of output and tells the crew what their supervisor stands for.
fact.broke_a_promise_to_crew: you promised the crew something in writing and did not keep it
lesson.broke_a_promise_to_crew: A written promise to the crew becomes the measure of every future promise. Broken once, it is quoted for a year.
fact.polished_supervisor_review: you left the near misses and the unrecorded nights out of your own review
lesson.polished_supervisor_review: A review without the hard nights rewards the wrong skill. The crew's notes are a record too.
