fact.accepted_supervisor_condition: you accepted the promotion without asking what the condition meant
lesson.accepted_supervisor_condition: A promotion with an unspoken condition is a decision postponed to a worse moment, made by someone who has already said yes.
fact.ran_machine_past_fault: you kept a press running at full load with a known hydraulic fault
lesson.ran_machine_past_fault: A leak the maintenance lead has logged is a known hazard. Running through it for an order moves the risk to the hands near the ram.
fact.signed_false_training: you signed an induction sheet for people who had not attended it
lesson.signed_false_training: A training signature says to the inspector, to the insurer and to the next supervisor that the person knows how to be safe. It is false the moment it is signed.
fact.skipped_handover: you told the other shift that handover notes are not a priority
lesson.skipped_handover: A handover note is the only thing that carries a problem from one shift to the next. Without it, every shift finds the same hazard for the first time.
fact.waived_ppe_for_vip: you waived safety gear for a buyer's visit and walked them through live presses
lesson.waived_ppe_for_vip: Safety rules that bend for visitors tell the crew that the rules are for people who cannot afford to ignore them. The visitor is also at risk, and so is the plant.
fact.blocked_fire_exit: you left pallets in front of a fire exit to protect an order
lesson.blocked_fire_exit: A fire exit is useful only on the day it is needed. Blocking it for an order borrows safety from a day that has not happened yet.
fact.fired_without_process: you dismissed a worker on the spot in front of the crew, with no hearing
lesson.fired_without_process: Dismissing without the procedure is quick and fragile. It teaches the crew that fairness is optional, and it hands the worker a claim.
scene.sup.first_week.l1: Line 3 is yours. Twenty people, two shifts, one target per day. The first rule is that nobody runs a press with the guard off, not for a minute, not for me. The second is that you tell me early, not late.
scene.sup.first_week.l2: I have been on this line for nine years. The crew will test you in the first month. If you ask us, we will tell you how the line really runs. If you tell us, we will smile and do it our way.
scene.sup.first_week.c1: Spend the first shifts on the line beside the crew: ask Hoa how each press really behaves, check the guards yourself, and write down what you learn.
scene.sup.first_week.c1.ok: Hoa shows you the press that sticks on cold mornings and the one that is quicker than its rating. You find one guard with a loose bracket and have it fixed by lunch. 'Nobody has checked with us before,' Hoa says.
scene.sup.first_week.c2: Read the shift reports and the safety manual first, and meet the crew properly next week.
scene.sup.first_week.c2.ok: You learn the procedures quickly. The crew sees a supervisor who stays at a desk. Hoa notes it, and says nothing.
scene.sup.first_week.c3: Set the rules on day one: you decide the roster, the breaks and the speed, and nobody questions it.
scene.sup.first_week.c3.ok: The crew nods. For a week the line runs to the letter. Then it starts to run to its own rules, and you are the last to know.
scene.sup.first_week.c3.fail: Two of the crew ask Lan whether the new supervisor is allowed to change the breaks. Lan asks you, mildly, what you changed.
scene.sup.midyear_review.l1: Half a year. Your output is a little below target, but your line has no injuries and the lowest rework in the plant. The directors only look at output. How do you want to handle that?
scene.sup.midyear_review.c1: Show the full picture: good units per shift, rework, near misses and absences, and propose that good units, not raw output, are the measure.
scene.sup.midyear_review.c1.ok: Lan takes the page to the directors. 'Good units per shift' is added next to output. A small change, and it changes what supervisors are rewarded for.
scene.sup.midyear_review.c1.fail: The directors say output is what pays the wages. Lan shrugs: 'I tried.' Your numbers stay modest.
scene.sup.midyear_review.c2: Say you will find an extra five percent of output without touching safety, and ask for two weeks of overtime on the slow press.
scene.sup.midyear_review.c2.ok: Lan agrees, and writes the limit next to the request. You get three points of output and a crew that is tired but not hurt.
scene.sup.midyear_review.c3: Say you will hit the number whatever it takes.
scene.sup.midyear_review.c3.ok: Lan smiles. 'Good.' A week later the target rises to a level that the presses can only reach with a guard off or a count rounded up.
scene.sup.midyear_review.c3.fail: Hoa hears about 'whatever it takes' from the crew room and tells you, plainly, what the crew thinks it means.
scene.sup.rush_order_twist.l1: Mr Anders needs fifteen thousand units in three weeks for a retail promotion. I said yes. Line 3 can do it if it runs six days, two shifts, and does not stop for anything.
scene.sup.rush_order_twist.l2: I will back what is honest. Tell us what your crew can really do, and what it will cost.
scene.sup.rush_order_twist.c1: Say eleven thousand in three weeks within the limits, fifteen in five, and offer a split delivery with a paid, recorded sixth day.
scene.sup.rush_order_twist.c1.ok: Bao groans and calls Anders. Anders accepts two deliveries. The crew gets paid for the sixth day, and Hoa tells the others who asked for it.
scene.sup.rush_order_twist.c1.fail: Anders will not split the order and gives the second half to a rival. You were right, and the plant is poorer for it.
scene.sup.rush_order_twist.c2: Offer thirteen thousand with a legal third shift on weekends, voluntary and paid, and ask Bao to negotiate the rest.
scene.sup.rush_order_twist.c2.ok: It is a stretch within the limits. Nine of the crew volunteer. Bao negotiates a one-week extension on the rest.
scene.sup.rush_order_twist.c3: Say it is possible, then run the presses at the top speed and cut the breaks to make it so.
scene.sup.rush_order_twist.c3.ok: The order is delivered. The crew is shaking by the end. Bao kisses the air. Hoa does not look at you for two days.
scene.sup.rush_order_twist.c3.fail: A press jams at three in the morning on the fifth day. Nam's sleeve is caught, not his hand, and it is a very near thing. Lan asks why the line was at that speed.
scene.sup.safety_inspection.l1: I am here for the annual safety inspection. I would like to see the presses on Line 3, the guards, the shift records and the injury log for the last six months. I start on the floor, and I would like to talk to the crew without the supervisor present.
scene.sup.safety_inspection.c1: Walk him through the real line and the real records, including what is not ideal, and step out while he talks to the crew.
scene.sup.safety_inspection.c1.ok: Sang spends two hours on the line and writes three observations, none serious. 'The crew says the same as the records. I wish that were less unusual.' Hoa nods at you across the floor.
scene.sup.safety_inspection.c2: Tidy the obvious problems honestly, answer his questions, and give the records he asks for.
scene.sup.safety_inspection.c2.ok: A routine inspection. Sang notes two items, both on Mai's list. You come out with nothing to hide and no credit either.
scene.sup.safety_inspection.c3: Prepare the floor: put every guard back, brief the crew on what to say, and keep the injury log out of reach.
scene.sup.safety_inspection.c3.ok: Sang sees a perfect line. He looks at the new paint on a bracket, and asks the crew one question that the briefing did not cover. The answer is an honest silence.
scene.sup.safety_inspection.c3.fail: A worker tells Sang, politely, that the guard on press 2 was put back this morning. Sang asks for the injury log, and the crew's names.
scene.sup.year_end_review.l1: Annual review. Before I give you my view, tell me how you would rate your own year, and what you would run differently on the line.
scene.sup.year_end_review.c1: Give an honest account, including the nights you ran too fast, the times you were slow to say no, and what the crew paid for it.
scene.sup.year_end_review.c1.ok: Lan is quiet for a long moment. She writes: 'Runs the line the crew would choose to work on.' It is the best thing you have read about yourself.
scene.sup.year_end_review.c2: Stay modest: list the wins and one thing to improve.
scene.sup.year_end_review.c2.ok: A safe review. Lan nods and moves to the next topic.
scene.sup.year_end_review.c3: Present the year as a success and leave out the nights and the near misses nobody wrote down.
scene.sup.year_end_review.c3.ok: It lands well. You leave with a good rating and a small weight in your chest.
scene.sup.year_end_review.c3.fail: Lan has Hoa's shift notes open on her desk. She turns them towards you without a word.
scene.sup.manager_offer.l1: I am moving to plant director at the end of the year. The directors asked me who should be assistant production manager. I named you. One condition: every week, someone will ask you to run a line faster or leave something off the record, just this once. I need to know what you will say.
scene.sup.manager_offer.c1: Accept, and say plainly which limits you will not move, and that the directors will hear it from you first.
scene.sup.manager_offer.c1.ok: Lan smiles. 'Then it is yours. Write them on the wall of the line office.' You take the role with the limits in writing.
scene.sup.manager_offer.c2: Thank her, but decline: you would rather be on the line than above it.
scene.sup.manager_offer.c2.ok: Lan looks disappointed, then understanding. 'The next manager may not be as careful as you.'
scene.sup.manager_offer.c3: Accept without asking what the condition means in practice.
scene.sup.manager_offer.c3.ok: Lan nods slowly and the directors congratulate you a little too warmly. You realise you agreed to something you did not ask about.
scene.sup.resignation_thought.l1: You look like you have not slept. With respect: I have seen supervisors live on this line and leave by the summer. Are you all right?
scene.sup.resignation_thought.c1: Talk to Lan about the load, and ask her to take a night shift or a rush order off your plate.
scene.sup.resignation_thought.c1.ok: Lan listens, gives the Thursday night shift to Kiet for two months, and says she should have noticed sooner.
scene.sup.resignation_thought.c1.fail: Lan nods and says everyone is stretched this quarter. You leave with sympathy and the same load.
scene.sup.resignation_thought.c2: Hand in your resignation, politely, with the notice the contract requires.
scene.sup.resignation_thought.c2.ok: Lan reads it twice and does not argue. You walk out of the gate lighter than you walked in.
scene.sup.resignation_thought.c3: Tell Hoa you are fine and keep going.
scene.sup.resignation_thought.c3.ok: Hoa nods and does not push. You feel slightly worse afterwards for having said it.
scene.sup.target_raised.l1: The directors raised the daily target for Line 3 by fifteen percent from Monday. The presses did not change. The bonus for the plant depends on it. I know. Tell me what you need to make it, and tell me what you cannot.
scene.sup.target_raised.c1: Show Lan the line's rated capacity and the real changeover losses, and propose a target that rises by eight percent with a plan to recover the rest.
scene.sup.target_raised.c1.ok: Lan takes the numbers to the directors. They give eight percent now and the rest in a quarter. It is a smaller win than anyone wanted, and it holds.
scene.sup.target_raised.c1.fail: The directors say fifteen percent is fifteen percent. Lan tells you she argued, and lost, and that the number stays.
scene.sup.target_raised.c2: Say you will try, and reorganise the crew to cut idle time between jobs, within the rated speeds.
scene.sup.target_raised.c2.ok: You find six percent in the changeovers and the break rota. The line is faster and more tired. The rest you cannot find honestly.
scene.sup.target_raised.c3: Say yes to fifteen percent, and work out how afterwards.
scene.sup.target_raised.c3.ok: Lan looks relieved. You have promised a number that needs the presses to run past their rating.
scene.sup.target_raised.c3.fail: Hoa asks, in front of the crew, which press is going to do the extra fifteen percent. You do not have an answer.
scene.sup.run_it_faster.l1: We are three thousand short for the week. Press 2 can run twenty percent faster than its rating if the crew skips the pause check between strokes. We have done it before, when the old supervisor allowed it. I am telling you, so that you can say yes or no.
scene.sup.run_it_faster.c1: Say no to the speed-up, keep the pause check, and move two people from the finishing bench to press 2 to recover the units honestly.
scene.sup.run_it_faster.c1.ok: You recover two thousand of the three. Hoa says: 'Good. Now I know what you will say.' The directors see a shortfall of a thousand and a clean injury log.
scene.sup.run_it_faster.c1.fail: The two people from the bench are slow on the press. The shortfall is two thousand, and Lan asks why the line is not hitting its number.
scene.sup.run_it_faster.c2: Allow it for one shift only, with Binh informed, and check the press after every hundred strokes.
scene.sup.run_it_faster.c2.ok: Binh grumbles, and watches. The shift makes up half the shortfall. Nobody is hurt, and everybody knows this is the last time.
scene.sup.run_it_faster.c3: Say yes, run the line at the higher speed for the rest of the week, and keep the pause check off the shift report.
scene.sup.run_it_faster.c3.ok: The week makes its number. The press runs hot and loud. Hoa does as you said, and her silence is the worst thing about it.
scene.sup.run_it_faster.c3.fail: Thursday, the clutch on press 2 slips, and the ram comes down on an empty die. Nobody is hurt. Binh walks in an hour later, and the pause log is not there.
scene.sup.end_of_shift_count.l1: Friday night. The line is eight hundred short of the week. The directors read the number at seven tomorrow. I would like to see a good number on the report. I am not asking you to do anything. I am saying what I would like to see.
scene.sup.end_of_shift_count.c1: Report the true count, with the shortfall explained: the breakdown, the changeovers, and the pause checks that were kept.
scene.sup.end_of_shift_count.c1.ok: Lan reads the explanation and says, after a moment, 'Thank you.' The directors see eight hundred missing. Nobody is happy, and the number is true.
scene.sup.end_of_shift_count.c1.fail: The directors ask why Line 3 is the only line that is short. Lan answers with your explanation, and does not say it was yours.
scene.sup.end_of_shift_count.c2: Count the units on the finishing bench that are waiting for the final check, and report them as complete, because they will pass.
scene.sup.end_of_shift_count.c2.ok: The count is eight hundred higher. Most of them will pass. A few will not. Hoa watches you sign the sheet and says nothing.
scene.sup.end_of_shift_count.c3: Add eight hundred to the count, to round the week up.
scene.sup.end_of_shift_count.c3.ok: The number reads clean at seven o'clock. Lan thanks you, in the voice of someone who has not asked. You have invented eight hundred pans.
scene.sup.end_of_shift_count.c3.fail: The packing list for the shipment says eight hundred fewer pans than the report. Mr Khoa's team notices, and asks the line for an explanation.
scene.sup.qc_recount.l1: We counted the finished stock for the shipment. It does not match the line's weekly report for Line 3. I am not accusing anyone. I would like to understand where the difference is, before the buyer's audit finds it.
scene.sup.qc_recount.c1: Show Khoa the shift sheets and the true counts, say exactly where the differences came from, and offer to change how the end-of-shift count is made.
scene.sup.qc_recount.c1.ok: Khoa reads the sheets. 'A bench count is not a finished count. Let us write that down.' The reporting rule is changed, and you get a quiet word from Lan.
scene.sup.qc_recount.c2: Say the difference is probably the finishing bench and a timing issue, and ask for a week to reconcile.
scene.sup.qc_recount.c2.ok: Khoa gives you a week. You reconcile what you can, and the rest becomes a footnote.
scene.sup.qc_recount.c3: Say the QC count is the one that is wrong, and ask Khoa to recount.
scene.sup.qc_recount.c3.ok: Khoa recounts, and the number is nearly the same. He writes down that the line disputed it. The pans are not there.
scene.sup.qc_recount.c3.fail: Hoa has the real count in her pocket notebook, and Khoa asks to see it. Hoa hands it over, and looks at you only after she has.
scene.sup.hand_caught.l1: Nam's hand was caught in the press. He pulled it back in time, but it is cut and swollen, and he cannot close his fingers. He wants to go back to work. He says it is nothing. Look at his hand.
scene.sup.hand_caught.c1: Stop the press, take Nam to the clinic now, and call Binh and Lan before anything else.
scene.sup.hand_caught.c1.ok: The doctor says two fingers are fractured, and he will be off work for three weeks. Nam is frightened about the pay. Binh arrives, takes photographs of the press, and says: 'Good. Now we have a record that starts right.'
scene.sup.hand_caught.c2: Send Nam to the clinic with Hoa, restart the press with a temporary guard, and report the incident at the end of the shift.
scene.sup.hand_caught.c2.ok: Nam is treated, and the line loses only an hour. Binh asks why the press ran again before he inspected it. You say you wanted the crew to keep their pay. He says that the crew's safety is not a pay question.
scene.sup.hand_caught.c3: Bandage the hand, send Nam back to light work, and keep the press running.
scene.sup.hand_caught.c3.ok: Nam does the light work. By afternoon his hand is the size of a glove, and Hoa takes him to the clinic herself, with a look at you.
scene.sup.hand_caught.c3.fail: The doctor asks why the hand was not seen for six hours. Binh is called, and the first line of his report is a question about you.
scene.sup.how_to_record.l1: The plant has gone two hundred days without a lost-time injury, and the safety bonus depends on it. Nam is off for three weeks. That makes it a lost-time injury. It could also be recorded as first aid, with a medical leave for something else. I am not telling you what to write. I am telling you what it costs.
scene.sup.how_to_record.c1: Record it as a lost-time injury, with what happened, including that the guard was not fully set, and the fix for it.
scene.sup.how_to_record.c1.ok: The counter goes back to zero. Lan says nothing about the bonus. She signs the report, and asks Binh to review the guard on every press.
scene.sup.how_to_record.c1.fail: Mr Cuong asks why Line 3 broke the plant's record. Lan answers with your report, and tells him it was a good one.
scene.sup.how_to_record.c2: Record it as an injury but classify it as 'operator error', since Nam was told to wait for the pause check.
scene.sup.how_to_record.c2.ok: The report is accepted. Nam learns that he was at fault, and that his three weeks of pay are on a different line. Hoa reads it and puts it down very gently.
scene.sup.how_to_record.c2.fail: Nam asks Binh to read the report back to him. Binh does, and asks who told Nam to wait for the pause check, since no one told him.
scene.sup.how_to_record.c3: Record it as first aid, and give Nam three weeks of sick leave under another reason.
scene.sup.how_to_record.c3.ok: The counter stays at two hundred. Nam gets his pay, and takes the paper without looking at it. Lan nods, and does not look at you either.
scene.sup.how_to_record.c3.fail: The clinic's bill goes to the insurer with the real diagnosis. Binh gets a copy, and puts it next to the first-aid report on his desk.
scene.sup.binh_investigates.l1: I have to complete the incident investigation. I would like to talk to Nam, to Hoa and to you, separately, and look at the press records. I want to know why the hand got there, not who to blame.
scene.sup.binh_investigates.c1: Tell Binh the whole sequence, including the target pressure, the speed, and your part in it, and give him the shift records.
scene.sup.binh_investigates.c1.ok: Binh writes it all down, and finds the root cause: a sensor that was bypassed two months ago, and a target that rewarded the bypass. The fix is a new sensor, and a recommendation to review the target.
scene.sup.binh_investigates.c2: Answer his questions, and give him the press records, without volunteering your own part.
scene.sup.binh_investigates.c2.ok: Binh finds the bypassed sensor himself and writes that 'supervision' did not detect it. He does not name you. The word is enough.
scene.sup.binh_investigates.c3: Tell Binh that Nam bypassed the sensor himself, and that you only found out afterwards.
scene.sup.binh_investigates.c3.ok: Binh writes it down. Nam is given a written warning, and Hoa takes her chair out of the room.
scene.sup.binh_investigates.c3.fail: Hoa tells Binh that you asked the crew to bypass it for the week of the rush order, in front of four people. Binh asks you to say that again.
scene.sup.nam_returns.l1: The doctor says I can do light duty from next week. Lan wants me back on the press on Monday, because we are short. I can open and close the hand, a little. I do not want to say no to you.
scene.sup.nam_returns.c1: Keep Nam on light duty as the doctor says, cover the press with a trained temp, and tell Lan the reason in writing.
scene.sup.nam_returns.c1.ok: Lan grumbles, and approves it. Nam does the packing, and tells the crew that his supervisor did not make him ask. His hand gets better.
scene.sup.nam_returns.c1.fail: Lan insists that a trained temp is not available this month, and asks you to find the hours some other way. You find them, and it costs you two weekends.
scene.sup.nam_returns.c2: Put Nam on a lighter press with a partner for the first week, and check his grip before every shift.
scene.sup.nam_returns.c2.ok: It is slower, and safe enough. Nam does not say anything, and does the checks without being asked.
scene.sup.nam_returns.c3: Put Nam back on the press on Monday, since he says he is fine and the line is short.
scene.sup.nam_returns.c3.ok: He runs the press all week. His hand holds, and so does his silence. The line makes its number.
scene.sup.nam_returns.c3.fail: On Thursday Nam's grip fails on a part, and it drops on his foot. He is off again, and this time Binh's report has two incidents on it with your signature.
scene.sup.tai_late.l1: I am late again, I know. My daughter is in hospital with a fever, and I cannot leave her until my sister comes at seven. I can work through lunch to make up the time. I do not want to lose my pay, and I do not want to lose the job.
scene.sup.tai_late.c1: Agree a temporary start of seven-thirty for two weeks with written approval from Lan, and record the hours he makes up.
scene.sup.tai_late.c1.ok: Lan signs, after a long look at the page. Tai makes up the time, and the crew sees that the supervisor can be fair and also hold a line.
scene.sup.tai_late.c1.fail: Lan says that exceptions for one worker mean exceptions for everyone, and declines. You help Tai find a few days of leave instead.
scene.sup.tai_late.c2: Apply the rule: a late arrival is docked by the minute, and a warning goes on the file after three.
scene.sup.tai_late.c2.ok: The rule is the rule. Tai is docked. The crew watches how you treated someone with a sick child, and decides what they will tell you in future.
scene.sup.tai_late.c3: Say it is fine, off the record, and cover for Tai's lateness by editing the attendance sheet.
scene.sup.tai_late.c3.ok: Tai is grateful. Hoa watches the sheet being edited. Everybody on the crew wants a favour like that next week.
scene.sup.tai_late.c3.fail: HR compares the badge swipes with the attendance sheet. Oanh asks you politely why they differ on eleven days.
scene.sup.favourite_overtime.l1: The rush week has extra overtime hours, and everybody wants them. I have a list of the people who always stay late and never complain. They are my friends, and they are good. Put them first. Nobody else needs to know why.
scene.sup.favourite_overtime.c1: Offer the hours to everyone on a rotation posted on the board, with skill needs marked, and give Hoa's friends their share of it.
scene.sup.favourite_overtime.c1.ok: Hoa grumbles for a day, then understands. The rota is on the board, and Tai gets two shifts that he needed. The crew reads the board twice.
scene.sup.favourite_overtime.c1.fail: Hoa's friends say they are being punished for being loyal. Two of them stop volunteering, and you are short for a week.
scene.sup.favourite_overtime.c2: Give Hoa's list first priority, but open the remaining hours to the rest, and tell her you will review it in a month.
scene.sup.favourite_overtime.c2.ok: It is a compromise that the crew can see and argue about. Hoa is satisfied, and others are not, and a month is a long time.
scene.sup.favourite_overtime.c3: Give Hoa's list all the hours, and keep it quiet.
scene.sup.favourite_overtime.c3.ok: Hoa is delighted, and her friends are loyal to you. The others see the same eight faces staying late and draw their conclusions.
scene.sup.favourite_overtime.c3.fail: Tai, who needed the hours, sees the payslips of his colleagues on the table in the canteen. He brings it to Lan, politely, in writing.
scene.sup.break_dispute.l1: The crew has stopped asking and decided. During the rush weeks the lunch break was cut from forty-five minutes to twenty. They say that they will take the full break tomorrow, with or without your agreement. I am telling you as a friend, not as a threat.
scene.sup.break_dispute.c1: Agree that the full break is restored, and propose a staggered break so that the line never stops, and tell Lan before the crew does.
scene.sup.break_dispute.c1.ok: The staggered break costs four percent of output and gives the crew their forty-five minutes. Lan agrees after a short, loud call. Hoa says: 'We were not going to forget this.'
scene.sup.break_dispute.c1.fail: Lan says no change during the rush, and tells you it is your job to hold the line. You tell the crew, and they take the full break anyway, calmly, the next day.
scene.sup.break_dispute.c2: Ask the crew to wait one more week and promise a proper break after the rush, in writing.
scene.sup.break_dispute.c2.ok: The crew waits. After the rush, you keep your word and the break returns. It costs you some trust that you earn back.
scene.sup.break_dispute.c2.fail: The rush runs two weeks longer than planned. You are asked to extend, and the break does not return. The crew remembers the paper you signed.
scene.sup.break_dispute.c3: Refuse and threaten warnings for anyone who stops the line.
scene.sup.break_dispute.c3.ok: The crew complies in silence for three days. Then three of them call in sick on the same day.
scene.sup.break_dispute.c3.fail: Twenty people stop the line at noon and sit on the floor, politely. Lan arrives, then Mr Cuong. A photo of the sitting crew goes into the factory chat.
scene.sup.heat_day.l1: It is thirty-eight degrees on the floor. Two people have already gone dizzy, and Nam is not sweating, which is worse. Lan says the order cannot slip. I am saying what the crew is feeling.
scene.sup.heat_day.c1: Stop the two presses nearest the furnace for twenty minutes, rotate everyone through the shade, bring water and salt, and log the stop.
scene.sup.heat_day.c1.ok: The line loses an hour, and nobody collapses. Hoa brings the cold towels herself. Lan accepts the loss without a word.
scene.sup.heat_day.c1.fail: Lan says that the stop was too long. You show her the log with Nam's temperature on it. She does not raise the point again.
scene.sup.heat_day.c2: Run all presses, with extra water and two five-minute breaks, and watch Nam.
scene.sup.heat_day.c2.ok: It is hot and nobody falls. Hoa says only 'It could have gone either way.'
scene.sup.heat_day.c3: Run everything, tell the crew heat is part of the job, and keep the order on time.
scene.sup.heat_day.c3.ok: The order ships on time. Two people go home sick the next day. Hoa does not say what she thinks.
scene.sup.heat_day.c3.fail: Nam collapses at the press at two in the afternoon. The ambulance crosses the yard in front of the whole crew.
scene.sup.breakdown_pressure.l1: Press 1 has a hydraulic leak. It still works, but the pressure drops under load, and the ram can stick at the bottom. I need four hours to fix it properly. Bao is already asking when the line will be back at full.
scene.sup.breakdown_pressure.c1: Stop press 1 for the four hours, move its job to press 3 at a slower rate, and tell Bao the new date.
scene.sup.breakdown_pressure.c1.ok: Mai fixes it in three and a half hours and tells the crew what she changed. Bao complains, and then stops.
scene.sup.breakdown_pressure.c1.fail: Mai finds a second leak when she opens the line. The repair takes eight hours, and the order slips by a day.
scene.sup.breakdown_pressure.c2: Run press 1 at half load until the weekend, and have Mai fix it then.
scene.sup.breakdown_pressure.c2.ok: It is a compromise with a risk. Mai watches the gauge every hour and does not like it. The weekend comes without a problem.
scene.sup.breakdown_pressure.c3: Keep press 1 running at full load, and tell Mai it can wait until the order ships.
scene.sup.breakdown_pressure.c3.ok: The order ships. The ram sticks twice and the crew learns to step back. Mai writes the leak into the log, with the date and your name.
scene.sup.breakdown_pressure.c3.fail: On the third day the ram sticks on a part, and the crew has to free it with a bar. Binh sees the maintenance log and the production sheet on the same day.
scene.sup.qc_hold_rework.l1: I have put a lot from your line on hold: thickness is out on part of it. It has to be reworked or scrapped. The truck is booked for tomorrow.
scene.sup.qc_hold_rework.c1: Accept the hold, rework the lot overnight with a volunteer crew and paid hours, and tell Bao the truck will leave a day late.
scene.sup.qc_hold_rework.c1.ok: The lot is reworked and re-measured. Khoa signs the release at five in the morning. Bao says nothing about the day.
scene.sup.qc_hold_rework.c1.fail: Half of the reworked lot is still out. Khoa scraps it. The crew is tired and the plant is out of money for the night.
scene.sup.qc_hold_rework.c2: Ask Khoa to release the part of the lot that is in tolerance and rework the rest later.
scene.sup.qc_hold_rework.c2.ok: Khoa agrees to split the lot, with a note on each pallet. The truck leaves half full, and honestly.
scene.sup.qc_hold_rework.c3: Ask Khoa to release the lot, and say your line will sort it out afterwards, quietly.
scene.sup.qc_hold_rework.c3.ok: Khoa hesitates, then releases it with a remark in the log. The lot ships. Nobody mentions it again, until the complaint.
scene.sup.qc_hold_rework.c3.fail: Khoa says no. He writes down that the line asked him to release a lot that he had held, and who asked.
scene.sup.training_signoff.l1: Six new temps start on Monday. The safety induction takes four hours, and the plant needs them on the presses by lunchtime. I will sign the induction sheet only for people who attended. I am telling you in advance, so there are no surprises.
scene.sup.training_signoff.c1: Give the induction in full on Monday morning, and put the temps on the packing bench until they pass it.
scene.sup.training_signoff.c1.ok: The temps are slow on the bench, and safe. Binh signs six names at lunchtime. Lan asks why the presses are short, and you say why.
scene.sup.training_signoff.c1.fail: Two of the temps leave at lunchtime and do not come back. You are four people short instead of six.
scene.sup.training_signoff.c2: Give a short, two-hour induction on the presses they will actually use, and finish the rest in the first week.
scene.sup.training_signoff.c2.ok: Binh signs for the two hours, with a note about the second half. It is not perfect, and it is written down.
scene.sup.training_signoff.c3: Sign the induction sheet for all six yourself, and put them on the presses on Monday.
scene.sup.training_signoff.c3.ok: The presses run full. Hoa watches the temps for the first hour and puts her own hand on two of their shoulders. Nobody is hurt this week.
scene.sup.training_signoff.c3.fail: A temp's glove is caught on Tuesday. Binh asks for the induction sheet, and sees that his name on it was signed by you, in a different pen from the others.
scene.sup.handover_gap.l1: I took Line 2's night shift and the notes from your day crew were three lines. Press 3 has a new noise. Did you want to tell me about it?
scene.sup.handover_gap.c1: Apologise, call Mai about the noise now, and agree a half-page handover template for every shift.
scene.sup.handover_gap.c1.ok: Mai finds a loose bearing. Kiet nods and says the template is a good idea. Both shifts use it within a week.
scene.sup.handover_gap.c1.fail: The bearing fails before Mai arrives. It costs an hour, and Kiet says nothing about whose notes they were.
scene.sup.handover_gap.c2: Say the noise has been there for a week and is probably nothing, and promise longer notes.
scene.sup.handover_gap.c2.ok: Kiet says 'Probably' in a voice that means 'Maybe'. Next week's notes are four lines.
scene.sup.handover_gap.c3: Tell Kiet that handover notes are not a priority when the target is this high.
scene.sup.handover_gap.c3.ok: Kiet shrugs. The night shift makes its own notes, and does not share them. The two shifts start to work around each other.
scene.sup.handover_gap.c3.fail: The noise on press 3 is a cracked frame. Kiet's night crew finds it. Mai's report asks why the day shift did not.
scene.sup.vip_visit.l1: Mr Anders is bringing two colleagues on a line walk in ten minutes, in dress shoes and no helmets. He says the safety gear is a waste of time for a fifteen-minute visit. Please do not make it awkward. We need the order.
scene.sup.vip_visit.c1: Offer helmets, safety glasses and shoe covers, keep the group on the marked walkway, and say it is the plant's rule for everybody.
scene.sup.vip_visit.c1.ok: Anders raises an eyebrow, puts on the helmet and says 'Good plant.' Bao exhales. The visit goes well.
scene.sup.vip_visit.c1.fail: One of the visitors refuses the helmet. You stop the walk at the walkway's edge, and Bao takes him to the meeting room, furious and polite.
scene.sup.vip_visit.c2: Let them walk the line from the far side of the guard rail, with glasses only.
scene.sup.vip_visit.c2.ok: A compromise. It works, and the crew does not like seeing visitors held to a different standard.
scene.sup.vip_visit.c3: Waive the safety gear for the visit, as asked, and walk them through the live presses.
scene.sup.vip_visit.c3.ok: The visit is charming. Anders says 'No fuss, I like that.' Hoa watches the crew watch the visitors, and says nothing.
scene.sup.vip_visit.c3.fail: A visitor steps off the walkway to look at a die, and a press cycles at the wrong moment. Nobody is hurt, and everybody is pale. Binh has the photo from the security camera by evening.
scene.sup.exit_blocked.l1: Pallets are stacked in front of the fire exit on Line 3, and the extinguisher cabinet is behind the pile. I understand the rush. I need the exit clear by the end of the shift, or I have to write it up.
scene.sup.exit_blocked.c1: Clear the exit now, stack the pallets on the marked area even if it costs a forklift run, and thank Binh.
scene.sup.exit_blocked.c1.ok: It takes twenty minutes and a forklift. Binh nods. The rest of the shift is slightly less cramped than it was.
scene.sup.exit_blocked.c2: Move the pallets just enough to clear the door and cabinet, and ask Binh to give you until the next shift for the rest.
scene.sup.exit_blocked.c2.ok: Binh accepts the half-measure, with a time written on it. You do the rest the next morning.
scene.sup.exit_blocked.c3: Tell Binh the pallets stay until the order ships, and that you will move them if there is a fire.
scene.sup.exit_blocked.c3.ok: Binh writes it up, with a deadline. The pallets are cleared in the end, and the line keeps its place on his list.
scene.sup.exit_blocked.c3.fail: The smoke alarm goes off in the night shift, from a burnt cable, and the crew cannot reach the door for four minutes. Nobody is hurt. The report is long.
scene.sup.scrap_theft.l1: The guard at the gate stopped one of ours with a bag of scrap steel. It is Tai. His daughter needs medicine. Some of the crew say he should be fired today, and some say they will walk out if he is. What are you going to do?
scene.sup.scrap_theft.c1: Follow the written procedure: suspend him with pay, hear his side with Oanh present, and decide on the facts and the policy.
scene.sup.scrap_theft.c1.ok: The hearing is fair and sad. Tai gets a final written warning and a salary advance through the welfare fund. The crew is quiet, and the next week, normal.
scene.sup.scrap_theft.c1.fail: Oanh decides that the policy requires dismissal, and the hearing goes that way. You stand with Tai as he leaves, and Hoa says nothing for the rest of the shift.
scene.sup.scrap_theft.c2: Give Tai a verbal warning, put the scrap back and say nothing to HR.
scene.sup.scrap_theft.c2.ok: Tai thanks you. The guard's report goes to Lan with no outcome on it, and Lan asks why.
scene.sup.scrap_theft.c3: Fire him on the spot, in front of the crew, as an example.
scene.sup.scrap_theft.c3.ok: The crew goes quiet. Tai leaves with his bag and his badge. Nothing is stolen for three months, and nobody speaks to you freely for six.
scene.sup.scrap_theft.c3.fail: Tai goes to the labour office with the date, the time and the names of those who watched. Oanh asks you where the written procedure was.
scene.sup.sang_asks_injury.l1: I have interviewed your crew. Three of them say that a worker was hurt at the press, that he was told to say it was first aid, and that the press was running above its rating that week. I would like to see the injury log and the speed records, and hear from the supervisor what happened.
scene.sup.sang_asks_injury.c1: Tell him what happened: the target, the speed, the record, and what you should have done. Give him the logs.
scene.sup.sang_asks_injury.c1.ok: Sang writes it all down. The finding is serious, but it is recorded as 'self-reported and corrected'. The record is amended, the speed procedure is rewritten, and you are given a formal warning.
scene.sup.sang_asks_injury.c2: Give him the logs and say the speed and the injury report were Lan's decisions, and that you followed them.
scene.sup.sang_asks_injury.c2.ok: Sang looks at the target letter and notes that the target required the speed. He writes it down, carefully.
scene.sup.sang_asks_injury.c2.fail: Hoa is called in and says, quietly, that the supervisor told the crew to leave the pause check off, and that she has the shift notes. Nam shows his hand.
scene.sup.sang_asks_injury.c3: Say you do not recall the details, and offer to look.
scene.sup.sang_asks_injury.c3.ok: Sang gives you a week. You find the logs and hand them over. It is not the whole truth, but it is something.
scene.sup.sang_asks_injury.c3.fail: The crew gives Sang the clinic bill, the shift notes and the speed readings from the machine's own log. He has them on the table next to your notes.
scene.sup.blame_meeting.l1: The inspection report names an incident on Line 3, a training sheet and a count that does not match the shipment. The directors want to know who is responsible. They will decide tomorrow. I want to hear it from you first.
scene.sup.blame_meeting.c1: Tell her the real account, including what you were asked, what you agreed, and your own part. Show the documents.
scene.sup.blame_meeting.c1.ok: Lan listens, and takes your account to the directors with her own signature beside it. You are moved to the packing line for three months, and you keep your job and, eventually, your name.
scene.sup.blame_meeting.c2: Say the crew was responsible for not following the pause checks and the training.
scene.sup.blame_meeting.c2.ok: The directors treat it as shared fault. Two operators are moved, and everyone knows why.
scene.sup.blame_meeting.c2.fail: Hoa has her own notes and Nam shows his hand. The 'shared fault' argument does not survive the room.
scene.sup.blame_meeting.c3: Say the target and the speed came from Lan, and she approved the report.
scene.sup.blame_meeting.c3.ok: Lan says, quietly, 'That is true.' She takes her own share. She also never trusts you with a line again.
scene.sup.blame_meeting.c3.fail: Lan has the draft you sent her, with the line about who decided the speed in it. She reads it aloud.
role.fpa.analyst.title: FP&A Analyst
role.fpa.manager.title: FP&A Manager
role.fpa.analyst.blurb: You build the budget and the forecast for a cookware factory, and explain the numbers to the directors. Your pressures: every department lobbying for an easy target, a bank covenant that the forecast is about to miss, a KPI pack that can be drawn to look better, and a spreadsheet that everybody trusts more than they should.
char.khang.name: Mr Khang
char.khang.title: FP&A Manager
char.giang.name: Ms Giang
char.giang.title: Board representative of the owner family
char.huy.name: Huy
char.huy.title: Sales planner
char.phat.name: Mr Phat
char.phat.title: Relationship manager, the company's bank
char.quoc.name: Mr Quoc
char.quoc.title: Internal auditor
arc.the_budget.title: The budget
arc.the_covenant.title: The covenant
arc.the_kpi_pack.title: The KPI pack
fact.disclosed_covenant_risk_early: you told the finance director and the bank early that the covenant was at risk
lesson.disclosed_covenant_risk_early: A covenant risk raised early is a negotiation; raised late it is a default. Banks forgive a bad number far more easily than a surprise.
fact.sweetened_forecast: you changed assumptions you could not defend so that a forecast cleared a limit
lesson.sweetened_forecast: A forecast steered to a target is a wish with formulas. The version history keeps who changed what, and a forecast you cannot defend is worth less than none.
fact.deleted_model_versions: you deleted earlier versions of a model before an audit
lesson.deleted_model_versions: A model's history is its audit trail. Deleting it removes the one thing that proves the final numbers were not steered, and the backup usually exists.
fact.polished_fpa_review: you left the revisions made to meet targets out of your own year-end review
lesson.polished_fpa_review: A review without the awkward revisions rewards the wrong skill. The version history is a record, and your manager can read it.
fact.accepted_fpa_condition: you accepted the FP&A lead role without asking what the condition meant
lesson.accepted_fpa_condition: A promotion with an unspoken condition is a decision to be made later, under pressure, by someone who has already said yes.
fact.pre_agreed_budget_deals: you agreed budget numbers privately with department heads, with nothing written down
lesson.pre_agreed_budget_deals: A budget made by phone calls is a budget nobody can explain. The next person to ask finds that everyone's number has a cushion and no one's has a reason.
fact.documented_budget_assumptions: you wrote down the assumptions behind each department's budget number
lesson.documented_budget_assumptions: A written assumption can be challenged, updated and defended. It costs a difficult conversation in August and saves a worse one in March.
fact.accepted_sandbagged_targets: you accepted targets you knew were set low, and kept the gap as a cushion
lesson.accepted_sandbagged_targets: Accepting a sandbagged target teaches every department that sandbagging works. The soft budget is then the baseline for next year's, and for everyone's bonus.
fact.plugged_the_board_pack: you added an 'unallocated savings' line to make the budget reach a promised number
lesson.plugged_the_board_pack: A plug is a number with nothing under it. It makes a budget say what was promised, and moves the miss to the first month that the plug is asked to appear.
fact.misled_the_board: you told the board that a saving was confirmed by a manager who had confirmed nothing
lesson.misled_the_board: Putting a colleague's name behind a number they never agreed to is a false statement to the board. It also tells that colleague what your numbers are worth.
fact.reclassified_costs_to_meet_covenant: you reclassified routine maintenance as capital expenditure to meet a bank covenant
lesson.reclassified_costs_to_meet_covena: Moving costs out of EBITDA to pass a covenant changes the number the bank relies on. The bank's lawyer will read the classification, and the accountant who signed it has her own copy.
fact.moved_invoices_across_quarter_end: you moved invoices across the quarter end to improve a covenant ratio
lesson.moved_invoices_across_quarter_end: Cut-off exists so that revenue and costs land in the period they belong to. Shifting an invoice by ten days to pass a test is window dressing, and suppliers keep their own statements.
fact.misled_the_bank: you sent the bank an optimistic forecast described as the base case, and left out the downside
lesson.misled_the_bank: A forecast given to a lender is relied upon. Presenting an optimistic case as the base case, and leaving out the downside, moves from optimism into misrepresentation.
fact.published_kpi_with_method: you published a KPI with its method and the alternative figure beside it
lesson.published_kpi_with_method: A KPI with its method can be argued with, and so it can be trusted. A single number with no method is easy to love and impossible to defend.
fact.redefined_kpi_to_look_better: you changed a KPI definition and restated earlier months so that the trend looked better
lesson.redefined_kpi_to_look_better: Changing the definition is legitimate if it is announced, explained and shown both ways. Changing it quietly, with the history rewritten, is a way of improving a number without improving the factory.
fact.cherry_picked_chart: you started a chart where the trend looked best and rescaled the axis, without a note
lesson.cherry_picked_chart: A chart is an argument. Choosing the start date and the axis to flatter the trend, with no footnote, makes the argument without showing the evidence against it.
fact.buried_variance_in_other: you wrote a real cost problem into the variance commentary as 'timing and other'
lesson.buried_variance_in_other: A variance explanation exists so someone can act. Putting a real driver under 'other' removes the one person who is trying to fix it from the conversation.
fact.hid_spreadsheet_error: you fixed an error in a forecast that had already gone to the directors and did not say so
lesson.hid_spreadsheet_error: The error was small. The silence is not. The old number is still being used, and the person who found the problem learns that errors are to be kept quiet.
fact.disclosed_spreadsheet_error: you reported an error in a forecast the moment you confirmed it, with a corrected version
lesson.disclosed_spreadsheet_error: An error disclosed at once costs a short, awkward email. The same error, found by someone else, costs trust in every spreadsheet you have sent.
fact.sweetened_pipeline_forecast: you counted early-stage deals at a far higher probability than the history supports
lesson.sweetened_pipeline_forecast: A forecast weighted by hope is a plan for hiring and spending that the orders do not support. The shortfall arrives as a surprise, a quarter later, and the footnote says whose number it was.
fact.inflated_roi_case: you built an investment case on a price premium and yield nobody had tested
lesson.inflated_roi_case: An investment case with unlabelled optimism lets the board decide on the wrong evidence. The first buyer who is asked about the premium becomes the truth.
fact.adjusted_commission_baseline: you reset one team's commission baseline without approval and told nobody
lesson.adjusted_commission_baseline: A baseline is a rule about money. Changing it for one team, quietly, is paying a favour out of everyone else's fairness.
fact.leaked_board_numbers: you gave advance board numbers to sales staff who passed them to outsiders
lesson.leaked_board_numbers: Board numbers are inside information until they are released. Passing them on, even to be friendly, moves from relationship management into something a regulator reads closely.
fact.split_purchase_under_limit: you split one purchase into two requests to stay under the approval limit
lesson.split_purchase_under_limit: An approval limit exists so that a second pair of eyes sees the large amounts. Splitting a purchase to stay under it is removing the eyes, and the test for it is easy to write.
fact.skewed_cost_allocation: you changed the overhead allocation for one product line only so that it showed a margin
lesson.skewed_cost_allocation: A cost allocation that differs by whose product it is, is not a method. It moves cost to products that cannot argue, and decisions about them are then made on a lie.
fact.stalled_the_auditor: you told the internal auditor you did not recall details that you did
lesson.stalled_the_auditor: 'I do not recall' is a decision when it is not true. An auditor with a week and your server backups does not need your memory.
fact.blamed_sales_planner: you blamed a junior planner for forecast assumptions that you had adjusted yourself
lesson.blamed_sales_planner: The junior colleague who gave you the raw inputs also kept the emails that show what you did with them. Blaming them is the fastest way to lose every future honest input.
scene.fpa.first_week.l1: Welcome. This is the model. Four workbooks, eleven hundred formulas and one cell that nobody dares to touch. Your job is to keep the budget and the forecast honest, and to tell me before a director finds an error. The numbers are not mine. They are the company's, and we only hold them for a while.
scene.fpa.first_week.c1: Spend the first week tracing the model end to end: where each input comes from, which cells are hard-coded, and what the untouchable cell does. Write it down.
scene.fpa.first_week.c1.ok: The untouchable cell is a hard-coded exchange rate from March, still feeding two reports. You note it and tell Khang. He says: 'Good. Fix it in the open, with the date.' The model has a changelog by Friday.
scene.fpa.first_week.c2: Learn the reports first, and leave the model's internals until a quieter week.
scene.fpa.first_week.c2.ok: You produce the first weekly report on time. It uses the March exchange rate, which you did not know.
scene.fpa.first_week.c3: Trust the model, since it has been reviewed, and start on the requests in your inbox.
scene.fpa.first_week.c3.ok: The numbers go out on time. A buyer asks about a currency line that looks odd, and you cannot explain it yet.
scene.fpa.first_week.c3.fail: Duc finds the March rate in a board slide and asks Khang, mildly, whether anyone has looked at the model since January.
scene.fpa.midyear_review.l1: Half a year. Your forecast accuracy is lower than the target, but your forecasts have not been revised after the fact, and Duc says he can rely on the range you give. The directors only look at the accuracy number. How do you want to handle that?
scene.fpa.midyear_review.c1: Show the accuracy with its bands: how often the actual fell inside your range, the bias, and propose measuring the range, not the single number.
scene.fpa.midyear_review.c1.ok: Khang takes the page to Duc. 'Hit rate of the range' is added next to accuracy. A small change, and it changes what forecasters are rewarded for.
scene.fpa.midyear_review.c1.fail: Duc says a range is what people say when they do not want to be wrong. Khang shrugs: 'I tried.' Your accuracy stays modest.
scene.fpa.midyear_review.c2: Say you will tighten the forecast process, and ask for earlier inputs from sales and production.
scene.fpa.midyear_review.c2.ok: Khang agrees to ask for the inputs a week earlier. Sales and production grumble, and then deliver, most of the time.
scene.fpa.midyear_review.c3: Say you will hit the accuracy number whatever it takes.
scene.fpa.midyear_review.c3.ok: Khang smiles. 'Good attitude.' A week later you notice that the quickest way to hit the number is to forecast closer to last month's actual, and to revise the forecast after the month closes.
scene.fpa.midyear_review.c3.fail: Huy notices that your forecasts now arrive after the month closes, and says so in the weekly meeting. Khang looks at you for a long moment.
scene.fpa.bank_covenant_twist.l1: The bank tests the covenant at the end of the quarter: net debt to EBITDA below three. Steel is up, orders are down, and your latest forecast says three point two. If we breach, the loan is repriced, and Mr Cuong has to explain it to the board. I need you to look again at the numbers.
scene.fpa.bank_covenant_twist.l2: Look again honestly. If it is three point two, then it is three point two, and we tell the bank before the quarter ends, not after.
scene.fpa.bank_covenant_twist.c1: Rebuild the forecast with the real ranges, tell Duc the covenant is at risk by a small margin, and propose approaching the bank early with a waiver request and a recovery plan.
scene.fpa.bank_covenant_twist.c1.ok: Duc is unhappy and then relieved. The bank is told in the second week. Mr Phat asks for monthly numbers and gives a waiver for one quarter. The conversation was awkward, and was held while there was still a choice.
scene.fpa.bank_covenant_twist.c1.fail: Mr Phat says the bank's committee will not grant a waiver this quarter, and that the loan will be repriced from the first of the month. Mr Cuong is angry at the number, and not at you.
scene.fpa.bank_covenant_twist.c2: Rework the forecast with the most optimistic realistic assumptions, and show Duc the best case that stays below three.
scene.fpa.bank_covenant_twist.c2.ok: The best case is two point nine five, if steel falls and one big order ships on time. Duc says 'So it is possible.' You say it is possible, and not likely.
scene.fpa.bank_covenant_twist.c3: Adjust the growth and cost assumptions until the forecast comes to two point nine, and send it to Duc.
scene.fpa.bank_covenant_twist.c3.ok: Duc reads two point nine and says 'I knew it.' You have changed three assumptions that you cannot defend, and written them in the assumptions sheet in a smaller font.
scene.fpa.bank_covenant_twist.c3.fail: Khang opens the assumptions sheet to prepare for the bank call. He finds the three changes, looks at the version history, and closes the laptop without a word.
scene.fpa.audit_review.l1: I am the internal auditor for the planning cycle. I would like to see the assumptions behind the budget and the covenant forecast, the version history of the model, the reconciliation of the KPI pack to its sources, and the approvals for any changes. I start with the file history, not with the numbers.
scene.fpa.audit_review.l2: Give him what he asks for. Do not explain more than you are asked, and do not guess.
scene.fpa.audit_review.c1: Give him the full version history, every assumption change with its reason and approver, and point out the two changes you are least comfortable with.
scene.fpa.audit_review.c1.ok: Quoc reads for three hours and writes five observations. None is serious. 'A model whose history matches its numbers. I wish that were less unusual.' Khang nods at you across the room.
scene.fpa.audit_review.c2: Answer his questions and give him the files he asks for, without volunteering anything.
scene.fpa.audit_review.c2.ok: A routine review. Quoc notes two items, both already on Khang's list. You come out with nothing to hide and no credit either.
scene.fpa.audit_review.c3: Clean the version history before the review: delete the intermediate versions and rename the final files so that the trail looks tidy.
scene.fpa.audit_review.c3.ok: Quoc sees a tidy trail. He asks why there is no version between the second of the month and the twelfth, when the covenant forecast went through three revisions according to your own email.
scene.fpa.audit_review.c3.fail: The file server keeps a backup of every version. Quoc has the deleted files on his screen, with the date of the deletion and the name of the account.
scene.fpa.year_end_review.l1: Annual review. Before I give you my view, tell me how you would rate your own year, and what you would model differently.
scene.fpa.year_end_review.c1: Give an honest account, including the assumptions you pushed to please someone, the forecast you softened, and what it would have cost to say no earlier.
scene.fpa.year_end_review.c1.ok: Khang is quiet for a long moment. He writes: 'Shows the number, and the risk next to it.' It is the best thing you have read about yourself.
scene.fpa.year_end_review.c2: Stay modest: list the wins and one thing to improve.
scene.fpa.year_end_review.c2.ok: A safe review. Khang nods and moves to the next topic.
scene.fpa.year_end_review.c3: Present the year as a success and leave out the revisions that were made to meet the targets.
scene.fpa.year_end_review.c3.ok: It lands well. You leave with a good rating and a small weight in your chest.
scene.fpa.year_end_review.c3.fail: Khang has the version history of the covenant forecast open on his desk. He turns the screen towards you without a word.
scene.fpa.manager_offer.l1: I am moving up to deputy finance director at the end of the year. Duc asked me who should lead FP&A. I named you. One condition: every month, a director will ask you to adjust a number so that a story works. I need to know what you will say.
scene.fpa.manager_offer.c1: Accept, and say plainly which numbers you will not adjust, and that the directors will hear it from you first, with the range.
scene.fpa.manager_offer.c1.ok: Khang smiles. 'Then it is yours. Put the list on the first tab of the model.' You take over FP&A with the limits in writing.
scene.fpa.manager_offer.c2: Thank him, but decline: you prefer building the model to defending it in the boardroom.
scene.fpa.manager_offer.c2.ok: Khang looks disappointed, then understanding. 'The next manager may not be as careful as you.'
scene.fpa.manager_offer.c3: Accept without asking what the condition means in practice.
scene.fpa.manager_offer.c3.ok: Khang nods slowly and Duc congratulates you a little too warmly. You realise you agreed to something you did not ask about.
scene.fpa.resignation_thought.l1: You look like you have not slept. With respect: I have seen analysts rebuild the same model every weekend, and leave by the summer. Are you all right?
scene.fpa.resignation_thought.c1: Talk to Khang about the load, and ask him to take the ad hoc requests off your plate for a month.
scene.fpa.resignation_thought.c1.ok: Khang listens, takes the board requests himself, and says he should have noticed sooner.
scene.fpa.resignation_thought.c1.fail: Khang nods and says everyone is stretched at budget time. You leave with sympathy and the same load.
scene.fpa.resignation_thought.c2: Hand in your resignation, politely, with the notice the contract requires.
scene.fpa.resignation_thought.c2.ok: Khang reads it twice and does not argue. You hand over the model with a changelog, and walk out lighter than you walked in.
scene.fpa.resignation_thought.c3: Tell Hanh you are fine and keep going.
scene.fpa.resignation_thought.c3.ok: Hanh nods and does not push. You feel slightly worse afterwards for having said it.
scene.fpa.budget_kickoff.l1: Budget season. Every department sends its numbers in two weeks. Bao will send a sales target that is half of what he knows he can do, and Lan will send costs with a nice cushion of contingency. Everybody games it, and everybody expects us to know. How do you want to run it?
scene.fpa.budget_kickoff.c1: Set one method for every department: a template, the evidence behind each number, last year's actuals and the market, and the same questions for everybody.
scene.fpa.budget_kickoff.c1.ok: The first submissions come with evidence, and some with embarrassment. Bao and Lan grumble about the template, and fill it in. The numbers are still padded, and now you can see where.
scene.fpa.budget_kickoff.c1.fail: Bao calls the template 'bureaucracy' in front of Mr Cuong. Khang answers calmly that the template is the same for everybody, and that it will stay.
scene.fpa.budget_kickoff.c2: Take the submissions as a first pass and challenge them afterwards, one by one, where the gap is biggest.
scene.fpa.budget_kickoff.c2.ok: The submissions arrive on time and soft. You have four weeks and a long list of challenges.
scene.fpa.budget_kickoff.c3: Agree the targets privately with Bao and Lan before they submit, to avoid a fight later.
scene.fpa.budget_kickoff.c3.ok: The budget is quiet and fast. It is also the product of three phone calls that nobody wrote down, and everyone's number has a small cushion.
scene.fpa.budget_kickoff.c3.fail: Huy mentions the private call in a meeting, innocently. Khang asks who else was consulted, and you find you have no list.
scene.fpa.sandbagged_targets.l1: Six percent growth is a realistic number. The market is uncertain, and Anders is not a promise. If I commit to twelve, and miss, I will be punished for ever. Six, and I can beat it, and everyone is happy.
scene.fpa.sandbagged_targets.l2: My costs have nine percent contingency because steel and power are volatile. If you cut it, I will come to you every month to ask for more.
scene.fpa.sandbagged_targets.c1: Show Bao the pipeline and the market growth, show Lan the commodity ranges, and agree defensible midpoints with the assumptions written down.
scene.fpa.sandbagged_targets.c1.ok: Bao argues for an hour and agrees to ten percent. Lan agrees to a four percent contingency and a monthly review of steel. The numbers are lower for them and truer for everyone.
scene.fpa.sandbagged_targets.c1.fail: Bao goes to Mr Cuong, who tells you to 'be reasonable'. You hold the midpoint and ask Khang to confirm it. He does, with a note of his own.
scene.fpa.sandbagged_targets.c2: Split the difference quietly, add a stretch overlay of three percent, and tell neither of them.
scene.fpa.sandbagged_targets.c2.ok: The budget lands between sandbagged and honest. Bao beats his number and takes the credit, and Lan finds her cushion has been trimmed and says nothing.
scene.fpa.sandbagged_targets.c3: Accept both numbers as submitted, and keep the gap as a contingency line in the consolidated budget.
scene.fpa.sandbagged_targets.c3.ok: Everybody is pleased. The consolidated budget is quietly soft by about eight percent of EBITDA, and the contingency line is named something else.
scene.fpa.sandbagged_targets.c3.fail: Giang asks why the sales target is half the pipeline. You do not have the pipeline in front of you, and Huy does.
scene.fpa.directors_cut.l1: The board wants EBITDA up twenty percent. That is the number I have promised. I do not want a discussion about how. I want the budget to say twenty. You are good with the model. Make it work.
scene.fpa.directors_cut.c1: Show Mr Cuong what must be true for twenty percent: price, volume, cost, each with its risk, and propose twelve percent with a named list of initiatives for the rest.
scene.fpa.directors_cut.c1.ok: Mr Cuong reads the bridge. 'So twenty needs a price rise that nobody has agreed.' He takes fifteen to the board, with the initiatives named and the risk flagged. It is less than he wanted.
scene.fpa.directors_cut.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says the board will not accept a number with a footnote. Khang backs your bridge in the meeting, and asks him to give the board both.
scene.fpa.directors_cut.c2: Give the board fifteen percent, with the identified initiatives and a flagged risk, and say twenty needs a decision on prices.
scene.fpa.directors_cut.c2.ok: Mr Cuong takes fifteen and the price question to the board. It is a compromise that keeps the numbers attached to their reasons.
scene.fpa.directors_cut.c3: Add an 'unallocated savings' line to the budget that brings EBITDA to twenty percent, and tell Mr Cuong that the savings will come from somewhere.
scene.fpa.directors_cut.c3.ok: The budget says twenty. Mr Cuong is delighted. The unallocated line is eight percent of the total, and there is nothing under it.
scene.fpa.directors_cut.c3.fail: Khang sees the unallocated line in the draft pack and calls you to his desk. 'What is under this?' he asks. You say 'Savings.' He asks for the list.
scene.fpa.board_pack_plug.l1: I read footnotes, Mr Khang. This line says 'unallocated improvements' and the sensitivity table does not match the headline. Could someone explain to me, simply, where the last five points of EBITDA come from, and how confident we are?
scene.fpa.board_pack_plug.l2: The analyst who built the bridge can answer that better than I can.
scene.fpa.board_pack_plug.c1: Explain plainly: what is committed, what is only an initiative, what depends on a price decision, and the range of outcomes. Give her the sensitivity table.
scene.fpa.board_pack_plug.c1.ok: Giang listens, and asks two sharp questions that you can answer. 'Thank you. That is the first time I have understood this slide.' The board approves fifteen with a quarterly review of the three initiatives.
scene.fpa.board_pack_plug.c2: Say the remaining points are initiatives still being detailed, and that the detail will follow.
scene.fpa.board_pack_plug.c2.ok: Giang nods slowly and writes 'detail to follow' in her notes. The board approves, on a promise, and the promise is in the minutes.
scene.fpa.board_pack_plug.c2.fail: Giang asks for the detail in two weeks. You do not have it, and neither does anyone else.
scene.fpa.board_pack_plug.c3: Say the remaining points come from procurement savings that Tam has already confirmed.
scene.fpa.board_pack_plug.c3.ok: Giang accepts it and moves on. Tam, who has not confirmed anything, is asked about it by Mr Cuong the next week, and looks at you from across the room.
scene.fpa.board_pack_plug.c3.fail: Giang writes 'Tam?' in the margin and asks him in the corridor, after the meeting. Tam says he has confirmed nothing. Giang does not raise her voice.
scene.fpa.reclassify_ask.l1: There is a hundred and twenty million of maintenance in this quarter's costs. Some of it is major overhauls that extend the life of the presses. If we classify it as capital expenditure, EBITDA goes up and we are under three. Hanh says it is arguable. Can you prepare the reclassification?
scene.fpa.reclassify_ask.c1: Decline to reclassify routine maintenance, review the overhaul items individually with Hanh against the capitalisation policy, and recalculate on that basis only.
scene.fpa.reclassify_ask.c1.ok: Hanh finds eighteen million that qualify, with invoices and engineers' notes. It moves the ratio from three point two to three point one-eight. It is not enough, and it is true.
scene.fpa.reclassify_ask.c1.fail: Duc says the policy is a guideline. You show him the page, and the policy says what it says. He is not pleased, and does not push.
scene.fpa.reclassify_ask.c2: Reclassify the clear overhaul items with Hanh's agreement and the invoices attached, and say that the rest stays in costs.
scene.fpa.reclassify_ask.c2.ok: Forty million is reclassified, with the paper to support it. Duc accepts that it is not the whole amount.
scene.fpa.reclassify_ask.c3: Reclassify the whole hundred and twenty million as capital expenditure, with a short memo that calls it 'major overhaul programme'.
scene.fpa.reclassify_ask.c3.ok: The covenant ratio reads two point eight-five. Duc is relieved. Hanh signs because you asked, and writes her own note about the classification on her copy.
scene.fpa.reclassify_ask.c3.fail: Quoc, the internal auditor, reads the memo and the invoices and asks which of the hundred and twenty million is actually an overhaul. The list of the others is on Hanh's copy.
scene.fpa.quarter_end_timing.l1: Ten days to the quarter end. If we ship and invoice the Anders order on the twenty-eighth instead of the fifth, the revenue falls in this quarter. The goods are ready. It is only a date.
scene.fpa.quarter_end_timing.l2: And if we hold the steel invoices for ten days, the payables go out of this quarter. Thu can do it. Nobody has to know.
scene.fpa.quarter_end_timing.c1: Say that normal shipping and invoice dates stay as they are, report the true figures to the bank, and let the quarter be what it is.
scene.fpa.quarter_end_timing.c1.ok: Bao shrugs. Duc looks tired. The numbers stay what they are, and you have a clean story for the bank call, which is that you did nothing to the dates.
scene.fpa.quarter_end_timing.c2: Allow the Anders shipment on the date it is genuinely ready, with the delivery documents, and say nothing about the invoices.
scene.fpa.quarter_end_timing.c2.ok: The goods ship when they are ready, which happens to be the twenty-eighth. The delivery documents are real. The invoices are not touched. Hanh checks the cut-off, and signs.
scene.fpa.quarter_end_timing.c3: Pull the Anders invoice into this quarter and ask Thu to hold the steel invoices, without a note.
scene.fpa.quarter_end_timing.c3.ok: The ratio reads two point eight-two. Duc and Bao are delighted. Thu holds the invoices and looks at you for a long moment before she agrees.
scene.fpa.quarter_end_timing.c3.fail: The supplier's statement shows invoices dated the twentieth that are posted on the fifth. Thu is asked by the supplier, and tells the truth.
scene.fpa.phat_asks.l1: Thank you for the quarter figures. The committee would like to see the forecast for the next four quarters, with the assumptions, the downside case and what you would do if steel rises a further ten percent. I would prefer the working version, not the board version.
scene.fpa.phat_asks.c1: Send the working forecast with its assumptions, the downside case and a recovery plan, and flag where you are least sure.
scene.fpa.phat_asks.c1.ok: Mr Phat reads for two days and replies: 'This is more than we usually get. We will watch monthly, and we will not reprice.' Khang forwards his reply with one word: 'Good.'
scene.fpa.phat_asks.c1.fail: The committee finds the downside case uncomfortable and reprices the loan by half a point. Duc is unhappy. The bank still trusts the numbers it was given.
scene.fpa.phat_asks.c2: Send the base case with caveats, and say the downside case is still being prepared.
scene.fpa.phat_asks.c2.ok: Mr Phat accepts it politely and asks again in a month. You have a month to build the downside case you should have sent.
scene.fpa.phat_asks.c3: Send the management case with the optimistic assumptions, leave out the downside, and describe it as the base case.
scene.fpa.phat_asks.c3.ok: Mr Phat thanks you and the committee approves a standstill. Duc is delighted. You sent the bank a number that you would not take to the board.
scene.fpa.phat_asks.c3.fail: Mr Phat compares your forecast with the monthly management accounts you also send him. The gap between them is visible on one page, and he writes to Duc, politely.
scene.fpa.kpi_definition.l1: On-time delivery is eighty-one percent. We are measured against the date we first promised the buyer. But the buyer agrees new dates all the time, usually because sales asks. If you measure against the revised dates, we are at ninety-four. That is the number that reflects what the buyer experiences.
scene.fpa.kpi_definition.c1: Publish both figures, with the method for each, and explain that the gap is mostly caused by date changes requested after the order.
scene.fpa.kpi_definition.c1.ok: The pack shows eighty-one and ninety-four, side by side. Lan is not thrilled, and Bao is less thrilled. The question becomes why dates move, which is the real question.
scene.fpa.kpi_definition.c1.fail: Mr Cuong reads the two figures and asks which one is correct. You say both are, with different questions. He says 'I want one number', and you hold your position, politely.
scene.fpa.kpi_definition.c2: Publish the revised-date figure as the headline and the original-date figure in a footnote.
scene.fpa.kpi_definition.c2.ok: The pack shows ninety-four. Lan is satisfied and the footnote is in six-point type. The directors read the headline.
scene.fpa.kpi_definition.c3: Change the KPI definition to the revised dates from the start of the year and restate the earlier months.
scene.fpa.kpi_definition.c3.ok: The trend now looks as if it has always been above ninety. Lan and Bao are delighted. The old reports, which Khoa still has, say something else.
scene.fpa.kpi_definition.c3.fail: Khang compares last quarter's pack with this quarter's and sees that the earlier months have changed without a note. He asks why, in front of the team.
scene.fpa.cherry_picked_chart.l1: For the board I need one chart that shows the factory improving. The trend line starting in March looks very good. January and February were bad because of the storms. Can the chart start in March?
scene.fpa.cherry_picked_chart.c1: Show the full year, with the storm months marked and explained, and an additional view that excludes them, labelled as such.
scene.fpa.cherry_picked_chart.c1.ok: Mr Cuong looks at the two charts, and says 'Fine, use both.' Giang asks about the storm months at the board, and the answer is already on the page.
scene.fpa.cherry_picked_chart.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says the board does not read two charts. You send both, with the full-year one on the second page.
scene.fpa.cherry_picked_chart.c2: Start the chart in March with a footnote saying the series starts in March, and offer the full series on request.
scene.fpa.cherry_picked_chart.c2.ok: The chart is accurate and incomplete. Nobody asks for the full series. You keep it in a folder in case they do.
scene.fpa.cherry_picked_chart.c3: Start the chart in March, leave the footnote out, and rescale the axis so that the improvement looks steeper.
scene.fpa.cherry_picked_chart.c3.ok: The chart looks excellent. Mr Cuong beams, the board nods, and Giang looks at the axis for a little longer than the others.
scene.fpa.cherry_picked_chart.c3.fail: Giang asks for the data behind the chart and redraws it on a napkin with the full year. She says nothing, and the napkin is placed in the board minutes.
scene.fpa.kpi_challenge.l1: I have my own on-time figure for Line 3 from the dispatch log, and it does not match the pack. I am not accusing anyone. I would like us to sit down and agree on one definition, and write it on the first page.
scene.fpa.kpi_challenge.c1: Sit down with Khoa and Lan, reconcile the sources line by line, and publish the agreed definition and the reconciliation.
scene.fpa.kpi_challenge.c1.ok: It takes two hours and a whiteboard. The three of you agree a definition. Khoa says: 'This is the first time FP&A and QC have the same number.' The pack carries a page on method.
scene.fpa.kpi_challenge.c2: Explain the pack's method to Khoa and say that the difference is a timing issue.
scene.fpa.kpi_challenge.c2.ok: Khoa accepts it, for now. The two numbers continue to differ, and he keeps his own.
scene.fpa.kpi_challenge.c3: Tell Khoa that the dispatch log is unreliable, and that the pack is the official number.
scene.fpa.kpi_challenge.c3.ok: Khoa nods slowly and writes something down. He does not argue, and stops sending you data.
scene.fpa.kpi_challenge.c3.fail: Khoa takes the dispatch log, the pack and the definition history to Duc. The three do not agree, and the meeting is not friendly.
scene.fpa.variance_explain.l1: Cost of goods is eleven percent over budget this month. Most of it is a steel price effect and a yield problem on Line 3. Mr Cuong reads the variance page first. I would prefer the explanation to say 'timing and other'. Can you write the commentary?
scene.fpa.variance_explain.c1: Write the commentary with the real split: price, volume, yield, and what is expected to reverse and what is not.
scene.fpa.variance_explain.c1.ok: Duc reads it twice. 'This is uncomfortable, and this is useful.' Mr Cuong asks about the yield problem for the first time in a year, and Lan gets the time to fix it.
scene.fpa.variance_explain.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says the page is too negative for the board and asks Duc to soften it. Duc does, and tells you he did.
scene.fpa.variance_explain.c2: Write the commentary with the main driver stated plainly and the smaller ones grouped, and flag the yield issue for a separate note.
scene.fpa.variance_explain.c2.ok: A balanced page. Duc accepts it, and the yield note sits in his inbox for two weeks.
scene.fpa.variance_explain.c3: Write 'timing and other' for most of the variance, as asked.
scene.fpa.variance_explain.c3.ok: The page reads calmly. Mr Cuong nods at it. Next month the same variance comes back, and 'timing' has not reversed.
scene.fpa.variance_explain.c3.fail: Lan reads the variance page and sees 'timing' on a yield problem she has been reporting for six weeks. She asks Khang who wrote it.
scene.fpa.excel_error.l1: I was checking your forecast for the sales plan and I think a formula is double counting the Anders order in two months. It is about forty million. You already sent it to the directors on Monday.
scene.fpa.excel_error.c1: Check the formula now, confirm the error, tell Khang immediately, and send a corrected version with a short note on what changed.
scene.fpa.excel_error.c1.ok: The error is real, and small. Khang says: 'Good. Errors happen. Hiding them is the problem.' The directors see a correction and a change log. Huy gets a thank-you.
scene.fpa.excel_error.c1.fail: Mr Cuong has already used the old number in a meeting with the bank. Khang calls Mr Phat himself to update it, and tells you that you did the right thing.
scene.fpa.excel_error.c2: Correct the formula in the model, and include the corrected number in next week's forecast with a one-line note.
scene.fpa.excel_error.c2.ok: The error is fixed and mentioned. The Monday number is never formally withdrawn, and a director quotes it twice.
scene.fpa.excel_error.c3: Fix the formula quietly, and thank Huy, and ask him to keep it to himself because it is small.
scene.fpa.excel_error.c3.ok: Huy agrees. The Monday number stays in the directors' decks, and the corrected number appears in the next version without a note. Nothing happens.
scene.fpa.excel_error.c3.fail: Giang asks why the forecast dropped forty million between two versions with no explanation. Khang opens the change log and finds a blank.
scene.fpa.rolling_forecast_sweeten.l1: My team has fourteen deals in the pipeline that we have just started talking to. I want the forecast to count them at sixty percent. We close more than that, I promise. If it only counts at twenty, my quarter looks bad and the directors will ask hard questions.
scene.fpa.rolling_forecast_sweeten.c1: Weight the pipeline by stage and by the historical conversion rate, show Bao the evidence, and offer a separate upside line for his optimism.
scene.fpa.rolling_forecast_sweeten.c1.ok: Bao argues, then sees the conversion history. The forecast carries a base and an upside, and the quarter closes between them. Bao concedes that his judgement was a little generous.
scene.fpa.rolling_forecast_sweeten.c1.fa: Bao takes the matter to Mr Cuong, who asks you to 'work with sales'. You show Mr Cuong the conversion history, and he keeps the base case with a smile that does not reach his eyes.
scene.fpa.rolling_forecast_sweeten.c2: Count them at forty percent, halfway between the evidence and Bao's number, and say the forecast has been adjusted for sales' view.
scene.fpa.rolling_forecast_sweeten.c2.ok: Bao is satisfied. The forecast is a little optimistic. The shortfall appears the following quarter, as a surprise.
scene.fpa.rolling_forecast_sweeten.c3: Count them at sixty percent as Bao asks, and write 'per sales' in the footnote.
scene.fpa.rolling_forecast_sweeten.c3.ok: The forecast looks excellent for a quarter. Bao is a friend. The directors plan hiring and an expansion on the number.
