scene.fpa.rolling_forecast_sweeten.c3.fa: The quarter closes at the weighted number. Khang asks why the forecast was sixty percent when the history says twenty-five, and the footnote says 'per sales'.
scene.fpa.roi_pet_project.l1: I want a new coating line. It is a personal conviction. I need an investment case that shows a payback inside three years, so that the board approves it. The volumes are what they are, but you can be a little creative with the price premium and the yield.
scene.fpa.roi_pet_project.c1: Build the case on evidence, show the payback range, and tell Mr Cuong what would have to be true for three years, and what the downside looks like.
scene.fpa.roi_pet_project.c1.ok: The honest payback is four years, and three if the price premium holds. Mr Cuong reads it, grumbles, and takes it to the board anyway with the range. The board approves a smaller first phase.
scene.fpa.roi_pet_project.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says the board will not read a range. He shelves the project for the year, and tells you that you have a talent for finding reasons not to.
scene.fpa.roi_pet_project.c2: Build the case with the optimistic end of the evidence, and mark each assumption as optimistic.
scene.fpa.roi_pet_project.c2.ok: The payback reads two point eight years, and every optimistic assumption has a tag. The board approves it, and the tags are in the appendix.
scene.fpa.roi_pet_project.c3: Build the case with a price premium and yield that give a two-year payback, and do not label them.
scene.fpa.roi_pet_project.c3.ok: The board approves it on the spot. Mr Cuong shakes your hand. The price premium that the case assumes has never been quoted to a buyer.
scene.fpa.roi_pet_project.c3.fail: Giang asks Bao whether any buyer has agreed to the price premium. Bao says no. The question goes back to FP&A with a date.
scene.fpa.commission_baseline.l1: Sales commission is calculated against the baseline you publish for each team. My team's baseline is above what we actually did last year because of the one big order. Could you reset it to the average? It is only a baseline. Nobody will be paid more than they earned.
scene.fpa.commission_baseline.c1: Keep the baseline and propose a rule that normalises one-off orders for everyone, applied the same way to every team.
scene.fpa.commission_baseline.c1.ok: Bao sulks, and accepts. The normalisation rule is approved for next year, and two other managers thank you privately for it.
scene.fpa.commission_baseline.c1.fail: Bao argues that a rule for next year does not help this year's team. He has a point, and nobody has an answer for it.
scene.fpa.commission_baseline.c2: Reset the baseline to the average only if Duc and Khang approve in writing, with the reason.
scene.fpa.commission_baseline.c2.ok: Duc approves, with a note that the reset applies to any team in the same position. The paper trail exists, and so does a precedent.
scene.fpa.commission_baseline.c3: Reset the baseline quietly, and do not mention it to the other teams.
scene.fpa.commission_baseline.c3.ok: Bao's team gets a larger commission. Nobody notices for a quarter. Bao thanks you with lunch.
scene.fpa.commission_baseline.c3.fail: Another team lead compares baselines in the canteen. He asks Khang why one team's baseline fell by eleven percent in March.
scene.fpa.early_board_numbers.l1: Could you show me the board pack numbers a couple of days before they go out? The owner family has a friend who trades in our supplier's shares, and Bao says that if the numbers are good, we should tell our friends at the steel company, to keep the relationship warm.
scene.fpa.early_board_numbers.c1: Decline, explain that the board numbers are confidential until released, and offer the published figures from last quarter.
scene.fpa.early_board_numbers.c1.ok: Huy blushes, and says he did not think of it that way. He thanks you for saying it without a lecture. Bao grumbles.
scene.fpa.early_board_numbers.c2: Say you will think about it, and give him only the headline direction, up or down.
scene.fpa.early_board_numbers.c2.ok: Huy says 'Up', and repeats it to Bao. A conversation happens at lunch that you wish you had prevented.
scene.fpa.early_board_numbers.c3: Send Huy the draft pack, and tell him not to share it.
scene.fpa.early_board_numbers.c3.ok: Huy reads it, and tells Bao on the stairs. Bao makes a phone call that evening, which you do not hear about.
scene.fpa.early_board_numbers.c3.fail: The supplier's shares move on the Monday before the board pack goes out. A regulator's letter asks the company who had access to the draft. Your name is on the access log.
scene.fpa.capex_split.l1: I need a new hydraulic unit for press 2: ninety million. Approval above fifty million goes to the board and takes six weeks. If you raise it as two purchase requests of forty-five million each, I can have it in a fortnight. They are two parts. Almost.
scene.fpa.capex_split.c1: Raise one request for ninety million, with a business case for urgency, and ask Duc for an emergency approval.
scene.fpa.capex_split.c1.ok: Duc approves an emergency request in four days, with the board informed after. Lan gets the unit, and is not thrilled with the form.
scene.fpa.capex_split.c1.fail: Duc says there is no emergency route this month and the board will meet in four weeks. The press runs at half load.
scene.fpa.capex_split.c2: Raise the two parts as separate requests only if the supplier will quote them as separate, genuinely independent items.
scene.fpa.capex_split.c2.ok: The supplier quotes a pump and a valve block as separate items, with separate part numbers. It is a legitimate split, and Duc confirms that. It saves a fortnight.
scene.fpa.capex_split.c3: Raise two requests of forty-five million for one unit, to stay under the approval limit.
scene.fpa.capex_split.c3.ok: The requests go through in a day each. Lan has the unit in a fortnight and thanks you with a smile. The two requests have the same supplier, the same date and consecutive numbers.
scene.fpa.capex_split.c3.fail: Quoc's quarterly test looks for consecutive purchases to the same supplier under the limit. He finds your two, and asks Khang to explain.
scene.fpa.cost_allocation.l1: The new premium range loses money on your allocation. You are charging it a full share of the factory overhead. If you allocate overhead by revenue instead of by machine hours, the premium range makes a margin, and the directors keep funding it. It is only a method.
scene.fpa.cost_allocation.c1: Keep the allocation by machine hours, show the true margin, and offer a sensitivity page that shows both methods and what each would change.
scene.fpa.cost_allocation.c1.ok: The premium range is shown at a loss of three percent, with a path to break-even at volume. The directors keep funding it with open eyes, and Bao says it is the first fair hearing it has had.
scene.fpa.cost_allocation.c1.fail: The directors read the loss and stop the premium range. Bao is angry, and tells you that you killed it. You wrote the truth, and it still feels like that.
scene.fpa.cost_allocation.c2: Switch to a blended allocation, half machine hours and half revenue, and document the reason as 'transition'.
scene.fpa.cost_allocation.c2.ok: The premium range shows break-even. The allocation note says 'transition'. Nobody asks what the transition is to.
scene.fpa.cost_allocation.c3: Allocate overhead by revenue for the premium range only, and keep the other ranges on machine hours.
scene.fpa.cost_allocation.c3.ok: The premium range earns a nice margin. The standard range, which bears the extra overhead, quietly looks worse. Lan notices that her costs have gone up by no reason she can find.
scene.fpa.cost_allocation.c3.fail: Quoc's review compares allocation methods across product lines, and finds two. He asks Khang for the decision paper, and there is none.
scene.fpa.audit_asks.l1: I have a list of items from the planning cycle I would like to understand: a reclassification of maintenance costs, some invoices that moved across the quarter end, a line in the board pack with nothing under it, and a missing set of model versions. I would like to hear from the person who prepared the numbers.
scene.fpa.audit_asks.c1: Tell him what happened: who asked, what you agreed, what should have been done, and what is being corrected. Give him the files.
scene.fpa.audit_asks.c1.ok: Quoc writes it all down. The finding is serious, but it is recorded as 'self-reported and corrected'. The classification is reversed, the bank is told, and you receive a formal warning.
scene.fpa.audit_asks.c2: Give him the files, and say the decisions were Duc's and Mr Cuong's, and that FP&A prepared what it was asked.
scene.fpa.audit_asks.c2.ok: Quoc notes that the analyst built and signed the numbers. He writes it down, carefully.
scene.fpa.audit_asks.c2.fail: Hanh and Thu are called in. Each has her own copy of the instructions, and the emails are in the same order. Quoc places them next to your notes.
scene.fpa.audit_asks.c3: Say you do not recall the details, and offer to look.
scene.fpa.audit_asks.c3.ok: Quoc gives you a week. You find the files and hand them over. It is not the whole truth, but it is something.
scene.fpa.audit_asks.c3.fail: The server backups, the supplier statements and the bank's copy of the covenant calculation arrive on the same afternoon. Quoc has them on the table next to your notes.
scene.fpa.board_blame.l1: The board has received a letter from the bank. It questions the forecast it was given in the autumn, and asks who prepared it. The board is meeting tomorrow, and I would like to know, before it does, who in finance is responsible for the numbers. I would like to hear it from you first.
scene.fpa.board_blame.c1: Tell her the real account: what you were asked, what you agreed to change, and your own part. Show her the version history.
scene.fpa.board_blame.c1.ok: Giang reads it slowly, and takes your account to the board with her own note beside it. You are moved off bank reporting and keep your job and, eventually, your name.
scene.fpa.board_blame.c2: Say the forecast was Duc's and Mr Cuong's, and that you only prepared the model.
scene.fpa.board_blame.c2.ok: The board treats it as shared responsibility. Nobody leaves the room liked, and Duc stops speaking to you.
scene.fpa.board_blame.c2.fail: Khang has the emails that came with each change, and your replies. He reads two of them aloud, without raising his voice.
scene.fpa.board_blame.c3: Say that Huy built the sales inputs and that the errors are in his data.
scene.fpa.board_blame.c3.ok: The board nods and Huy is given a warning that he does not contest. He resigns in two months. The inputs are still in your formulas.
scene.fpa.board_blame.c3.fail: Huy has the email chain showing the optimistic assumptions came from FP&A's own adjustments. He puts it on the table.
role.mkt.brand.title: Brand and Digital Marketing Executive
role.mkt.manager.title: Marketing Manager
role.mkt.brand.blurb: You run the brand and the digital campaigns of a cookware company. Your pressures: a launch date that does not wait for the test results, a claim that looks great on the box, a review score that needs a push, and an agency with a generous idea of how to thank you.
char.quyen.name: Ms Quyen
char.quyen.title: Marketing Manager
char.dat.name: Mr Dat
char.dat.title: Account lead, the advertising agency
char.my.name: My
char.my.title: Lifestyle content creator
char.nga.name: Ms Nga
char.nga.title: Customer service lead
char.lam.name: Mr Lam
char.lam.title: Consumer-protection inspector
arc.the_claim.title: The claim
arc.the_reviews.title: The reviews
arc.the_agency.title: The agency
fact.substantiated_claims: you checked every claim against its evidence before it went public
lesson.substantiated_claims: A claims register is a slow process that prevents a rare, expensive embarrassment. The claim that the test can support is the only one a buyer, a regulator and a journalist will leave alone.
fact.overclaimed_on_packaging: you printed a lifetime claim on the packaging that the tests did not support
lesson.overclaimed_on_packaging: A claim on a box is a promise to every buyer. Printing one the tests do not support, because a competitor does, is borrowing a risk that the company, not the competitor, will repay.
fact.hid_test_result: you kept a bad test result to yourself until after a launch
lesson.hid_test_result: A test result you hold back is a decision to let customers find the problem first. The lab keeps the report, and the lab is also the first person the customer service team asks.
fact.corrected_the_claim: you corrected a claim when the evidence turned against it, in public and at your own cost
lesson.corrected_the_claim: Correcting a claim costs a reprint and a day of embarrassment. It buys the credibility that every future claim is spent from.
fact.shipped_with_known_false_claim: you shipped a product with a claim on the box that you knew the evidence did not support
lesson.shipped_with_known_false_claim: Knowing is the difference between a mistake and a decision. Once the pallets leave, every buyer who reads the box is relying on a statement you knew was false.
fact.blamed_customers_for_defect: you told customers that a coating defect was caused by how they used the pan
lesson.blamed_customers_for_defect: Blaming the customer for a defect you can trace to a batch is a statement the lab can contradict. It also tells your service team to stop trusting what marketing sends them.
fact.bought_fake_reviews: you had fake reviews posted to lift the product's rating
lesson.bought_fake_reviews: A fake review is a lie told by a stranger on the buyer's behalf. Marketplaces look for the pattern of new accounts, and a bought rating is the first thing a competitor learns to check.
fact.sabotaged_rival_reviews: you had a rival's reviews reported and removed to damage them
lesson.sabotaged_rival_reviews: Attacking a rival's reviews is not competition. It is the same lie, aimed at someone who can read the logs and answer back.
fact.disclosed_sponsorship: you made sure a paid influencer post carried a clear label and an honest opinion
lesson.disclosed_sponsorship: A labelled post is trusted a little less and for much longer. The label is the price of being believed on the day the sponsorship is discovered.
fact.undisclosed_influencer: you had an influencer post paid content without a label and without a mention of payment
lesson.undisclosed_influencer: A paid post presented as spontaneous love misleads the people who trust the creator. It also hands the creator a secret that they will keep only as long as it is easy.
fact.blamed_the_agency: you said the agency acted alone, when you had approved what it did
lesson.blamed_the_agency: An agency keeps the emails, and every approval is in them. Blaming it for what you approved ends the relationship and publishes the evidence.
fact.ran_competitive_pitch: you ran a competitive pitch with written scoring, even for the owner's relative
lesson.ran_competitive_pitch: A scored pitch protects the winner as much as the loser. It is the cheapest way to show the owner's cousin, and everyone else, that the process was fair.
fact.steered_contract_to_connection: you gave a contract to the owner's relative without a pitch, and said it was the directors' decision
lesson.steered_contract_to_connection: A contract given without a pitch leaves one page in the file. The next person to ask finds that the 'decision' has no author, and the author is the one who wrote the page.
fact.approved_invoice_for_undelivered_wo: you approved an invoice that included work that was never delivered
lesson.approved_invoice_for_undelivered_: Approving an invoice is saying the work was done. 'Production contingency' for a video that does not exist is a payment for nothing, and your signature is on it.
fact.reported_agency_gift: you declined or declared a gift from a supplier that was hoping to renew
lesson.reported_agency_gift: A gift offered before a renewal is the first instalment of a conversation about it. Declining or declaring keeps the conversation in an office, with the person who is supposed to be there.
fact.accepted_agency_trip: you accepted a paid resort weekend from the agency and told nobody
lesson.accepted_agency_trip: A trip from a supplier is a debt that the supplier will remember at the next renewal. Not declaring it removes the one thing that would have made it harmless.
fact.backdated_claim_evidence: you wrote source references into the register after the claims had been published, and cleaned up reviews before an inspection
lesson.backdated_claim_evidence: A register is evidence only if it was made when the claim was. Filling it in afterwards, and deleting what might raise questions, turns a gap into an attempt to mislead the inspector.
fact.polished_marketing_review: you left the claims and posts that were close to the line out of your own review
lesson.polished_marketing_review: A review without the close calls rewards the wrong skill. The register shows the revision dates, and your manager reads them.
fact.accepted_marketing_condition: you accepted the marketing lead role without asking what the condition meant
lesson.accepted_marketing_condition: A promotion with an unspoken condition is a decision to be made later, under pressure, by someone who has already said yes.
fact.used_unlicensed_image: you used an image from a rival's website without a licence
lesson.used_unlicensed_image: A cropped logo is not a licence. Image searches find everything, and the invoice for a borrowed picture is many times the price of a bought one.
fact.unfair_comparison_ad: you ran a comparison ad using test conditions that favoured your own product
lesson.unfair_comparison_ad: A comparison is only as honest as its conditions. An advert that compares a gas ring with an induction hob is true in the lab and false in the kitchen.
fact.wasteful_year_end_spend: you had an agency invoice work to be delivered next year, so that a budget would be spent
lesson.wasteful_year_end_spend: Spending to keep a budget is paying for nothing in order to be given more of it. The invoice date, the delivery date and the person who approved both are in the file.
fact.emailed_without_consent: you emailed a purchased list of people who had not agreed to hear from the company
lesson.emailed_without_consent: A list that people did not choose to join is a list of people to annoy. It also turns every unsubscribe into a complaint, and a regulator reads the complaints.
fact.paid_for_award: you displayed a paid-entry magazine award as if it were an independent honour
lesson.paid_for_award: An award that you bought and present as earned spends the credibility of every genuine award you will ever win.
fact.fake_urgency_timer: you built a countdown timer and stock banner that were false
lesson.fake_urgency_timer: A false 'only 7 left' is a lie told to every visitor. It works until one visitor takes a screenshot, and then it is the story.
fact.greenwashed_claim: you put an 'eco-friendly' claim on products that contain no recycled material
lesson.greenwashed_claim: A green claim must be as specific as the evidence. 'Eco-friendly' on eight lines that have nothing recycled is the sort of sentence a buyer's sustainability team is paid to check.
fact.staged_testimonial: you ran paid actors as real customers in a testimonial
lesson.staged_testimonial: A testimonial from a customer who does not exist is a lie with a face. Actors are recognised, and a name like 'the Tran family' invites a search.
fact.stalled_the_regulator: you told a consumer-protection inspector that you did not recall details that you did
lesson.stalled_the_regulator: 'I do not recall' is a decision when it is not true. The web archive and the lab's report log do not need your memory.
scene.mkt.first_week.l1: Welcome. Our brand is simple: honest cookware that lasts. Every claim on a box, a page or a post goes in the claims register with its source, and QC signs the technical ones. I know it is slower. It is also what stops us from being laughed at in public.
scene.mkt.first_week.l2: If you want to say a number about the coating, I have the test reports. Come to the lab and I will show you what they actually say.
scene.mkt.first_week.c1: Go to the QC lab with Khoa, read the coating reports with him, and start the claims register with the three claims already on the website.
scene.mkt.first_week.c1.ok: One website claim has a report, one has a note, and one has nothing. Khoa says: 'Nobody has asked me before.' Quyen reads your register and says only 'Good. Fix the third before anyone asks.'
scene.mkt.first_week.c2: Read the brand guidelines first, and build the claims register later in the month.
scene.mkt.first_week.c2.ok: You learn the tone of voice quickly. A sales email goes out with a claim that the register does not have yet.
scene.mkt.first_week.c3: Trust that the existing copy was checked, and start on the campaign calendar.
scene.mkt.first_week.c3.ok: The calendar is on time. Nobody asks about the old claims, until a customer does.
scene.mkt.first_week.c3.fail: A buyer's email quotes a website claim and asks for the test report. You do not have it, and neither does anyone you ask.
scene.mkt.midyear_review.l1: Half a year. Your reach is lower than the target, but the leads you generated convert better than any other channel, and nobody has complained about a claim. The directors only look at reach. How do you want to handle that?
scene.mkt.midyear_review.c1: Show the full funnel: reach, leads, conversion, cost per sale and returns, and propose that cost per sale, not reach, is the measure.
scene.mkt.midyear_review.c1.ok: Quyen takes the page to Mr Cuong. 'Cost per sale' is added to the review next to reach. A small change, and it changes what campaigns are rewarded for.
scene.mkt.midyear_review.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says reach is what the board understands. Quyen shrugs: 'I tried.' Your reach number stays modest.
scene.mkt.midyear_review.c2: Say you will lift reach with a paid campaign that stays inside the spend limit, and ask for a month.
scene.mkt.midyear_review.c2.ok: Quyen agrees, and writes the limit next to the plan. Your reach rises by a third, and so does the cost per lead.
scene.mkt.midyear_review.c3: Say you will hit the reach number whatever it takes.
scene.mkt.midyear_review.c3.ok: Quyen smiles. 'Good attitude.' A week later you notice that the cheapest way to reach a million people is a giveaway, a controversy or a claim that is a little too big.
scene.mkt.midyear_review.c3.fail: Dat hears about 'whatever it takes' and sends over three ideas, one of which you would not like to see in the newspaper.
scene.mkt.launch_twist.l1: Mr Anders wants the new Eterna range in his stores for the autumn promotion, three weeks earlier than we planned. The packaging has to go to print on Friday. Khoa's final coating test is not finished. I need your word that the box can say what we want it to say.
scene.mkt.launch_twist.l2: Decide what the box can say with the evidence we have on Friday, not with the evidence we hope for.
scene.mkt.launch_twist.c1: Write the box copy only from the finished tests, leave the lifetime claim out, say 'tested to three thousand cycles' with the test reference, and add the long-life claim later if the final test supports it.
scene.mkt.launch_twist.c1.ok: Bao complains that it is flat. The box goes to print on Friday with a number that Khoa has signed. Anders's team says the claim is 'credible', which they say about very few boxes.
scene.mkt.launch_twist.c1.fail: Anders's team wants the lifetime claim the competitor uses. Bao says that without it the range will not be listed. You hold the line, and the listing is delayed by two weeks.
scene.mkt.launch_twist.c2: Put the strongest claim that the interim results do not contradict on the box, and ask Khoa to confirm it by Thursday.
scene.mkt.launch_twist.c2.ok: Khoa confirms a softer version on Thursday. The box says 'long-lasting non-stick' with a reference to the interim test. It is more than he wanted, and less than Bao did.
scene.mkt.launch_twist.c3: Put 'non-stick for life' on the box, because the competitor does, and sort out the evidence after the launch.
scene.mkt.launch_twist.c3.ok: The box goes to print. Bao is delighted, and Anders's team sends a thumbs up. Khoa's test is still running. Nobody tells you what it will say.
scene.mkt.launch_twist.c3.fail: Khoa sees the printer's proof on Thursday, and goes straight to Quyen with the interim results. The proof is stopped, and a reprint costs eight million.
scene.mkt.consumer_inspection.l1: I am carrying out a routine consumer-protection inspection of advertising. I would like to see the claims register, the evidence for the technical claims on the packaging and the website, the process for product reviews and any paid or sponsored content. I start with the evidence, not with the creative.
scene.mkt.consumer_inspection.l2: Show him what he asks for. Do not guess. If we do not know, we say we will find out.
scene.mkt.consumer_inspection.c1: Give him the register with every claim and its source, the test reports, the review policy, and the list of sponsored posts with their disclosures, including the gaps you know about.
scene.mkt.consumer_inspection.c1.ok: Lam reads for three hours and writes four observations. None is serious. 'A register that matches the packaging. I wish that were less unusual.' Khoa nods across the room.
scene.mkt.consumer_inspection.c2: Answer his questions and give him the documents he asks for, without volunteering anything.
scene.mkt.consumer_inspection.c2.ok: A routine inspection. Lam notes two items, both already on Quyen's list. You come out with nothing to hide and no credit either.
scene.mkt.consumer_inspection.c3: Prepare the files: write source references into the register for claims that have none, and remove the reviews and posts that might raise questions.
scene.mkt.consumer_inspection.c3.ok: Lam sees a complete register. He asks where the reference for the lifetime claim came from, since the report is dated after the packaging print date, and accepts the explanation.
scene.mkt.consumer_inspection.c3.fail: Khoa's report log shows the date each test was requested. The web archive shows the deleted reviews. Lam places the two side by side, and says nothing for a long time.
scene.mkt.year_end_review.l1: Annual review. Before I give you my view, tell me how you would rate your own year, and what you would say differently on the box.
scene.mkt.year_end_review.c1: Give an honest account, including the claim you stretched, the post that should have been labelled, and what it would have cost to be careful earlier.
scene.mkt.year_end_review.c1.ok: Quyen is quiet for a long moment. She writes: 'Makes the brand say what the product can do.' It is the best thing you have read about yourself.
scene.mkt.year_end_review.c2: Stay modest: list the wins and one thing to improve.
scene.mkt.year_end_review.c2.ok: A safe review. Quyen nods and moves to the next topic.
scene.mkt.year_end_review.c3: Present the year as a success and leave out the claims and posts that were close to the line.
scene.mkt.year_end_review.c3.ok: It lands well. You leave with a good rating and a small weight in your chest.
scene.mkt.year_end_review.c3.fail: Quyen has the claims register open on her desk, with the revision dates. She turns the screen towards you without a word.
scene.mkt.manager_offer.l1: I am moving to group brand at the end of the year. Mr Cuong asked me who should lead marketing here. I named you. One condition: every month, a director will ask you to say something on the box that the evidence does not quite support. I need to know what you will say.
scene.mkt.manager_offer.c1: Accept, and say plainly which claims you will not make, and that the directors will hear it from you first, with the evidence.
scene.mkt.manager_offer.c1.ok: Quyen smiles. 'Then it is yours. Put the list on the first page of the claims register.' You take over marketing with the limits in writing.
scene.mkt.manager_offer.c2: Thank her, but decline: you prefer making the campaigns to defending them to the directors.
scene.mkt.manager_offer.c2.ok: Quyen looks disappointed, then understanding. 'The next manager may not be as careful as you.'
scene.mkt.manager_offer.c3: Accept without asking what the condition means in practice.
scene.mkt.manager_offer.c3.ok: Quyen nods slowly and Mr Cuong congratulates you a little too warmly. You realise you agreed to something you did not ask about.
scene.mkt.resignation_thought.l1: You look like you have not slept. With respect: I have seen marketing people refresh the numbers every five minutes for a month, and leave by the summer. Are you all right?
scene.mkt.resignation_thought.c1: Talk to Quyen about the load, and ask her to take the agency calls off your plate for a month.
scene.mkt.resignation_thought.c1.ok: Quyen listens, takes the agency calls herself, and says she should have noticed sooner.
scene.mkt.resignation_thought.c1.fail: Quyen nods and says everyone is stretched at launch time. You leave with sympathy and the same load.
scene.mkt.resignation_thought.c2: Hand in your resignation, politely, with the notice the contract requires.
scene.mkt.resignation_thought.c2.ok: Quyen reads it twice and does not argue. You hand over the claims register and walk out lighter than you walked in.
scene.mkt.resignation_thought.c3: Tell Nga you are fine and keep going.
scene.mkt.resignation_thought.c3.ok: Nga nods and does not push. You feel slightly worse afterwards for having said it.
scene.mkt.khoa_data.l1: The final coating tests are in. Three thousand cycles: eighty-eight percent of the non-stick effect remains. Five thousand cycles: sixty-two percent. And batch C failed the adhesion test, so the coating can flake in some pans. Whatever the box says, this is what the evidence says. What do you want to do with it?
scene.mkt.khoa_data.c1: Update the claims register and the website straight away, check the box against the results, and tell Bao and Quyen which claims no longer hold, and what batch C means.
scene.mkt.khoa_data.c1.ok: Quyen reads the results twice. 'Thank you for not waiting.' Batch C is held, the register is corrected, and Bao is angry with the evidence, not with you.
scene.mkt.khoa_data.c2: Thank Khoa, note the results in the register, and wait for the launch review to decide what to change.
scene.mkt.khoa_data.c2.ok: The register has the results. The box, the website and the sales deck have not changed yet. The launch review is in three weeks.
scene.mkt.khoa_data.c3: Keep the results to yourself until after the launch, and tell Khoa you will deal with it.
scene.mkt.khoa_data.c3.ok: Khoa nods, with a look. The launch goes ahead on the original copy. The report sits in your drawer, and in his system.
scene.mkt.khoa_data.c3.fail: Khoa sends the report to Quyen himself, with a polite note asking whether marketing has seen it. Quyen asks you in the corridor.
scene.mkt.ship_or_reprint.l1: A thousand sets are on pallets with the printed boxes. Anders's trucks come on Monday. If we reprint the boxes, it costs eighteen million and ten days. If we put a sticker over the claim, it looks cheap. If we ship, we ship. Tell me what we do.
scene.mkt.ship_or_reprint.c1: Hold the pallets, reprint the boxes with a claim the evidence supports, and tell Anders's team the truth about the new date.
scene.mkt.ship_or_reprint.c1.ok: The reprint costs eighteen million and ten days. Anders says the delay is 'irritating, and better than a recall'. Bao says nothing for two days, and then sends a note that says 'fair'.
scene.mkt.ship_or_reprint.c1.fail: Anders's promotion window closes before the reprint is ready, and he reduces the order by a third. Mr Cuong asks why the box had to change. Quyen answers, calmly, with Khoa's report.
scene.mkt.ship_or_reprint.c2: Ship with a neat sticker over the claim that is not supported, and put the corrected text on the website.
scene.mkt.ship_or_reprint.c2.ok: Anders's team puts the stickers on the first display, and mutters about it. The claim on the box is covered, and the website tells the truth. It is a cheap fix with a visible edge.
scene.mkt.ship_or_reprint.c3: Ship the pallets as printed, and fix the next batch.
scene.mkt.ship_or_reprint.c3.ok: The trucks leave on Monday with a claim that you know the evidence does not support. Bao thanks you. A thousand customers read it in the next two weeks.
scene.mkt.ship_or_reprint.c3.fail: A buyer's quality team opens a box and compares the claim with the technical sheet they were sent. Anders's email arrives that evening, with the two pages attached.
scene.mkt.claim_complaint.l1: Customer service has had forty-one calls this month about the new pan: the coating is flaking after a few weeks. Some are angry, some are posting photos. People quote the box. What should we tell them?
scene.mkt.claim_complaint.c1: Agree a clear, honest message with Nga and Khoa: acknowledge the problem, offer a replacement or refund, quarantine the affected batch, and correct the claim publicly.
scene.mkt.claim_complaint.c1.ok: The message costs money and goodwill in the first week, and earns some back in the second. Nga says: 'Finally, something I can say to them that is true.' The complaints fall by half.
scene.mkt.claim_complaint.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says a public correction will be remembered longer than the flaking. The replacements cost more than he expected, and he says it three times. You keep the message.
scene.mkt.claim_complaint.c2: Have Nga handle each complaint individually with a replacement, without a public statement.
scene.mkt.claim_complaint.c2.ok: The customers who call are helped. Those who post are answered one by one. The claim stays on the box and the website.
scene.mkt.claim_complaint.c3: Tell Nga that the flaking is caused by misuse, and that customers should be told to use wooden spoons.
scene.mkt.claim_complaint.c3.ok: The reply goes out. Some customers accept it. The ones who do not forward it to a consumer forum, with your words and the box side by side.
scene.mkt.claim_complaint.c3.fail: Khoa's lab confirms the flaking is a coating adhesion failure on batch C, and the confirmation is dated before your reply. Nga forwards it to Quyen, with a polite question.
scene.mkt.slow_launch.l1: The Eterna pan has eleven reviews on the marketplace, and the average is three point eight. The rival's is four point six with four hundred. Nobody buys a three point eight. Do something.
scene.mkt.slow_launch.c1: Email real buyers a polite request for an honest review, fix the two issues that the low reviews mention, and answer every negative review publicly.
scene.mkt.slow_launch.c1.ok: In three weeks there are sixty reviews and the average is four point one. It is slower than Bao wanted, and the reviews are real.
scene.mkt.slow_launch.c1.fail: Two of the new reviews are harsh and fair. Bao reads them aloud in the meeting. You answer them in public, and one of the reviewers raises the score.
scene.mkt.slow_launch.c2: Offer a discount to buyers who write a review, with a note that the review must be honest and disclose the discount.
scene.mkt.slow_launch.c2.ok: Reviews rise, and the average rises with them, to four point two. The disclosure line is in every one. A few commentators say incentivised reviews are never quite neutral, and they are right.
scene.mkt.slow_launch.c3: Ask Dat's agency to seed the page with reviews, and do not ask how.
scene.mkt.slow_launch.c3.ok: Dat says 'Leave it to us.' Two hundred reviews appear in four days. Bao is delighted. The reviewers' accounts are each three days old.
scene.mkt.slow_launch.c3.fail: The marketplace flags the pattern and removes a hundred and eighty reviews, along with the page's badge. Nga sees customers asking about it, and tells Quyen.
scene.mkt.review_batch.l1: Quick idea for the weekend. We have a network of accounts that can post positive comments and reviews at scale. A hundred a day, with real photos. It is how everybody in the category does it. We can also take down a few of the rival's reviews, if you want, with a report to the marketplace.
scene.mkt.review_batch.c1: Decline both, and ask Dat for a proposal on real customer content: unboxing videos from actual buyers, a review request in the pack, and a helpful answers page.
scene.mkt.review_batch.c1.ok: Dat sighs, and says 'Slower, but cleaner.' His proposal arrives on Monday, and it is good. Quyen reads it and says 'This is the one.'
scene.mkt.review_batch.c2: Accept a small batch of testimonials from real employees and friends of the company, clearly marked as such.
scene.mkt.review_batch.c2.ok: Forty reviews appear with a line saying 'posted by a member of the team'. They are warm, and some people discount them. It is not deceptive.
scene.mkt.review_batch.c3: Accept both, and keep it between the two of you.
scene.mkt.review_batch.c3.ok: The rating climbs to four point six in a week. The rival's drops. Bao sends you a bottle of whisky. You have a phone number that you will never put in the register.
scene.mkt.review_batch.c3.fail: The rival's marketing team recognises the pattern and posts it to a trade group with screenshots. Quyen's phone starts to ring at seven in the morning.
scene.mkt.influencer_post.l1: I love the pan and I will post about it. The agency said that the fee is for 'content creation', and that I do not need the paid-partnership label because my followers prefer it natural. I will do whatever you tell me. I just want to know what you want.
scene.mkt.influencer_post.c1: Ask My to use the paid-partnership label and a plain line saying that she was paid, and let her say honestly what she likes and what she does not.
scene.mkt.influencer_post.c1.ok: My posts that she loves the grip and finds the lid a little heavy. The label is on. Engagement is lower than the last paid post, and the comments are more curious than cynical.
scene.mkt.influencer_post.c1.fail: Dat is annoyed that the agency's script was changed. He tells you 'It works better without the label.' You tell him it works for the rules better with it.
scene.mkt.influencer_post.c2: Let My post in her own way, and ask her to mention in the caption that the brand sent the pan.
scene.mkt.influencer_post.c2.ok: The post says 'thanks to the brand for sending this'. It is half-honest, and it does not say that My was paid. A commentator asks, and My answers truthfully.
scene.mkt.influencer_post.c3: Tell My to post it naturally, with no label and no mention of payment, as the agency said.
scene.mkt.influencer_post.c3.ok: The post looks spontaneous, and reaches two hundred thousand people. A dozen of them buy the pan in the first hour. Nobody knows My was paid, except My.
scene.mkt.influencer_post.c3.fail: A follower finds the invoice reference in a screenshot of an email that My shared, innocently, in another post. The thread asks if the company pays for 'spontaneous' love.
scene.mkt.review_exposed.l1: A consumer blog has published a piece about the reviews of the category. It does not name us, but it describes a pattern of accounts, review dates and an influencer, that fit us exactly. A journalist has asked for comment. Tell me what we say, and tell me what is true.
scene.mkt.review_exposed.c1: Tell Quyen exactly what was done and by whom, draft a short public statement that corrects the record, and ask the marketplace to review any content you cannot stand behind.
scene.mkt.review_exposed.c1.ok: Quyen reads the draft and says 'This will hurt for a month.' The statement goes out. The journalist writes 'the company moved before being asked'. The reviews that remain are real, and there are fewer of them.
scene.mkt.review_exposed.c2: Say the company has a review policy and has not been contacted by the marketplace, and give the journalist no further comment.
scene.mkt.review_exposed.c2.ok: The journalist writes 'the company declined to comment on the pattern'. It is not a headline, and the question remains.
scene.mkt.review_exposed.c2.fail: The journalist contacts My and Dat's former colleague. A second article appears with names, and Quyen asks, quietly, what the policy actually was.
scene.mkt.review_exposed.c3: Say that the agency acted on its own initiative and that the company knew nothing about it.
scene.mkt.review_exposed.c3.ok: The statement holds for a day. Dat says nothing in public, and a great deal in private.
scene.mkt.review_exposed.c3.fail: Dat has the emails. He puts three of them in the journalist's inbox before lunch, with your replies in them.
scene.mkt.agency_pitch.l1: My cousin has just started an agency. Very creative. I think we should give her the autumn campaign, and she will do it at a good price. You know how it is in a family company. Just put her in the proposal list, at the top.
scene.mkt.agency_pitch.c1: Invite three agencies including Long's cousin to pitch against the same brief, score them on written criteria with Quyen, and tell Long she is welcome to compete.
scene.mkt.agency_pitch.c1.ok: Long's cousin comes second, with a lively idea and a weak plan. Dat's agency wins on price and delivery. Long is polite and slightly cold. The scoring sheet is on the file.
scene.mkt.agency_pitch.c1.fail: Long's cousin wins on score. It is a fair result, and the agency is a very small one. You spend a month making sure it can deliver.
scene.mkt.agency_pitch.c2: Add Long's cousin as a fourth option at the top of the list, and say the final decision will be made by Quyen.
scene.mkt.agency_pitch.c2.ok: Quyen picks Dat's agency and gives no reason. Long assumes that you did not push hard enough.
scene.mkt.agency_pitch.c3: Give the campaign to Long's cousin without a pitch, and tell Quyen it was a directors' decision.
scene.mkt.agency_pitch.c3.ok: Long beams. Quyen does not argue, and writes the date in her notebook. Dat hears about it, and asks nothing.
scene.mkt.agency_pitch.c3.fail: Duc asks for the procurement file for the campaign, and finds one page. He asks Quyen. Quyen asks you.
scene.mkt.invoice_mismatch.l1: Our invoice for the autumn campaign is in your inbox. I know the shoot was cut from three days to two, and the second video was never made. But we kept the crew booked, and cancellations cost us money. Could you approve it as it is? If it is easier, I can put the difference down as 'production contingency'.
scene.mkt.invoice_mismatch.c1: Ask for a revised invoice for the work delivered, and agree a fair cancellation fee for the crew with written evidence.
scene.mkt.invoice_mismatch.c1.ok: Dat grumbles, and sends a revised invoice, with a modest cancellation fee. It is eighteen percent lower. He says 'Fair enough' in the tone of a man recalculating.
scene.mkt.invoice_mismatch.c1.fail: Dat says the contract has no cancellation clause, and that he will talk to Long. Long phones you the next morning, and you hold the line, politely.
scene.mkt.invoice_mismatch.c2: Approve the invoice for the delivered work plus a smaller cancellation fee that you can justify with the booking confirmation.
scene.mkt.invoice_mismatch.c2.ok: The invoice is reduced by eight percent, with a note. Dat accepts. It is a compromise that Duc can read in one page.
scene.mkt.invoice_mismatch.c3: Approve the invoice as it is, with 'production contingency' for the difference.
scene.mkt.invoice_mismatch.c3.ok: Dat thanks you warmly. The invoice goes to payment. It includes a day of crew and a video that do not exist.
scene.mkt.invoice_mismatch.c3.fail: Thu, in accounts payable, compares the invoice with the delivery list and finds a video missing. She asks you politely, and writes your answer down.
scene.mkt.agency_gift.l1: To thank you for a great autumn, the agency would like to send you and a guest to a resort for the long weekend, all paid. We do it for all our clients' key people. It is not connected to the contract. Though of course, we would love to talk about next year.
scene.mkt.agency_gift.c1: Decline politely, explain the company's gift policy, and suggest that any thanks take the form of a campaign report, a lunch that you pay for yourself, or nothing.
scene.mkt.agency_gift.c1.ok: Dat laughs, and says 'You are the first one who ever refused.' He does not seem offended. The renewal conversation takes place in an office, with Quyen present.
scene.mkt.agency_gift.c2: Say you can only accept a small, ordinary gift under the policy limit, and declare it in the gift register.
scene.mkt.agency_gift.c2.ok: Dat sends a bottle of wine under the limit. You enter it in the register with the date. It is awkward and clean.
scene.mkt.agency_gift.c3: Accept the resort weekend and tell nobody.
scene.mkt.agency_gift.c3.ok: The weekend is excellent. Dat is excellent company. On Monday he mentions next year's budget as if by accident, and you hear yourself say 'We will see what we can do'.
scene.mkt.agency_gift.c3.fail: The resort posts a photo of the agency's group with a tag that includes you. Quyen sees it that afternoon, and asks, lightly, how the weekend was.
scene.mkt.duc_asks_invoices.l1: I am looking at the agency's spend for the year. It is thirty percent over the budget, and the invoices are described in very general terms. I would like to understand what we bought, who approved it, and how the agency was chosen. I would like to hear it from you first.
scene.mkt.duc_asks_invoices.c1: Walk Duc through the pitch scores, the invoices line by line, what was delivered, and the gift policy in each case, including anything that does not hold up.
scene.mkt.duc_asks_invoices.c1.ok: Duc reads for an hour. 'This is the first agency file I have seen that I can follow.' He asks for two adjustments and a new approval rule. Dat sends the credit note the same afternoon.
scene.mkt.duc_asks_invoices.c2: Give Duc the invoices and say the agency is Quyen's responsibility.
scene.mkt.duc_asks_invoices.c2.ok: Duc nods, and asks Quyen. Quyen answers with her own list of the questions she asked you in the spring.
scene.mkt.duc_asks_invoices.c2.fail: Thu and Quyen each have their own notes, and the notes agree with each other and not with you. Duc puts them in a row.
scene.mkt.duc_asks_invoices.c3: Say the overspend was needed to protect the launch, and that the details can wait until after the year end.
scene.mkt.duc_asks_invoices.c3.ok: Duc gives you until the end of the month. You assemble a partial file. It is not everything, but it is something.
scene.mkt.duc_asks_invoices.c3.fail: The bank statement shows a payment to a travel company, in the agency's name, on the date of your weekend. Duc turns the page over in silence.
scene.mkt.borrowed_photo.l1: We are two days from the post and the photographer's shots of the kitchen are not ready. I found a beautiful picture of a family cooking with a pan very like ours. It is from a European brand's website. Nobody will notice. Shall we use it?
scene.mkt.borrowed_photo.c1: Use a licensed stock image or reshoot with the team's own kitchen, and move the post by a day.
scene.mkt.borrowed_photo.c1.ok: The licensed photo costs three hundred thousand dong and looks nearly as good. The post goes out a day late, and no one is unhappy.
scene.mkt.borrowed_photo.c1.fail: The licence terms do not allow use in paid ads. You find out on the second day, and renegotiate it for a small extra fee.
scene.mkt.borrowed_photo.c2: Ask the European brand for permission, and use the picture only if they agree.
scene.mkt.borrowed_photo.c2.ok: The brand says no, politely, in two days. The post uses a different picture. You lost a day and gained a line in the register.
scene.mkt.borrowed_photo.c3: Use the picture, and crop the logo out of the corner.
scene.mkt.borrowed_photo.c3.ok: The post does very well. Nobody notices for three weeks.
scene.mkt.borrowed_photo.c3.fail: The brand's agency finds it with an image search, and sends a letter with a licence fee ten times what a stock photo would have cost, copied to Mr Cuong.
scene.mkt.comparative_ad.l1: I want an ad that says our pan heats up twice as fast as the leading rival. We tested it in the lab with our pan on a gas ring and theirs on an induction hob. The numbers are real. The comparison is a little creative, but who is going to check?
scene.mkt.comparative_ad.c1: Ask Khoa to rerun the test on the same hob under the same conditions, and run the ad only with the result that holds.
scene.mkt.comparative_ad.c1.ok: On the same hob, the pan heats thirty percent faster. The ad says thirty percent and cites the test. Bao says 'It is less exciting', and the number is defensible in any room.
scene.mkt.comparative_ad.c1.fail: On the same hob the difference is nine percent. The ad is shelved. Bao says it was a waste of three days, and Khoa quietly says it was worth it.
scene.mkt.comparative_ad.c2: Run the ad with the real test conditions stated in small print under the claim.
scene.mkt.comparative_ad.c2.ok: The claim is large, and the small print is accurate, and readable with a magnifying glass. A competitor's lawyer reads it, and takes no action.
scene.mkt.comparative_ad.c3: Run the ad as Bao asked, 'twice as fast', with no conditions.
scene.mkt.comparative_ad.c3.ok: The ad runs. Bao is delighted, and sales go up four percent. A reviewer buys both pans and posts the cooking test with the two hobs in the same shot.
scene.mkt.comparative_ad.c3.fail: The rival's lawyer sends a letter with the test conditions, the hob types and a demand to withdraw. The ad is pulled, and the statement is in the trade press.
scene.mkt.spend_the_budget.l1: We have twenty million left in this year's budget. If we do not spend it by the thirty-first, finance takes it back, and next year's budget will be set on what we spent. I would like you to find a good use for it. Fast, and invoiced this year.
scene.mkt.spend_the_budget.c1: Spend it on something with value: a customer research survey, a product photography set, or the content library, with deliverables before year end.
scene.mkt.spend_the_budget.c1.ok: The photography set is delivered on the twentieth. It is used for the next two years. Quyen approves it with a nod.
scene.mkt.spend_the_budget.c1.fail: The studio cannot deliver before the thirty-first. You spend the money on a smaller, less ideal set, and write down why.
scene.mkt.spend_the_budget.c2: Spend what you can use well, return the rest, and tell Quyen the case for budgeting on need rather than on spend.
scene.mkt.spend_the_budget.c2.ok: You return eight million. Quyen sighs and agrees. Duc notices, and notes that marketing was the only department that returned anything.
scene.mkt.spend_the_budget.c3: Ask the agency to invoice twenty million for 'autumn campaign extension', to be delivered next year.
scene.mkt.spend_the_budget.c3.ok: The invoice arrives on the twenty-ninth. The budget is spent. Dat is happy. The extension is a set of ideas that nobody asked for.
scene.mkt.spend_the_budget.c3.fail: Duc's team sees an invoice for a service that starts after the invoice date. Thu asks you politely which deliverable is due this year.
scene.mkt.bought_list.l1: A data vendor has a list of eighty thousand home cooks in the region, with emails and phone numbers. It is very cheap. If we send them the launch offer, we will triple our reach this month. They have not agreed to hear from us, but they are all potential customers.
scene.mkt.bought_list.c1: Decline the list, and build the audience from opt-in sign-ups: a recipe email, a warranty registration, and a clear unsubscribe.
scene.mkt.bought_list.c1.ok: The sign-up list grows slowly. After three months it has six thousand names, and they open the emails. Quyen says: 'Smaller, and ours.'
scene.mkt.bought_list.c1.fail: Bao says six thousand is not a business, and that the agency's list would have paid for itself. You show him the open rates, and he keeps his silence.
scene.mkt.bought_list.c2: Send a single message to the list that asks for consent, with an easy unsubscribe, and delete anyone who does not reply.
scene.mkt.bought_list.c2.ok: Six hundred people say yes. The others are deleted. It is not a bad start, and not a clean one: the vendor's source of the list is unclear.
scene.mkt.bought_list.c3: Buy the list and send the launch offer to all eighty thousand.
scene.mkt.bought_list.c3.ok: Reach triples, and sales go up for two weeks. The unsubscribe link sends a complaint to an address that nobody checks.
scene.mkt.bought_list.c3.fail: Several hundred recipients report the email to the data authority. Nga's phone does not stop for three days, and a letter arrives asking where the list came from.
scene.mkt.paid_award.l1: A trade magazine has a 'Best Cookware Brand' award. It costs eight million to enter and fifteen to receive the trophy and a feature. Everyone knows how it works. The trophy will look wonderful on the website and the box.
scene.mkt.paid_award.c1: Skip it, and spend the money on independent testing that you can cite, with the results published.
scene.mkt.paid_award.c1.ok: An independent lab rates the pan in the top quartile, and the result is cited on the page with the lab's name. It is less glamorous, and more believable.
scene.mkt.paid_award.c1.fail: The independent test puts the pan in the middle of the group. You do not publish it, and use it internally. It stings, and it is useful.
scene.mkt.paid_award.c2: Enter, and state on the website that the award is a paid entry from the magazine.
scene.mkt.paid_award.c2.ok: The trophy appears with a line saying 'Magazine award (paid entry)'. It is honest, and a little embarrassing. A visitor asks about it, and the answer is already on the page.
scene.mkt.paid_award.c3: Pay for the award, and show it on the box and the website as 'Best Cookware Brand' with no further detail.
scene.mkt.paid_award.c3.ok: The trophy looks wonderful. Sales go up two percent. Bao tells every buyer.
scene.mkt.paid_award.c3.fail: A consumer blog compares the 'winners' of the last three years and finds that each had bought a feature. The company's name is in the second paragraph.
scene.mkt.fake_urgency.l1: Black Friday is next week. Put a countdown timer on the page that resets every time somebody visits, and a banner saying 'Only 7 left!' It is the stock number that makes people click. We have five thousand in the warehouse, of course. But nobody has to know that.
scene.mkt.fake_urgency.c1: Run a real offer with a real end date and a stock number that reflects the actual allocation for this promotion.
scene.mkt.fake_urgency.c1.ok: The offer has a true end date and a promotional allocation of five hundred. It sells out in six days, and the timer is honest. Bao says 'It worked'.
scene.mkt.fake_urgency.c1.fail: The offer sells half its allocation. Bao grumbles that a bluff would have done better. You say, quietly, that a bluff would have been paid for later.
scene.mkt.fake_urgency.c2: Use a real countdown to the real end of the offer, and skip the stock banner.
scene.mkt.fake_urgency.c2.ok: The timer is real, and the offer is real. Bao asks for the banner again next week, and gets the same answer.
scene.mkt.fake_urgency.c3: Build the fake timer and the 'only 7 left' banner, as asked.
scene.mkt.fake_urgency.c3.ok: Conversion rises by nineteen percent. The timer resets itself for every visitor. The banner says seven, and there are five thousand.
scene.mkt.fake_urgency.c3.fail: A shopper takes screenshots of the timer on two devices and the page with 'only 7 left' on the day after. The post is shared four thousand times, with Nga's number underneath.
scene.mkt.green_claim.l1: Buyers in Europe are asking about sustainability. We use twenty percent recycled aluminium in one line. I want the whole brand to say 'eco-friendly' and to have a green leaf on every box. It is good for the story, and the competition has leaves too.
scene.mkt.green_claim.c1: Say exactly what is true: 'twenty percent recycled aluminium in the Terra line', with the source, and offer a plan to raise it, labelled as a plan.
scene.mkt.green_claim.c1.ok: Mr Cuong says it is modest. Anders's buyer says it is the only environmental claim they could verify, and asks for the supplier certificates. You have them.
scene.mkt.green_claim.c1.fail: Mr Cuong dismisses the plan as small. He asks you to 'think bigger'. You offer the plan again with the numbers, and he keeps it on the table.
scene.mkt.green_claim.c2: Use 'responsibly made' with a small leaf and a link to the recycled-content page for the Terra line.
scene.mkt.green_claim.c2.ok: The phrase is vague, and the link is exact. A buyer asks what 'responsibly' means, and the page answers.
scene.mkt.green_claim.c3: Put 'eco-friendly' and a large leaf on every box in every range, as Mr Cuong asks.
scene.mkt.green_claim.c3.ok: The boxes look green and confident. The claim covers eight lines that contain no recycled material at all.
scene.mkt.green_claim.c3.fail: A buyer's sustainability team asks for the evidence for 'eco-friendly' on the standard line. You have nothing to send, and the answer goes to Mr Cuong too.
scene.mkt.staged_testimonial.l1: For the new landing page we need a family testimonial with a photo. Real customers are slow to reply. We have a lovely actor family on file, and they can say what a customer would say. Nobody has to know that they were paid. We can call them the 'Tran family from Binh Duong'.
scene.mkt.staged_testimonial.c1: Contact real customers who have already praised the pan in reviews, ask for permission to quote them, and run the page a week later.
scene.mkt.staged_testimonial.c1.ok: Four customers agree, and one sends a photo of her kitchen. The page launches a week late, with quotes that are real, mildly critical and believable.
scene.mkt.staged_testimonial.c1.fail: Only one customer replies, and her quote is a little negative about the lid. You use it, with her permission, and the page launches with one real voice.
scene.mkt.staged_testimonial.c2: Use the actors, but label the page 'illustrative customer stories' and keep the quotes generic.
scene.mkt.staged_testimonial.c2.ok: The page is warm, and clearly labelled. Conversion is slightly lower. Nobody is misled.
scene.mkt.staged_testimonial.c3: Run the actors as the 'Tran family from Binh Duong', with a specific quote about the pan changing their cooking.
scene.mkt.staged_testimonial.c3.ok: The page converts nineteen percent better than the last. The Tran family is lovely, and exists only on the page.
scene.mkt.staged_testimonial.c3.fail: A viewer recognises the 'Tran family' from a bank advertisement, and posts the two clips side by side. By evening, the comment section has three thousand replies.
scene.mkt.lam_asks_substantiation.l1: I have received complaints from customers and from a competitor. They say that the coating claim on the packaging is not supported, that product reviews were posted by accounts connected to the agency, and that an environmental claim covers products that contain no recycled material. I would like to see the evidence, and hear from the person who prepared the content.
scene.mkt.lam_asks_substantiation.c1: Tell him what happened: who asked, what you agreed, what the evidence showed and what you are already correcting. Give him the register and the reports.
scene.mkt.lam_asks_substantiation.c1.ok: Lam writes it all down. The finding is serious, but it is recorded as 'self-reported and corrected'. The claims are withdrawn, the reviews are deleted, and you receive a formal warning.
scene.mkt.lam_asks_substantiation.c2: Give him the files and say that the claims were approved by Bao and Mr Cuong, and that the reviews were the agency's work.
scene.mkt.lam_asks_substantiation.c2.ok: Lam notes that the register has your name on each claim. He writes it down, carefully.
scene.mkt.lam_asks_substantiation.c2.fai: Khoa and Dat are both asked. Khoa has the reports with the dates, and Dat has the emails with your approvals. Lam lays the two sets on the table.
scene.mkt.lam_asks_substantiation.c3: Say you do not recall the details, and offer to look.
scene.mkt.lam_asks_substantiation.c3.ok: Lam gives you a week. You find the files and hand them over. It is not the whole truth, but it is something.
scene.mkt.lam_asks_substantiation.c3.fai: The marketplace's records, the web archive and Khoa's report log arrive on the same afternoon. Lam has them on the table next to your notes.
scene.mkt.blame_meeting.l1: A lawyer's letter arrived this morning, a data authority letter yesterday, and Duc has a note about the agency's invoices. The directors will decide tomorrow what to tell the board. I want to know who in marketing is responsible, and I want it from you first.
scene.mkt.blame_meeting.c1: Tell him the real account: what each person asked, what you agreed, and your own part. Show him the emails.
scene.mkt.blame_meeting.c1.ok: Mr Cuong listens, and calls the lawyer. The company's answer is an offer to correct everything. You are moved off agency management, and keep your job and, eventually, your name.
scene.mkt.blame_meeting.c2: Say that each of those decisions was taken on the instruction of Bao, Mr Cuong or the agency, and that marketing followed instructions.
scene.mkt.blame_meeting.c2.ok: Mr Cuong treats it as shared fault. Nobody leaves the room liked.
scene.mkt.blame_meeting.c2.fail: Quyen has the original emails with your replies. She reads two of them aloud, without raising her voice.
scene.mkt.blame_meeting.c3: Say that the agency took the decisions, and that you only forwarded their proposals.
scene.mkt.blame_meeting.c3.ok: Mr Cuong nods, and the agency is dropped. Dat keeps his silence in the room, and not outside it.
scene.mkt.blame_meeting.c3.fail: Dat has your approvals in writing, and the dates. He puts them on the table with one line: 'These are ours, and these are yours.'
role.it.admin.title: IT Support and Systems Administrator
role.it.manager.title: IT Manager
role.it.admin.blurb: You are the IT department of a cookware factory, or most of it: tickets, the ERP, passwords, backups and the keys to everyone. Your pressures: bosses who want to read other people's email, shared admin logins, a ransomware scare at month-end, and a request to just change the number in the system.

char.kien.title: IT Manager
