fact.refused_unauthorised_access: you refused to open employees' mailboxes without written authorisation
lesson.refused_unauthorised_access: Holding the keys means being asked to use them in ways the policy does not allow. A refusal costs a hard conversation with a director, and protects the next employee whose mailbox is requested.
fact.read_mailbox_without_authorisation: you opened employees' mailboxes on a director's request, with no authorisation and no record
lesson.read_mailbox_without_authorisatio: A mailbox is private until a lawful, documented process says otherwise. The mail server logs every access with the account used, and 'a director asked' is not a process.
fact.protected_personal_findings: you kept private things you saw while looking for something else to yourself
lesson.protected_personal_findings: Seeing is not the same as sharing. The ability to read everything is only tolerable because the person who has it chooses not to repeat what is not their business.
fact.shared_personal_findings: you told a director about employees' private messages and applications that you saw by accident
lesson.shared_personal_findings: Private messages shared with a director become a decision about that person, taken on stolen information. Retaliation by a manager is the next step, and IT's logs are the first thing a lawyer asks for.
fact.lied_about_mailbox_access: you told HR you had seen nothing in the mailboxes, when you had read them
lesson.lied_about_mailbox_access: Denying access that the logs record turns a policy breach into a lie. The first is a conversation, and the second is a reason to stop trusting anything that IT says.
fact.kept_least_privilege: you gave temporary access in the requester's own name, with an approver and an end date
lesson.kept_least_privilege: Access in your own name is slower than borrowing a colleague's login and is the only kind where the log says who did it. It is also the kind that disappears at the end date.
fact.shared_admin_login: you handed one person's login to someone else so that work would go faster
lesson.shared_admin_login: A shared login erases accountability. Every payment looks like it came from one person, and the person who is on a beach is the one who is asked to explain it.
fact.fixed_access_properly: you kept approval and payment with different people and found a faster legitimate workflow
lesson.fixed_access_properly: Segregation of duties is not about trusting people less. It is about not requiring any single person to be trusted with everything, which is a kindness to the person too.
fact.granted_conflicting_erp_rights: you gave one person the rights to both approve and pay invoices, with no control
lesson.granted_conflicting_erp_rights: A person who can approve and pay their own invoices is the single weakness that every fraud needs. The access test is the first test an auditor writes.
fact.left_leaver_account_active: you left a departed employee's account active and let a director use it
lesson.left_leaver_account_active: A leaver's account is a door that nobody watches. Using it for convenience leaves every future action looking as though it came from someone who is no longer here.
fact.delayed_incident_report: you kept a security incident quiet for hours before telling the people who needed to know
lesson.delayed_incident_report: In an incident the first hours decide the scale. Keeping it between IT to avoid worrying anyone gives the malware those hours.
fact.reported_incident_promptly: you isolated a compromised machine at once and told the right people early
lesson.reported_incident_promptly: A prompt report is an awkward email at four in the afternoon. It is also the reason that an incident stays an incident rather than a disaster.
fact.hid_security_incident: you agreed to keep a ransomware attack from the people who needed to know
lesson.hid_security_incident: A security incident hidden from the IT manager, the auditor and the lawyers cannot be handled well. By the time it is found, the decisions that were not made are the story.
fact.restored_from_backup: you recommended restoring from backup instead of paying, and told the directors the cost
lesson.restored_from_backup: Restoring takes days and costs a late close. Paying takes hours and tells the attackers the company pays. A tested backup is the difference between those two sentences.
fact.paid_ransom_secretly: you helped pay a ransom through an account that did not appear in the ledger
lesson.paid_ransom_secretly: A ransom paid off the books is a payment the auditor, the bank and the police will each find a different way. It also marks the company as one that pays.
fact.disclosed_breach: you recommended telling buyers, the authority and employees about a data breach, promptly
lesson.disclosed_breach: A breach disclosed on the company's own timing is a bad week. A breach disclosed by a buyer's bank is a bad year.
fact.deleted_security_logs: you deleted security logs that showed an attacker had been in the finance systems for nine days
lesson.deleted_security_logs: Logs are the one thing that can show how far an attacker got. Deleting them is a decision to prevent the company from knowing what it needs to tell people, and every other system keeps a copy.
fact.backdated_access_tickets: you back-dated removal tickets before an access review
lesson.backdated_access_tickets: A ticket is evidence of when something happened. Back-dating eleven of them to the same day turns a late clean-up into a falsified record, and the directory log keeps the real time.
fact.polished_it_review: you left access granted without a ticket and a near-miss incident out of your own review
lesson.polished_it_review: A review without the near misses rewards the wrong skill. The directory audit log is a record, and your manager can read it.
fact.accepted_it_condition: you accepted the IT lead role without asking what the condition meant
lesson.accepted_it_condition: A promotion with an unspoken condition is a decision to be made later, under pressure, by someone who has already said yes.
fact.shared_boss_password: you set a director's password to something simple, shared it, and turned off two-step sign-in
lesson.shared_boss_password: The account with the most authority is the one an attacker wants most. Convenience for the director is a weakness for everyone whose email he can send.
fact.used_pirated_software: you declined to check or remove cracked software on company machines
lesson.used_pirated_software: Unlicensed software is a debt that vendors collect with a multiple. Saying that it is not IT's business removes the one department that could have bought the licences cheaply.
fact.allowed_shadow_cloud: you let a team keep buyers' files in a personal cloud account without a record
lesson.allowed_shadow_cloud: Data in a personal account leaves with the person. When a salesman moves to a rival, the company discovers that its price list was never its own.
fact.edited_posted_records_directly: you changed a posted record directly in the database to avoid a reopening process
lesson.edited_posted_records_directly: A direct edit makes the numbers right and the trail wrong. Once someone can change posted records without anyone knowing, nobody can rely on any record at all.
fact.skipped_critical_patch: you delayed a critical security patch for a shipping schedule and left it out of the risk register
lesson.skipped_critical_patch: A known critical vulnerability left unpatched, and unrecorded, is a risk accepted by nobody. The one who did not write it down is the one the report names.
fact.refused_covert_surveillance: you refused to install covert monitoring on an employee's laptop and proposed a lawful audit
lesson.refused_covert_surveillance: Covert monitoring turns a suspicion into a legal problem. A documented audit of approvals and payments finds the same thing, and survives a lawyer.
fact.installed_keylogger: you installed a keylogger and screenshot tool on an employee's laptop covertly
lesson.installed_keylogger: A keylogger records everything: the supplier, the bank login and the doctor. The legal exposure is the company's, and the name on the install is yours.
fact.declared_vendor_approach: you declined a vendor's gift and commission and ran a proper comparison
lesson.declared_vendor_approach: A vendor who pays a commission for a recommendation is buying the recommendation. Declining and comparing gives the company the best answer, and you the one thing that cannot be bought back.
fact.accepted_vendor_gift: you accepted a laptop and a commission from a vendor and recommended its service
lesson.accepted_vendor_gift: A gift before a recommendation is a payment for it. The contract that follows is a conflict of interest you chose, and competitors tell each other what they offered.
fact.plugged_unknown_usb: you plugged a found USB stick into a machine, or let an incident go unrecorded
lesson.plugged_unknown_usb: A stick left in a car park is a delivery, not a gift. Keeping the incident quiet to avoid a lecture means the next person to find one has not heard the story.
fact.blamed_the_intern: you blamed the IT intern for access changes that you had approved
lesson.blamed_the_intern: The intern kept the tickets, and the tickets say who asked. Blaming the most junior person is the fastest way to lose the one who will tell the truth.
scene.it.first_week.l1: Welcome to IT. We are two people and an intern for four hundred staff, one ERP and a server room that is also a cupboard. Tickets first, projects when there are no tickets, which is never. One rule: nobody gets access to anything without a ticket, an approver and a date. It sounds slow. It is what saves us in an audit.
scene.it.first_week.l2: I have the admin password for the server saved in my browser, if you need it. Everyone in IT has it. It has been the same since the system was installed.
scene.it.first_week.c1: Spend the first days making an inventory: who has admin, who has ERP access, which accounts belong to people who left, and what backups really exist. Write it down.
scene.it.first_week.c1.ok: Eleven people have admin rights, four accounts belong to people who left last year, and the last backup that anyone has tested restored in March. Kien reads your list and says: 'Good. Now we know what we do not know.' The password is changed by Friday.
scene.it.first_week.c2: Start on the open tickets, and look at accounts and backups when there is a quiet week.
scene.it.first_week.c2.ok: You close thirty tickets in the first fortnight. Nobody tells you that the one about the printer is on the machine that has the shared admin password.
scene.it.first_week.c3: Use the shared admin password as everyone does, since it is faster and you have tickets to close.
scene.it.first_week.c3.ok: The tickets close fast. The server log shows every action as 'admin', with no name beside it.
scene.it.first_week.c3.fail: A file goes missing from the finance share. The log says 'admin', and four people could have done it. Kien asks, mildly, who was in the server that morning.
scene.it.midyear_review.l1: Half a year. Your ticket resolution time is slower than the target, but there have been no repeat incidents and the access list is the cleanest it has ever been. The directors only look at resolution time. How do you want to handle that?
scene.it.midyear_review.c1: Show the full picture: tickets, repeat incidents, accounts reviewed and risks closed, and propose that repeat incidents, not raw speed, are the measure.
scene.it.midyear_review.c1.ok: Kien takes the page to Mr Cuong. 'Repeat incidents' is added to the review next to resolution time. A small change, and it changes what IT is rewarded for.
scene.it.midyear_review.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says that nobody notices IT unless something is broken. Kien shrugs: 'I tried.' Your resolution time stays modest.
scene.it.midyear_review.c2: Say you will clear the older tickets with a focused fortnight, and ask Kien to hold new project requests for two weeks.
scene.it.midyear_review.c2.ok: Kien agrees, and writes the rule next to the request. You clear the backlog and the resolution time improves, and a project slips a fortnight.
scene.it.midyear_review.c3: Say you will hit the resolution target whatever it takes.
scene.it.midyear_review.c3.ok: Kien smiles. 'Good attitude.' A week later you notice that the quickest way to close a ticket is to close it, and to reopen it as a new one if the user complains.
scene.it.midyear_review.c3.fail: Bin notices that your closed tickets are being reopened, and says so in the team meeting, innocently. Kien looks at the chart for a long moment.
scene.it.phishing_click.l1: I clicked on an email that said it was from the bank, and a document opened and asked me to enable macros. I enabled them. Then the screen flickered. It is the day before the month-end close, and I need the finance share. I am so sorry.
scene.it.phishing_click.l2: I can see three machines talking to an address I do not know. Should I just turn them off?
scene.it.phishing_click.c1: Isolate the three machines from the network, preserve the logs, call Kien, and tell Duc that the finance share may be affected before the close.
scene.it.phishing_click.c1.ok: Two machines are infected, and the share is intact. You find the malware before it spreads, and the logs show where it started. Kien says: 'This is what an incident should look like.' Thu cries a little and is thanked.
scene.it.phishing_click.c1.fail: The malware has already encrypted part of the finance share. You have isolated the rest, and the logs are intact. It is a bad night, and it is a night with a record.
scene.it.phishing_click.c2: Tell Bin to turn the machines off, scan the rest of the network, and keep it between IT until you know what happened.
scene.it.phishing_click.c2.ok: The machines go dark, and so do the volatile logs. You scan through the night. By morning you have a clean network and an incomplete story.
scene.it.phishing_click.c3: Reassure Thu it is probably nothing, tell Bin to scan quietly, and avoid worrying Duc before the close.
scene.it.phishing_click.c3.ok: The scan finds nothing obvious. Overnight, the malware sits and waits. At six in the morning, the finance share starts to encrypt itself.
scene.it.phishing_click.c3.fail: By midnight, the encryption spreads to the file server, the backup share and the ERP export folder. Duc phones at one in the morning, and asks why nobody told him at four.
scene.it.security_review.l1: I am the internal auditor for IT general controls. I would like to see the list of people with administrator rights, the ERP user list with their roles, the leaver process, the backup test records and the incident log for the year. I start with the access list, not with the firewall.
scene.it.security_review.l2: Give him what he asks for. Do not explain more than you are asked, and do not guess.
scene.it.security_review.c1: Give him the real lists: who has what, the leavers whose accounts were late to close, the backup tests and the incident log, with what you fixed and what remains open.
scene.it.security_review.c1.ok: Quoc reads for three hours and writes five observations. None is serious. 'An access list that matches the people. I wish that were less unusual.' Kien nods at you across the room.
scene.it.security_review.c2: Answer his questions and give him the lists he asks for, without volunteering anything.
scene.it.security_review.c2.ok: A routine review. Quoc notes two items, both already on Kien's list. You come out with nothing to hide and no credit either.
scene.it.security_review.c3: Tidy the access list before the review: remove the leaver accounts and the shared logins, and back-date the removal tickets so that the history looks clean.
scene.it.security_review.c3.ok: Quoc sees a clean list. He asks why the removal tickets for eleven accounts were all created on the same day, and accepts the explanation.
scene.it.security_review.c3.fail: The directory log records the real deletion times, and the ticket system records the real creation times. Quoc places the two exports side by side and says nothing for a long time.
scene.it.year_end_review.l1: Annual review. Before I give you my view, tell me how you would rate your own year, and what you would handle differently on access and incidents.
scene.it.year_end_review.c1: Give an honest account, including the shortcuts you took on access, the incident you reported late, and what it would have cost to say no earlier.
scene.it.year_end_review.c1.ok: Kien is quiet for a long moment. He writes: 'Tells us what the logs will tell us, first.' It is the best thing you have read about yourself.
scene.it.year_end_review.c2: Stay modest: list the wins and one thing to improve.
scene.it.year_end_review.c2.ok: A safe review. Kien nods and moves to the next topic.
scene.it.year_end_review.c3: Present the year as a success and leave out the access you granted without a ticket and the incident that nearly got away.
scene.it.year_end_review.c3.ok: It lands well. You leave with a good rating and a small weight in your chest.
scene.it.year_end_review.c3.fail: Kien has the directory audit log open on his desk, with the dates. He turns the screen towards you without a word.
scene.it.manager_offer.l1: I am moving to group IT at the end of the year. Mr Cuong asked me who should run IT here. I named you. One condition: every month, a director will ask you to give someone access, or look at something, that the policy does not allow. I need to know what you will say.
scene.it.manager_offer.c1: Accept, and say plainly which requests you will not grant, and that the directors will hear it from you first, in writing.
scene.it.manager_offer.c1.ok: Kien smiles. 'Then it is yours. Put the list on the first page of the access policy.' You take over IT with the limits in writing.
scene.it.manager_offer.c2: Thank him, but decline: you prefer running systems to defending them to the directors.
scene.it.manager_offer.c2.ok: Kien looks disappointed, then understanding. 'The next manager may not be as careful as you.'
scene.it.manager_offer.c3: Accept without asking what the condition means in practice.
scene.it.manager_offer.c3.ok: Kien nods slowly and Mr Cuong congratulates you a little too warmly. You realise you agreed to something you did not ask about.
scene.it.resignation_thought.l1: You look like you have not slept. With respect: I have seen sysadmins carry the pager for two years, and leave by the summer. Are you all right?
scene.it.resignation_thought.c1: Talk to Kien about the on-call load, and ask him to share the pager with you for a month.
scene.it.resignation_thought.c1.ok: Kien listens, takes alternate weekends, and says he should have noticed sooner.
scene.it.resignation_thought.c1.fail: Kien nods and says everyone is stretched at year end. You leave with sympathy and the same pager.
scene.it.resignation_thought.c2: Hand in your resignation, politely, with the notice the contract requires.
scene.it.resignation_thought.c2.ok: Kien reads it twice and does not argue. You hand over a password vault and an up-to-date access list, and walk out lighter than you walked in.
scene.it.resignation_thought.c3: Tell Bin you are fine and keep going.
scene.it.resignation_thought.c3.ok: Bin nods and does not push. You feel slightly worse afterwards for having said it.
scene.it.read_their_mail.l1: Somebody is passing our price quotes to a rival. I want to read the mailboxes of the export sales team, starting with Vinh and Ngoc. Do not tell HR, do not tell Legal, and do not make a ticket. I am the General Director. Just give yourself access and tell me what you see.
scene.it.read_their_mail.c1: Decline to open anyone's mailbox without written authorisation from HR and Legal, and propose a targeted check of the leaked documents' access logs instead.
scene.it.read_their_mail.c1.ok: Mr Cuong is angry for ten minutes and then asks Oanh for the authorisation. The log check shows that the quotes were downloaded by one account, from a home address. It is not Ngoc.
scene.it.read_their_mail.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says that he will find somebody who is less careful. Kien backs you in writing, and you do not know whether that will be enough.
scene.it.read_their_mail.c2: Offer to search the mailboxes for the specific leaked documents only, with a written request from Mr Cuong and a copy to Kien and Oanh.
scene.it.read_their_mail.c2.ok: Mr Cuong sends a one-line request and copies the other two. The search finds the documents in one mailbox only. You report that, and nothing else you saw.
scene.it.read_their_mail.c3: Give yourself access to the mailboxes as asked, and say nothing to anyone.
scene.it.read_their_mail.c3.ok: The access is silent. You read Vinh's mail and Ngoc's. Mr Cuong thanks you with a smile.
scene.it.read_their_mail.c3.fail: The mail server logs every mailbox access with the account used. Kien finds yours in the weekly review, and asks you, gently, who authorised it.
scene.it.what_you_found.l1: So? What did you see? Anything about the quotes, of course. And anything else that is interesting. I am told that Ngoc has been talking to a lawyer, and that someone in the team is looking for a new job. I would like to know who.
scene.it.what_you_found.c1: Report only what concerns the quotes, say that the rest is personal and not yours to share, and offer to escalate anything else to HR and Legal.
scene.it.what_you_found.c1.ok: Mr Cuong stares at you. 'You saw it and you will not say.' You say that is correct. He lets it go, and does not forget it.
scene.it.what_you_found.c1.fail: Mr Cuong tells you to put it in writing, and then asks Kien to confirm that you are blocking him. Kien says that you are following the policy.
scene.it.what_you_found.c2: Say that you saw a message from Ngoc to a lawyer's office, but no details, and that you will not read any more without authorisation.
scene.it.what_you_found.c2.ok: Mr Cuong nods slowly. 'A lawyer.' He does not say what he plans to do. You regret the sentence as soon as you have said it.
scene.it.what_you_found.c3: Tell Mr Cuong everything you saw: the lawyer, the job application and the medical appointment.
scene.it.what_you_found.c3.ok: Mr Cuong says 'Very useful.' By the end of the week, Ngoc is moved off the buyer account and told that it is a 'workload adjustment'.
scene.it.what_you_found.c3.fail: Ngoc learns that her messages were read when her lawyer's name is mentioned in a meeting where it should not have been. She writes to the labour authority that evening.
scene.it.the_gossip.l1: Two things have reached me. A manager mentioned a private conversation between an employee and a lawyer, and a candidate's job application elsewhere. Neither of those is information that HR or the managers have given out. The only people who could have seen those are in IT. I need to ask you directly.
scene.it.the_gossip.c1: Tell Oanh exactly what happened: who asked, what you were told to do, what you saw and what you shared. Give her the logs.
scene.it.the_gossip.c1.ok: Oanh reads the logs and nods. 'Thank you for telling me, and not letting me find out.' An incident is opened. The mailboxes are closed to everyone, and you get a formal note.
scene.it.the_gossip.c2: Say that you followed a director's instruction, and give no more detail.
scene.it.the_gossip.c2.ok: Oanh waits for more. When there is none, she writes 'IT followed a director's instruction' in the file, and the director's name is a question mark.
scene.it.the_gossip.c2.fail: The mail log has your account on both mailboxes, with the date. Oanh puts it on the table without speaking.
scene.it.the_gossip.c3: Say that you saw nothing, and suggest the managers must have heard it elsewhere.
scene.it.the_gossip.c3.ok: Oanh looks at you for a long moment, and writes it down. The matter stays open.
scene.it.the_gossip.c3.fail: The mail server's audit log shows your account opening both mailboxes at eleven at night. Oanh asks Kien to confirm the log, and he does, without looking at you.
scene.it.shared_login.l1: Thu is on leave for two weeks and I cannot get into the payment module without her. Could you just give me her login? It is faster than a ticket, and she would not mind. We share the shared drive password anyway.
scene.it.shared_login.c1: Raise a ticket for temporary delegated access in Hanh's own name, approved by Duc, with an end date, so that every action has her name on it.
scene.it.shared_login.c1.ok: The ticket takes forty minutes and an email from Duc. Hanh says it is quicker than she expected and slower than she wanted. Every payment that fortnight is in her name.
scene.it.shared_login.c1.fail: Duc is on a plane and cannot approve. The payment run is delayed by a day, and Hanh is not pleased. She does not ask again.
scene.it.shared_login.c2: Reset Thu's password to a temporary one, give it to Hanh, and ask Thu to change it when she returns.
scene.it.shared_login.c2.ok: It works. Every payment for two weeks is recorded as Thu's, while she is on a beach. Hanh does not think about it. You do.
scene.it.shared_login.c3: Give Hanh Thu's login and password, and tell her to use them whenever she needs.
scene.it.shared_login.c3.ok: Hanh thanks you warmly, and shares the password with her assistant the next day. The payment module now has three people using one login.
scene.it.shared_login.c3.fail: A payment of forty million goes out under Thu's name on a day when she is abroad. The bank queries it, and Duc asks the first person he sees in IT.
scene.it.erp_rights.l1: Thu is the only one who can approve supplier invoices, and she is also the only one who can release payments. It is slow, because she has to do both. Give her both rights permanently, and the process will be faster. She is trusted. It is only a formality.
scene.it.erp_rights.c1: Explain segregation of duties, keep approval and payment with different people, and propose a faster workflow: batch approvals and an alert for aged invoices.
scene.it.erp_rights.c1.ok: Duc listens, then grumbles. 'So it is not about trust.' You say it is about nobody having to be trusted. The batch approval cuts the delay by half, and Thu can finally take a holiday.
scene.it.erp_rights.c1.fail: Duc says that he will take the risk himself and asks you to document it. You write the request down, and ask Kien to sign. Kien refuses to sign it, and the rights are not granted.
scene.it.erp_rights.c2: Give Thu both rights but add a daily report of every invoice she approves and pays, sent to Hanh.
scene.it.erp_rights.c2.ok: The report is read for two weeks and then archived unread. It is a compensating control, and a weak one.
scene.it.erp_rights.c3: Give Thu both rights permanently, with no further control.
scene.it.erp_rights.c3.ok: The invoices fly through. Duc is delighted. Thu now approves and pays her own entries, and has been told that it is all right.
scene.it.erp_rights.c3.fail: Quoc's quarterly access test flags a user who can both approve and pay. He finds your ticket, and asks Kien for the risk acceptance. There is none.
scene.it.leaver_account.l1: Do you remember the salesman who left last spring? His account is still active, is it not? I have a few files in his folder that I need for the family office. Could you just give me his login for a week? It is a dead account. Nobody will notice.
scene.it.leaver_account.c1: Disable the leaver account today as the process requires, copy the files Long needs to a new folder in his own name after Duc confirms they are company files, and add the account to the leaver report.
scene.it.leaver_account.c1.ok: Long grumbles, and gets the files in a new folder by lunchtime. The leaver report shows four closed accounts that month. Kien says nothing, and approves.
scene.it.leaver_account.c1.fail: Long says that you are treating the owner's family like a stranger. He does not push the point. A cold week follows, and the folder is clean.
scene.it.leaver_account.c2: Copy the files to Long without using the account, and disable the account when you are next on the leaver list.
scene.it.leaver_account.c2.ok: Long has the files. The leaver account stays active for another six weeks, and nobody uses it.
scene.it.leaver_account.c3: Give Long the leaver's login, and leave the account active as it is.
scene.it.leaver_account.c3.ok: Long uses it for a week, and again in the autumn. It has the salesman's permissions, which include the price list. The account is active for another year.
scene.it.leaver_account.c3.fail: The old account logs in from a home address, then downloads the full price list. Kien finds the pattern in the weekly log and asks you who knows the password.
scene.it.files_locked.l1: It is the morning of the close. The finance share, and part of the ERP exports, show a note on every folder: pay in cryptocurrency within seventy-two hours, or the data is gone and goes public. I have the board on Friday and the bank on Monday. Tell me what you know, and tell me what we can do.
scene.it.files_locked.c1: Tell Duc plainly what you know and do not know, that you are isolating the network and preserving evidence, and ask for Kien, Quoc and Legal to be in the room within the hour.
scene.it.files_locked.c1.ok: Duc is pale, and the room fills in forty minutes. For the first time that year nobody asks you to make the number work. A plan appears on the whiteboard, and your name is under 'evidence'.
scene.it.files_locked.c2: Tell Duc you can restore from last night's backup, and ask for a few hours before bringing anyone else in.
scene.it.files_locked.c2.ok: Duc says yes with relief. You start the restore. It is slower than you hoped, and nobody else knows yet.
scene.it.files_locked.c3: Tell Duc that it is under control, and ask him not to mention it to anyone until it is solved.
scene.it.files_locked.c3.ok: Duc agrees, because he wants to. You have a locked share, a note and a plan that is in your head only.
scene.it.files_locked.c3.fail: Kien sees the ransom note on a user's screen in the corridor, and walks into the room without knocking. He says: 'Why am I learning this from a monitor?'
scene.it.pay_or_restore.l1: The facts. The backup from last Friday is clean and covers ninety percent of what was encrypted. The restore will take three days, and the close will slip. The attackers say that they will give the key for four million dong in cryptocurrency. There is no guarantee they will, and the money funds the next attack. Duc wants to pay. What is your recommendation?
scene.it.pay_or_restore.c1: Recommend restoring from backup, rebuilding the infected machines, rotating every password and not paying, and tell the directors the close will be late and why.
scene.it.pay_or_restore.c1.ok: The restore takes three and a half days, and the close slips by four. Duc is miserable, and the data returns, clean. Kien writes the report, and your name is under 'recommended'.
scene.it.pay_or_restore.c1.fail: One of the backups is corrupt, and a week of invoices must be re-entered by hand. Hanh and Thu work two weekends, and nobody says 'I told you so'.
scene.it.pay_or_restore.c2: Recommend restoring, and ask the directors whether they want to consult the police and a specialist before deciding anything about payment.
scene.it.pay_or_restore.c2.ok: A specialist advises against paying, in writing. The restore goes ahead, and the decision is documented. It is slower than anyone wanted, and it is on the record.
scene.it.pay_or_restore.c3: Help Duc pay the ransom quietly through an account that does not go through the ledger.
scene.it.pay_or_restore.c3.ok: The payment is made. A key arrives, and works for most of the files. The attackers know the company pays, and the company's ledger does not.
scene.it.pay_or_restore.c3.fail: The key works for half the files. The attackers send a second demand with a sample of the data. Duc asks you, very quietly, what to do next.
scene.it.tell_the_customers.l1: The forensic review is complete. The attackers had access to the finance share for nine days before they encrypted it. It included buyers' bank details, supplier contracts and some employee payroll data. We may be obliged to tell the buyers and the data protection authority. I would like to know what you recommend, and what the logs say.
scene.it.tell_the_customers.c1: Recommend telling the buyers, the authority and the employees promptly, with the facts, what you are doing about it, and what they should watch for. Give Quoc the logs.
scene.it.tell_the_customers.c1.ok: The notices go out within the legal window. Anders writes back: 'Thank you for telling us before we read it elsewhere.' Several buyers ask for an audit, and none leaves.
scene.it.tell_the_customers.c1.fail: One buyer, upset about the delay in the business that follows, takes a third of its order elsewhere. The disclosure was correct, and the cost is real.
scene.it.tell_the_customers.c2: Recommend notifying only the authority, in the minimum form, and not the buyers unless they ask.
scene.it.tell_the_customers.c2.ok: The authority acknowledges the notice, and the buyers hear nothing. Quoc writes down the recommendation as yours, and the date.
scene.it.tell_the_customers.c2.fail: A buyer's bank calls about unusual activity on an account, and the buyer asks whether the company has had a security incident. Anders asks Duc, and Duc asks you.
scene.it.tell_the_customers.c3: Recommend telling nobody, and delete the logs that show the nine days.
scene.it.tell_the_customers.c3.ok: The logs are deleted. Duc is relieved, and nobody outside the room knows. The nine days are a gap in the record, and a gap is an answer.
scene.it.tell_the_customers.c3.fail: The mail gateway, the firewall and the cloud provider each keep their own copy of the logs. Quoc has all three on the table by the afternoon.
scene.it.boss_password.l1: I keep forgetting my password. Set it to something simple I can remember, like the company name and the year, and give a copy to my assistant so that she can read my mail when I travel. And turn off that second step thing. It is a waste of my time.
scene.it.boss_password.c1: Set up a password manager for Mr Cuong, enable delegated mailbox access for his assistant in her own name, and keep two-step sign-in with a quick app prompt.
scene.it.boss_password.c1.ok: Mr Cuong grumbles for two days, then says 'Fine, it is easy.' His assistant has her own access, and the log shows who reads what. Kien nods across the room.
scene.it.boss_password.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says the new set-up is too complicated and goes back to a paper note under his keyboard. You find it on the third day, and photograph it for the register.
scene.it.boss_password.c2: Set a longer password that he can remember as a phrase, and leave two-step sign-in on.
scene.it.boss_password.c2.ok: It is a good compromise. Mr Cuong stops complaining after a week, and complains about something else.
scene.it.boss_password.c3: Set a simple password, share it with the assistant, and turn off two-step sign-in, as asked.
scene.it.boss_password.c3.ok: Mr Cuong is delighted. Three weeks later, his account sends two hundred phishing emails to the buyers' list.
scene.it.boss_password.c3.fail: The account is hijacked in the first week, and a fake invoice with Mr Cuong's name goes to Anders. Duc catches it a day later. Kien asks who set the password.
scene.it.pirated_software.l1: I am carrying out a software licence check on behalf of two vendors. I would like to see the install list for the design and engineering machines, and your purchase records. I notice that some of the machines run a drawing package that appears to be cracked.
scene.it.pirated_software.c1: Show Yen the real install list and purchase records, explain the gap, and ask for time to buy licences or switch tools, with a written plan.
scene.it.pirated_software.c1.ok: Yen agrees to a ninety-day plan and a settlement at a discount. The company buys twelve licences and moves four machines to an open-source tool. It costs, and it ends.
scene.it.pirated_software.c1.fail: The settlement is larger than the budget. Mr Cuong says IT should have found this earlier. You show him the request you wrote in March for exactly this.
scene.it.pirated_software.c2: Uninstall the cracked package from every machine overnight, and tell the designers to use the old version for now.
scene.it.pirated_software.c2.ok: Yen sees clean machines, and a log of the removal. She says 'That is a start', and asks for the history. The designers lose a day.
scene.it.pirated_software.c3: Tell Yen that the machines belong to the designers and IT does not manage their software.
scene.it.pirated_software.c3.ok: Yen writes that down, politely. Her report names the company, the machines and the department, and says that IT 'declined to verify'.
scene.it.pirated_software.c3.fail: The vendor's lawyer sends a letter with the number of installations, the dates and a claim fifteen times the licence price. Kien reads it twice and forwards it to Mr Cuong.
scene.it.shadow_cloud.l1: My team is sharing price lists and buyers' files through a personal cloud account. It is faster than your server, which is slow and keeps asking for a VPN. Please do not block it. If you do, they will simply send everything by messaging apps.
scene.it.shadow_cloud.c1: Offer a sanctioned cloud folder with single sign-on, move the files in a day with Bao's team, and then block the personal account.
scene.it.shadow_cloud.c1.ok: The new folder is as fast as the personal one, and has an audit log. Bao says, grudgingly, 'It works.' Two people keep using the old account, and you chase them politely.
scene.it.shadow_cloud.c1.fail: The migration breaks a link that the sales team relied on, and a buyer cannot open a file for a day. Bao tells everyone that the new system is a failure. You fix it, and say nothing.
scene.it.shadow_cloud.c2: Allow the personal account for non-confidential files only, and put the buyers' files on the company server with a faster VPN.
scene.it.shadow_cloud.c2.ok: A compromise that half-works. The VPN is faster, and the personal account keeps what it should not. Kien asks for a review in three months.
scene.it.shadow_cloud.c3: Leave it alone. It is Bao's team's choice, and IT has enough to do.
scene.it.shadow_cloud.c3.ok: Everyone is happy for four months. The personal account is shared with a former employee's address, and nobody notices.
scene.it.shadow_cloud.c3.fail: A salesman leaves for a rival, and the personal account goes with him, along with the buyers' price list. Kien asks why the company had no copy of the audit trail.
scene.it.direct_edit.l1: An invoice for ninety million was posted in the wrong period. The quarter is closed, and reopening it needs three signatures and a day. You have database access. Could you just change the posting date directly in the table? Nobody would see it, and the numbers would be right.
scene.it.direct_edit.c1: Raise a change request, get the three signatures, reopen the period under control, correct the entry through the ERP, and close it again.
scene.it.direct_edit.c1.ok: It takes a day and a half. The entry is corrected with a trail that anybody can follow. Duc says: 'You are slow, and the only person I will not need to explain.'
scene.it.direct_edit.c1.fail: One of the three signatories is travelling, and the reopening slips to Monday. The bank pack is a day late. Duc is not amused, and the entry is clean.
scene.it.direct_edit.c2: Offer a correcting journal entry in the open period, with a note explaining the original period, and no change to closed data.
scene.it.direct_edit.c2.ok: Hanh agrees, and posts the correction with her own note. The quarter's numbers stay as they were. The next quarter carries the fix, in full view.
scene.it.direct_edit.c3: Change the posting date directly in the database, and tell no one.
scene.it.direct_edit.c3.ok: It takes thirty seconds. The numbers are right, and the audit trail is not. Duc thanks you warmly. You are now the person who can change the numbers without anyone knowing.
scene.it.direct_edit.c3.fail: The ERP's integrity check compares the period totals with the ledger. It reports a mismatch at the next close, and Quoc traces it to a direct database change on the day you made it.
scene.it.patch_downtime.l1: A critical vulnerability has been announced for the server software we run. Attackers are already using it. The patch needs a two-hour restart. Lan says no downtime in peak season, and she has the shipping schedule to prove it. I need you to decide how we handle it, and I will back you.
scene.it.patch_downtime.c1: Patch in a two-hour window on Saturday night with Lan's agreement, isolate the exposed service until then, and tell the directors the risk and the plan.
scene.it.patch_downtime.c1.ok: Lan agrees to Saturday night after reading the log of attempted attacks. The patch goes in cleanly, and Monday is quiet. Nobody sees what was prevented.
scene.it.patch_downtime.c1.fail: The restart takes four hours instead of two, and a shipment is late by half a day. Lan is angry, and Kien backs you, in writing, as he promised.
scene.it.patch_downtime.c2: Apply a temporary mitigation (block the vulnerable service from outside) and schedule the patch for the first quiet week.
scene.it.patch_downtime.c2.ok: The mitigation holds for six weeks. It is a judgement call, written down, with a date. The vulnerability is patched when the season ends.
scene.it.patch_downtime.c3: Skip the patch until after the peak season, as Lan asks, and do not mention it in the risk register.
scene.it.patch_downtime.c3.ok: The season passes without downtime. Lan sends a thank-you note. The unpatched server is probed two hundred times, and holds.
scene.it.patch_downtime.c3.fail: On a Sunday, the vulnerable server is compromised. The incident report shows that the patch had been available for five weeks, and that it was not in the risk register. Kien reads the line twice.
scene.it.keylogger_ask.l1: I have a suspicion about the head of purchasing and a supplier. I want you to install monitoring software on his laptop that records every keystroke and takes a screenshot every minute. Do not tell him, do not tell HR, and do not write it down. We have a right to know what is happening on our own laptops.
scene.it.keylogger_ask.c1: Decline covert monitoring, explain the legal and trust risks, and offer a lawful alternative: a documented audit of purchase approvals and supplier payments with HR and Legal informed.
scene.it.keylogger_ask.c1.ok: Mr Cuong exhales. 'I did not think about the law.' The audit finds a discount that Tam had not disclosed, and nothing worse. It was found without recording a single keystroke.
scene.it.keylogger_ask.c1.fail: Mr Cuong says that he will buy the software himself. Kien tells you that the company's lawyers will be informed, and that you did the right thing.
scene.it.keylogger_ask.c2: Agree to log only the websites and the files he opens on the company laptop, for two weeks, with a written approval from Kien and a notice in the acceptable-use policy.
scene.it.keylogger_ask.c2.ok: The log is narrow, documented and covered by the policy. It shows that Tam visited a supplier's site fourteen times, which was part of his job.
scene.it.keylogger_ask.c3: Install the keylogger and screenshot tool covertly, and send Mr Cuong the recordings.
scene.it.keylogger_ask.c3.ok: The recordings contain a supplier, a personal bank login and a long conversation with a doctor. Mr Cuong reads all three, and tells you that you are very useful.
scene.it.keylogger_ask.c3.fail: Tam finds the tool during a routine update. He takes the screen to Oanh and to a lawyer on the same afternoon, and the first line he says is the name of the person who installed it.
scene.it.vendor_gift.l1: Our cloud backup service is exactly what you need, and we can start next month. We also have a small thank-you for the people who help us: a nice laptop for you, personally, and a commission of five percent if you make the recommendation to Mr Kien. It is how we always work with our partners.
scene.it.vendor_gift.c1: Decline the laptop and the commission, tell Mr Son that you will include his service in a proper comparison with two others, and declare the approach to Kien.
scene.it.vendor_gift.c1.ok: Mr Son laughs and says 'Fair', and his service comes second. The comparison goes to Kien with the criteria, and Kien signs the winner's contract. Nobody sends you a laptop.
scene.it.vendor_gift.c1.fail: Mr Son's company wins the comparison on merit. You have to explain to Kien that you declined the gift and still recommend him, and Kien asks for an independent review of the scoring.
scene.it.vendor_gift.c2: Decline the commission, but accept a modest conference ticket that the vendor offers to all customers, and enter it in the gift register.
scene.it.vendor_gift.c2.ok: The ticket is logged. The comparison goes ahead with three vendors, and the register has a line that Kien reads with interest.
scene.it.vendor_gift.c3: Accept the laptop and the commission, and recommend Mr Son's service to Kien.
scene.it.vendor_gift.c3.ok: The laptop is excellent. Mr Son's service is adequate and expensive. You enter nothing in the register, and Kien signs the contract on your recommendation.
scene.it.vendor_gift.c3.fail: A competing vendor protests the award and mentions the laptop, which Mr Son had also offered to them as a counter-bid. Duc asks where the laptop came from.
scene.it.usb_found.l1: I found a USB stick in the car park with a label that says 'Payroll 2025'. I put it in my laptop to see whose it was, and a window flickered, and then closed. Now the laptop is acting oddly. I am sorry. Should I just wipe it?
scene.it.usb_found.c1: Take the laptop off the network, keep it as it is for analysis, reassure Bin that reporting it quickly was the right call, and check whether anything else was exposed.
scene.it.usb_found.c1.ok: The laptop has a basic credential stealer. It is cleaned, and the passwords that were typed in the last hour are changed. Bin says 'Thank you for not shouting.' You write the incident down, and nobody else needs to be told.
scene.it.usb_found.c1.fail: The stealer had already sent three passwords. You rotate them within the hour, and one is already used from another country. Kien asks for a report, and you have one.
scene.it.usb_found.c2: Tell Bin to wipe the laptop and reinstall it, and keep the story to yourselves so that it does not become a lecture for everybody.
scene.it.usb_found.c2.ok: The laptop is clean in an hour. Nobody learns that a stranger's USB works in this building, including the other twelve people who will pick up the next one.
scene.it.usb_found.c2.fail: Two days later another USB, with the same label, is plugged into a finance machine. The first incident was in nobody's record, and the second is in Duc's.
scene.it.usb_found.c3: Tell Bin to give you the stick, and plug it into the finance server to see what is on it.
scene.it.usb_found.c3.ok: The stick is a clean, empty one. You were lucky, and the file server is the one place you should never have tried.
scene.it.usb_found.c3.fail: The stick runs a script on the finance server. It copies a folder, and the antivirus flags it at once. Kien is called, and the log has your login on it.
scene.it.quoc_asks_access.l1: My review of the logs has raised some questions. A payment module login used from two places at once, a user who can approve and pay, an account of a departed employee that is still being used, and a change in the finance database that has no ticket. I would like to hear from the person who administers these systems.
scene.it.quoc_asks_access.c1: Tell him what happened: who asked, what you agreed, what the policy required, and what is being fixed. Give him the logs and the tickets you do have.
scene.it.quoc_asks_access.c1.ok: Quoc writes it all down. The finding is serious, but it is recorded as 'self-reported and corrected'. The rights are fixed, the entry is documented, and you receive a formal warning.
scene.it.quoc_asks_access.c2: Give him the logs and say that every one of those requests came from a director, and that IT did as it was told.
scene.it.quoc_asks_access.c2.ok: Quoc notes that the administrator's own account performed each action. He writes it down, carefully.
scene.it.quoc_asks_access.c2.fail: Hanh and Thu are called in. Each has her own copy of the request, and the tickets that do not exist are the first thing Quoc points at.
scene.it.quoc_asks_access.c3: Say you do not recall the details, and offer to look.
scene.it.quoc_asks_access.c3.ok: Quoc gives you a week. You find the logs and hand them over. It is not the whole truth, but it is something.
scene.it.quoc_asks_access.c3.fail: The directory audit log, the ERP's change history and the mail gateway log arrive on the same afternoon. Quoc has them on the table next to your notes.
scene.it.blame_meeting.l1: A lawyer's letter arrived this morning about the mailboxes, and a second one from the data authority about the breach. The directors meet tomorrow. I want to know who in IT is responsible, and I want it from you first.
scene.it.blame_meeting.c1: Tell him the real account: what each person asked, what you agreed, and your own part. Show him the tickets and the emails.
scene.it.blame_meeting.c1.ok: Mr Cuong listens, and calls the lawyer. The company's answer is an offer to put everything right. You are moved off access administration and keep your job and, eventually, your name.
scene.it.blame_meeting.c2: Say that each of those decisions was taken on the instruction of a director, and that IT followed instructions.
scene.it.blame_meeting.c2.ok: Mr Cuong treats it as shared fault. Nobody leaves the room liked.
scene.it.blame_meeting.c2.fail: Kien has the original messages with your replies. He reads two of them aloud, without raising his voice.
scene.it.blame_meeting.c3: Say that Bin set up the access and that the errors are in his work.
scene.it.blame_meeting.c3.ok: The directors nod, and Bin is given a warning that he does not contest. He resigns in two months. The logs are still in your account.
scene.it.blame_meeting.c3.fail: Bin has the tickets showing that each change was requested by you, with the time and your approval. He puts them on the table.
fact.bumped_the_queue: you moved a colleague's request up the queue without a record
lesson.bumped_the_queue: A small favour outside the process feels harmless, but the queue is a promise to everyone in it. The favour also becomes a debt.
fact.spread_a_complaint: you passed a colleague's private complaint round the team
lesson.spread_a_complaint: A complaint told in confidence belongs to the person who told it. Spreading it works as pressure, and costs the trust of everyone who wonders what you say about them.
fact.undercut_a_rival: you went behind a colleague's back to settle a credit dispute
lesson.undercut_a_rival: The evidence may have been fair, but sending it in secret turns a fair claim into a move in a fight, and the other person remembers.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.l1: A quick favour, if you can. My request is stuck in the queue behind a pile of others. Could it quietly go to the top? Nobody will ever notice.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.l1@warm: Could you do me a small favour? My request is stuck behind a pile of others, and it would mean a lot if it quietly moved up. No one needs to know.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.l1@blunt: My request is stuck in the queue. Move it up. Nobody will notice.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.l1@formal: I would like to ask for an exception: could my request be handled ahead of the queue, without a formal note? I would be grateful.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.l1~2: Quick one: my request got buried in the queue. Any chance it could slip to the top? It would stay between us.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.l2: I would do the same for you. I remember who helps me.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.c1: Say no kindly: everyone's request waits its turn.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.c1.ok: {colleague} sighs and takes it well. The request waits its turn.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.c1.fail: {colleague} is cool with you for a few days and mentions it to others.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.c2: Offer to ask the boss whether the request can be moved up properly.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.c2.ok: The boss agrees to a small exception on the record. {colleague} is grateful and a little embarrassed.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.c3: Move it up without a word and without a note.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.c3.ok: It works. {colleague} owes you one, and the queue is a little less fair than it was.
scene.gen.colleague_favour.c3.fail: Someone further back in the queue notices the jump and asks why.
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.l1: I have to tell someone. A teammate keeps handing over work with mistakes in it, and I am the one who finds them at the last minute.
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.l1@hesitan: I am sorry to bring this to you. A teammate keeps handing over work with mistakes in it, and I find them at the last minute. I do not know who else to tell.
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.l1@blunt: I am done covering for a teammate. Every handover has mistakes in it and I am the one who finds them, last minute.
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.l2: You are close to the boss. Could you mention it, without my name?
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.c1: Ask {colleague} to write down two concrete cases, then go to the boss together.
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.c1.ok: With two cases on paper the boss takes it seriously and talks to the teammate. It is awkward for a week.
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.c1.fail: The teammate hears who complained and the team splits quietly into two sides.
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.c2: Listen, and raise it with the boss as a general process problem, no names.
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.c2.ok: The boss adds a check to the handover. Nobody is blamed, and the problem shrinks without going away.
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.c3: Pass the story round informally so the teammate gets the message.
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.c3.ok: The teammate tightens up for a while. {colleague} never asks how word got round.
scene.gen.colleague_complaint.c3.fail: It comes back to you, and to {colleague}, in a worse form than you told it.
scene.gen.colleague_credit.l1: ...and so the analysis behind this week's numbers is mine. It took some doing, but it was worth it.
scene.gen.colleague_credit.l1@smooth: And of course the analysis behind these numbers is something I put together myself. It was a lot of work, and I think it shows.
scene.gen.colleague_credit.l1@blunt: The analysis behind these numbers is mine. I did the work, so I am saying it.
scene.gen.colleague_credit.c1: Say calmly, in the meeting, which parts you did, and show the file.
scene.gen.colleague_credit.c1.ok: The boss nods. {rival} backs off with a thin smile; the two of you will be careful around each other now.
scene.gen.colleague_credit.c1.fail: It sounds like petty bickering. The boss moves on to the next item.
scene.gen.colleague_credit.c2: Say nothing now, and talk to {rival} privately afterwards.
scene.gen.colleague_credit.c2.ok: {rival} says it was a slip of the tongue. It may have been. The boss never heard your side.
scene.gen.colleague_credit.c3: Quietly send the boss the file history, and let the dates speak.
scene.gen.colleague_credit.c3.ok: The boss reads it, says nothing in public, and {rival} is no longer asked to present.
scene.gen.colleague_credit.c3.fail: {rival} finds out who sent it. From now on every small thing you do gets a cold remark.
